papers.title: Know What You Don't Know: Agentic Data Synthesis by Evolving Generation Space for Closed-Loop Learning
papers.summary: The continued improvement of large language models increasingly depends on synthetic experience, yet effective data synthesis for interactive agents requires not only executable and verifiable trajectories, but also interactions that provide learning value for the current task agent. Existing methods increasingly incorporate environment feedback, data validation, or learner failures, but still face a feedback-to-decision gap: observed weaknesses do not directly specify how future synthesis should change, or whether they can be represented by the current synthesis space. To address this gap, we propose EvoSyn, a learning-feedback-driven multi-agent framework that organizes synthesis around a revisable state specifying what interaction factors can be deliberately generated and where synthesis effort should be allocated. A role-specialized multi-agent system translates learner feedback into synthesis revisions, while a Designer allocates synthesis directions and a Planner grounds them into executable experience. This process enables within-space adaptation toward weak or under-covered regions and synthesis-space expansion that promotes newly discovered factors into explicit generation controls. Experiments on $τ^2$-Bench and CAR-Bench show that EvoSyn improves average task success by 13.3 points over the strongest synthesis baseline, while producing higher-quality and structurally broader synthetic experience and discovering controllable factors missed without learner feedback.
papers.title_zh: 知道自己不知道什么：通过演化生成空间进行闭环学习的智能体数据合成
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型的持续改进越来越依赖于合成经验，然而，针对交互式智能体的有效数据合成不仅需要可执行且可验证的轨迹，还需要能够为当前任务智能体提供学习价值的交互。现有方法越来越多地纳入环境反馈、数据验证或学习者的失败，但仍然面临从反馈到决策的鸿沟：观察到的弱点并不能直接指明未来的合成应如何改变，也不能直接说明它们是否能被当前合成空间所表示。为弥合这一鸿沟，我们提出 EvoSyn，一个由学习反馈驱动的多智能体框架，它围绕一个可修订状态来组织合成，该状态规定了可以有意生成哪些交互因素，以及应将合成努力分配到何处。一个角色专门化的多智能体系统将学习者反馈转化为合成修订，而一个 Designer 分配合成方向，一个 Planner 将其落实为可执行经验。这一过程使得能够在空间内适应薄弱或覆盖不足的区域，并进行合成空间扩展，将新发现的因素提升为显式的生成控制。在 $τ^2$-Bench 和 CAR-Bench 上的实验表明，EvoSyn 相比最强的合成基线将平均任务成功率提高了 13.3 个百分点，同时生成了更高质量且结构上更广泛的合成经验，并发现了在没有学习者反馈时会被遗漏的可控因素。

papers.title: SpireBench: Evaluating Long-Horizon Strategic Play of Agentic Models with Slay the Spire
papers.summary: Agentic large language models now tackle complex tasks, yet strategic reasoning over long horizons is under-studied: most agentic benchmarks are short and episodic, and performance on long tasks is hard to dissect into stored knowledge, reasoning and luck. We introduce SpireBench, in which models play the complete commercial deck-builder Slay the Spire (StS), where early decisions decide long-term success. Across 20 large language models (LLMs) at the game's highest difficulty, frontier models beat heuristic baselines and match the average human player but remain far behind experts. This gap widens as the run lengthens: the strongest models win the first act as often as experts, then fall behind. What separates strong models from weak is how well they play each fight; all of them misjudge risk over a run, preserving health rather than spending it to grow stronger. A comprehensive, self-consistent renaming of every game term shows that part of their performance rests on prior knowledge of the game, and models do not improve from the memories they write across runs, which are often wrong and overly cautious. Our harness is the first to give a model the complete original game, and we compare it with existing harnesses. Overall, SpireBench offers an unsaturated long-horizon benchmark with tools to locate where and why agents fail.
papers.title_zh: SpireBench：以《杀戮尖塔》评估智能体模型的长时程策略游玩
papers.abstract_zh: 智能体大语言模型如今能够处理复杂任务，但长时程上的策略推理仍研究不足：大多数智能体基准都是短时程且分幕式的，而长任务上的表现很难被分解为存储知识、推理和运气。我们提出了 SpireBench，其中模型游玩完整的商业牌组构建游戏《杀戮尖塔》(Slay the Spire, StS)，在该游戏中早期决策决定长期成功。在游戏最高难度下，对 20 个大语言模型（LLM）进行评估，前沿模型击败了启发式基线，并与普通人类玩家相当，但仍远远落后于专家。随着一局游戏变长，这一差距会扩大：最强的模型赢得第一幕的频率与专家一样高，随后便落后了。区分强模型与弱模型的因素在于它们每场战斗玩得有多好；它们全都会在一局游戏中误判风险，倾向于保全生命值，而不是消耗生命值来变得更强。对每个游戏术语进行全面的、自洽的重命名表明，它们的部分表现依赖于对该游戏的先验知识，并且模型不会从它们跨多局游戏写下的记忆中取得提升，这些记忆常常是错误的且过于谨慎。我们的测试框架首次将完整的原版游戏提供给模型，并且我们将其与现有测试框架进行了比较。总体而言，SpireBench 提供了一个尚未饱和的长时程基准，并配有工具来定位智能体在何处以及为何失败。

papers.title: Beyond Binary Verifiable Rewards: Behavioral Self-Rewarding for SWE Agents
papers.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) provides reliable supervision for software engineering agents through executable tests, but binary rewards fail to distinguish trajectories with substantially different debugging quality. We investigate whether the current policy can judge its own trajectories and use these judgments to improve task performance without a separately trained reward model. To this end, we introduce Behavioral Self-Rewarding (BSR), a reward-refinement method that reuses the policy to compare observable debugging behavior among trajectories from the same task with the same verifier outcome. BSR aggregates pairwise preferences into task-local scores and converts them into bounded auxiliary rewards, introducing reward contrast while preserving the verifier-defined pass/fail ordering. This provides additional supervision from already-collected trajectories without requiring new environment interactions. Experiments on SWE-bench Verified and SWE-bench-Live show consistent improvements across the evaluated Qwen3-14B and Qwen3-32B configurations, supporting using the policy's own comparative judgments as a complementary learning signal for training software engineering agents.

papers.title: CLEAT: Learning Value-Guided Clarification for Interactive Agents
papers.summary: LLM agents can execute increasingly complex tasks, but effective assistance also requires aligning their actions with goals and constraints that users may leave unstated. We study this problem as interactive intent alignment through clarification. Yet clarification is useful only when the agent can turn the answer into better decisions. As training changes how the agent handles incomplete information and uses additional answers, the same clarification can become more or less useful. We introduce CLEAT (CLarification through valuE-guided Agent co-Training), a framework that co-trains a clarification-value controller and the task policy from shared interaction outcomes. We formulate residual query value to measure the task utility gained by asking rather than proceeding under the current policy, and estimate it through paired rollouts from the same interaction history. These paired returns train the controller to predict clarification value and the task policy to select useful questions and act on the answers. The controller guides subsequent rollout collection, while outcomes from the updated agent provide new value labels that allow clarification guidance to adapt as the agent learns. With Qwen3-4B, CLEAT achieves the highest mean score in all ten evaluation settings across four benchmarks. Gains over the strongest baseline reach 13.2 and 6.5 percentage points on UserGym Travel and IN3 underspecification judgment accuracy, respectively. Ablations show that co-training improves the task policy even when the controller is removed at inference, while adapting clarification guidance to the evolving policy yields further gains.

papers.title: MagicBeanStalk: Escaping the RLVR Zero Advantage Trap with Recursive Data Synthesis
papers.summary: Data-centric scaling of RLVR has focused on collecting or generating verifiable training problems. However, corpus size alone does not determine whether the dataset provides a useful learning signal for a target policy. To guide the synthesis of effective RLVR data, we experimentally characterize dataset effectiveness as a function of its problems, the target policy, and the training rollout budget. Under this characterization, we show that a large open-source math corpus pooled from widely used RLVR datasets falls almost entirely into a zero-advantage trap: for a fixed target policy and rollout budget, roughly 88% of its problems are solved in every rollout or failed in every rollout. Filtering concentrates what remains, but it can only select, discarding the hard problems. Effective synthetic problems should therefore require the reasoning operations and compositions required to solve those hard problems. Yet their difficulty must be calibrated, so that some rollouts succeed, some fail, and at least one correct solution fits within the training budget. Prompting a teacher to vary hard problems directly does not achieve this. Guided by these empirical principles, we introduce MagicBeanStalk, a top-down decomposition and bottom-up recursive data-synthesis algorithm that grows seed problems into families of substantively new, policy- and budget-calibrated training problems while preserving the seeds' reasoning blueprints. Across 8 math benchmarks, continual RLVR on MagicBeanStalk problems improves gpt-oss-120b from 61.2 to 69.8 (+8.6) and DeepSeek v4Flash from 72.4 to 77.9 (+5.4) on a 16K-token budget. Training on the full 78K source corpus improves by only +1.1 and its best filtered real data subset by +5.8. In finance, we synthesize over 14K verifiable problems from only 340 solutions and improve over base by 6.9 and 2.4 points on SecQue and FinanceBench, respectively.

papers.title: Faithful and Complete LLM-Assisted Automated Construction of Hierarchical Hardware Knowledge Graphs
papers.summary: Hardware datasheets contain engineering specifications essential for component selection, system integration, and hardware compatibility verification. However, manual inspection is tedious and error-prone because datasheets are lengthy and heterogeneous, with dense information fragmented across tables, figures, and text. Although large language models (LLMs) can automate this process, naïve one-shot processing omits relevant specifications even when the document fits within the model's context window. We present an automated LLM-driven pipeline that transforms hardware datasheets into general-purpose hierarchical hardware knowledge graphs through chunk-based property extraction, hierarchical routing, and iterative refinement. The framework uses LLMs for information extraction and semantic reasoning while preserving source provenance and applying graph updates through validated instructions and deterministic local execution. This staged design reduces per-query context and maintains traceable intermediate representations. The resulting knowledge graphs provide semantically organized, source-grounded hardware properties for downstream retrieval and reasoning. We evaluate the framework on 20 hardware datasheets spanning diverse component types and document lengths. We assess property faithfulness and introduce inter-graph completeness to measure relative semantic coverage without exhaustive ground truth. Our framework achieves 98.8% property faithfulness compared with 76.1% for the one-shot baseline, while fully covering 83.6% of faithful baseline properties; in the reverse direction, the baseline fully covers only 10.5% of ours. These improvements provide more reliable and comprehensive engineering information for downstream hardware design and verification, reducing the risk of overlooked constraints and incorrect decisions.
papers.title_zh: 忠实且完整的LLM辅助层次化硬件知识图谱自动构建
papers.abstract_zh: 硬件数据手册包含对元器件选型、系统集成和硬件兼容性验证至关重要的工程规格。然而，人工审查既繁琐又容易出错，因为数据手册篇幅冗长且格式异构，密集的信息分散在表格、插图和正文之中。尽管大语言模型（LLM）可以将这一过程自动化，但朴素的单次处理会遗漏相关规格，即使该文档能够放入模型的上下文窗口内。我们提出了一种由LLM驱动的自动化流水线，通过基于分块的属性抽取、层次化路由和迭代式精炼，将硬件数据手册转换为通用型层次化硬件知识图谱。该框架使用LLM进行信息抽取和语义推理，同时保留来源溯源信息，并通过经过验证的指令和确定性的本地执行来应用图更新。这种分阶段设计减少了每次查询所需的上下文，并保持了可追溯的中间表示。由此生成的知识图谱为下游检索与推理提供了语义组织化、有来源依据的硬件属性。我们在20份涵盖多种元器件类型和不同文档长度的硬件数据手册上对该框架进行了评估。我们评估属性忠实度，并引入图间完整度，以在没有穷尽式真值标注的情况下衡量相对语义覆盖度。我们的框架实现了98.8%的属性忠实度，而单次处理基线为76.1%；同时，我们的框架完整覆盖了基线中83.6%的忠实属性；反方向上，基线仅完整覆盖了我们属性的10.5%。这些改进为下游硬件设计与验证提供了更可靠、更全面的工程信息，降低了遗漏约束条件和做出错误决策的风险。

papers.title: Representation Alignment from a Few Paired Data via Distilled Optimal Transport
papers.summary: Aligning two independently pretrained unimodal encoders typically demands millions of paired examples. In this paper, we study the regime where only $N \sim 100$--$500$ pairs are available, while unpaired data on either side is abundant. Our method expresses every representation by its similarities to the $N$ paired anchors, which places both modalities in a common coordinate system; matches the two point clouds with a single entropic optimal transport problem solved over the entire pool, whose marginal constraints counteract the hubness that defeats nearest-neighbor matching; and distills the resulting plan into two lightweight encoders, so that the correspondence becomes inductive. We additionally put this marginal constraint in relation with the one-step hub corrections of the bilingual lexicon induction literature. Pairing is required only for the anchors: the unpaired collections may be drawn independently from the two marginals, so that no item outside the anchor set needs to have both of its modalities observed. We evaluate on image-text and molecule-text alignment, where our method outperforms existing approaches at the same anchor budget on Flickr30k, MS-COCO and ChEBI-20.

papers.title: EvoBelief: Falsifiable World Models for Self-Improving LLM Agents
papers.summary: Self-evolving LLM agents typically improve how they act through accumulated experience, reflection, or skills. Yet even procedurally capable agents can fail when their beliefs about environment dynamics are incomplete, incorrect, or outdated. We study a complementary axis of self-evolution: evolving those beliefs during deployment. Such beliefs can support multiple tasks, but incorrect ones can also propagate across them. We introduce EvoBelief, a self-evolving world model that represents environment knowledge as falsifiable hypotheses. Unexpected outcomes and decision-relevant unknowns trigger hypothesis formation. Later observations and controlled experiments provide independent validation before a rule can guide predictions or plans within its supported scope. Counterexamples narrow or retire rules as the environment changes. The language model remains frozen, and each rule remains linked to its evidence and the decisions it changes. Across four benchmarks spanning static dynamics, hidden drift, and scientific discovery, EvoBelief improves task performance and reuses learned rules across tasks. On ALFWorld without actor-side transition memory, it improves success over the matched Frozen World Model by 23.9% and 31.3% with Claude Haiku 4.5 and GPT-5.4, respectively. On MiniGrid, it revises stale rules and recovers after unannounced dynamics changes. In DiscoveryWorld's Reactor Lab, it discovers and validates quantitative laws, completing 83.3% of Normal-tier and 58.3% of Challenge-tier instances, versus 0% for each evaluated baseline. These results demonstrate self-improvement through testable, revisable environment knowledge rather than model-parameter updates.

papers.title: VEPA: Verified Evolving Formal Policy for Lifelong LLM Agent Guardrails
papers.summary: LLM agents increasingly operate over sensitive resources, such as private documents and mutable system states, which can create serious safety and security risks. Runtime guardrails should therefore make inspectable, reproducible, and deterministic allow or refuse decisions before potentially irreversible agent actions are executed. However, safety and security requirements are rarely complete before deployment, so guardrails need to keep adapting as new risks emerge. Existing adaptive guardrails learn from deployment experience, but they usually apply safety policies through LLM inference, which can lead to inconsistent decisions and ambiguous policy interpretations. Formal guardrails, on the other hand, enforce policies deterministically, but they usually rely on pre-deployment or task-specific policies and have no mechanism to adapt to newly observed risks. We introduce VEPA, a framework for the verified evolution of formal agent guardrails. VEPA represents the guardrail as a formal policy of executable symbolic rules over typed agent events. During deployment, we use an LLM guided by deployment feedback to propose policy patches that fix newly observed failures while preserving previously correct behavior. Then, a deterministic verifier only accepts policies that are structurally valid and conflict-free. Finally, an evidence-aware authority layer activates a verified rule only when it has enough supporting evidence, so uncertain updates cannot directly affect guardrail decisions. Across ASSEBench-Safety, ASSEBench-Security, and ATBench, VEPA consistently outperforms baselines while expanding the scope of deterministic formal-policy enforcement. These gains also hold under more challenging deployment conditions, including mixed streams, corrupted feedback, and longer horizons.

papers.title: Reward Hacking as a Transmissible Strategy in Multi-Agent Coding Systems
papers.summary: Multi-agent systems are increasingly used to solve coding tasks by coordinating agents that share code and plans. These agents are often optimized with reinforcement learning (RL) using automated evaluators, but bypassing evaluation can earn reward without producing a genuine solution. Prior work has largely treated reward hacking as a single-agent failure. In this work, we show that a reward-hacking strategy elicited in one agent can propagate to others and affect system coordination. Across four open-weight backbones, coding RL elicits and amplifies reward hacking in two settings: explicit mechanism descriptions in the system prompt and mid-training that models upstream exposure to facts about the coding environment. Using post-RL agents from the mid-training setting as sources, we observe propagation through code and shared memory, and across roles through natural-language plans. Even agents based on small open-weight models induce reward hacking in stronger closed-weight targets. On hard tasks, propagation can intensify along a transmission chain after the original source leaves as the code acquires more persuasive justifications. We also theoretically analyze conditions under which reward hacking amplifies, persists, or decays across agent interactions. Beyond propagation, reward hacking can bias task routing toward reward-hacking agents and survive candidate aggregation. As potential mitigations, we evaluate code review by the coder or a separate verifier, both of which reduce delivered hacks. Together, these results establish reward hacking as a transmissible strategy whose effects extend beyond the agent in which it first emerges.

papers.title: Neural networks are more modular than single neurons suggest
papers.summary: Neural networks routinely develop representations in which individual neurons contribute to multiple distinct functions, leading to the widespread view that such networks lack modular organization. We challenge this conclusion by introducing a formally nested hierarchy of modularity: unit-level, which requires distinct computations to occupy disjoint neurons; orthogonal, which asks whether a rotation reveals functionally independent subspaces; and linear, which asks whether a bounded linear map can separate task-relevant computations into independent subspaces. We develop a unified framework for learning decompositions at each level and evaluating them causally through selective ablation. Across vision models, language models and multi-task Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), we find that networks which lack unit-level modularity nonetheless often exhibit clear functional modularity at the subspace level. In vision and language models, content versus style and syntax versus semantics respectively dissociate under subspace ablation despite sharing overlapping populations of neurons. These learned subspaces also align differentially with brain data, with content and style subspaces predicting higher and lower visual cortex respectively, and semantic subspaces outperforming syntactic ones in predicting language cortex activity. In RNNs trained on multiple cognitive tasks and previously shown to lack modular structure, our decomposition recovers sharp double dissociations between tasks. The absence of unit-level modularity frequently coexists with clear subspace-level modularity across domains, enabling targeted intervention on specific computations even in networks where no individual neuron is specialized, with broad implications for mechanistic interpretability and for understanding functional organization in both biological and artificial neural systems.

papers.title: Towards Defining, Measuring, and Leveraging Creativity in AI Applications
papers.summary: Despite extensive research, computational creativity still lacks a conceptually grounded, practically relevant, and empirically applicable formal definition across contexts such as art, scientific research, and games. Existing approaches to creativity often focus on proposing informal conceptual definitions without providing formal computational concepts. Alternatively, they propose formal definitions without carefully examining their underlying assumptions or providing validation of these definitions by testing their performance in specific application settings. To address these problems, this paper proposes several formal postulates of creativity grounded in prior psychological work on creativity, especially as related to Boden's three core criteria of creativity: newness, value, and surprise. Furthermore, we propose a conceptual mathematical definition of creativity that aligns with these postulates. We also validate our proposed creativity formula in two applications: determining the creativity of particular chess moves, and assessing the creativity of paintings by some artists, such as Picasso, Renoir, and other painters. Experimental results demonstrate that our formula of creativity successfully captures creative patterns across both the chess and the art domains. This suggests that creativity can be effectively characterized through a unified mathematical structure based on three fundamental criteria, namely newness, value, and surprise, whose specific measurements are adapted to the particular domains.

papers.title: Mitigating Capability Degradation in LLM Self-Improvement via Representation Geometry Regularization
papers.summary: On-Policy Self-distillation is a self-improvement paradigm that enables large language models (LLMs) to improve their capabilities by leveraging the same model as both teacher and student under different conditioning contexts. However, we find that OPSD methods can progressively degrade previously acquired capabilities: queries that are correctly responded at earlier training stages may become incorrectly responded as optimization proceeds, even the overall performance continues to improve. Further analysis reveals that this degradation coincides with a deterioration of the geometry of hidden representations, characterized by reduced intra-cluster compactness and diminished inter-cluster separation. Motivated by this observation, we propose Representation Geometry Regularization (RGR), which preserves representation geometry during post-training by encouraging compactness within cluster and separation across cluster. RGR can be seamlessly integrated into existing OPSD methods without altering their core optimization procedures. Extensive experiments on multiple OPSD methods and benchmarks show that RGR generally alleviates capability degradation while retaining capability improvements. Our code is available in https://github.com/supermachinelearner/RGR.
papers.title_zh: 通过表示几何正则化缓解LLM自我改进中的能力退化
papers.abstract_zh: 在线策略自蒸馏（On-Policy Self-distillation）是一种自我改进范式，它通过在不同的条件上下文下将同一个模型同时用作教师和学生，使大语言模型（LLM）能够提升其能力。然而，我们发现OPSD方法会逐步退化此前已获得的能力：在训练早期阶段能够被正确回答的查询，随着优化的进行可能会变得被错误回答，即使整体性能仍在持续提升。进一步分析表明，这种退化与隐藏表示几何结构的恶化同时发生，其特征是簇内紧凑性降低和簇间分离度减小。受这一观察的启发，我们提出了表示几何正则化（Representation Geometry Regularization，RGR），它通过在簇内鼓励紧凑性、在簇间鼓励分离性，在后训练期间保持表示几何结构。RGR可以无缝集成到现有的OPSD方法中，而无需改变其核心优化流程。在多种OPSD方法和基准上的大量实验表明，RGR总体上缓解了能力退化，同时保留了能力提升。我们的代码可在 https://github.com/supermachinelearner/RGR 获取。

papers.title: Collaborative Theory of Mind: Learning to Self-Revise by Anticipating User Responses
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) demonstrate strong individual task performance, yet still struggle to collaborate with users over extended, multi-turn interactions, for example by attempting solutions before understanding the user's needs or by failing to revise mistaken assumptions after receiving feedback. We propose Collaborative Theory of Mind (CToM), a framework that addresses these challenges by explicitly training LLMs to anticipate user responses and to use those predictions to improve their own behavior. CToM drafts a response, predicts how the user will respond, and uses this prediction to guide internal revision before presenting a response. During training, the user's reply to each draft serves as the target for predicting the next turn, and we train the assistant to minimize the negative log-likelihood of that reply. We combine this prediction objective with group-relative policy optimization (GRPO) to optimize both task performance and interaction efficiency. Across mathematical reasoning, coding, and writing tasks, CToM achieves higher collaborative task performance than all baselines; for example, on a collaborative mathematical reasoning task, it improves final accuracy from 74.1% to 79.6% compared with naive GRPO. Ablations show that predicting user responses also makes collaboration more efficient: under the same reward, adding prediction supervision reduces the number of user replies by 8% on coding and 17% on writing while improving task performance. Behavioral analyses of interaction trajectories show that user-response predictions become more accurate after training, and that more accurate predictions are associated with larger improvements in collaborative task performance through self-revision.
papers.title_zh: 协作心智理论：通过预判用户回应学习自我修正
papers.abstract_zh: 大型语言模型（LLMs）展现出很强的独立任务性能，但在长时、多轮交互中仍难以与用户协作，例如在理解用户需求之前就尝试解决方案，或在收到反馈后未能修正错误假设。我们提出协作心智理论（CToM），一个通过显式训练 LLMs 预判用户回应并利用这些预测改进自身行为来应对这些挑战的框架。CToM 起草一个回应，预测用户将如何回应，并利用这一预测在呈现回应之前指导内部修正。在训练期间，用户对每个草稿的回复作为预测下一轮的目标，我们训练助手最小化该回复的负对数似然。我们将这一预测目标与组相对策略优化（GRPO）相结合，以同时优化任务性能和交互效率。在数学推理、编码和写作任务中，CToM 实现了比所有基线更高的协作任务性能；例如，在协作数学推理任务上，与朴素 GRPO 相比，它将最终准确率从 74.1% 提高到 79.6%。消融实验表明，预测用户回应还能使协作更高效：在相同奖励下，加入预测监督在编码任务上将用户回复数量减少 8%，在写作任务上减少 17%，同时提高任务性能。对交互轨迹的行为分析表明，经过训练后，用户回应预测变得更准确，而且更准确的预测与通过自我修正带来的协作任务性能更大提升相关。

papers.title: One-Step Text Generation by Seq-Drifting
papers.summary: Diffusion language models generate tokens in parallel, but still require multiple sampling steps to produce high-quality text. In this paper, we investigate whether a model can learn to generate an entire sequence in a single forward pass. We propose Seq-Drifting, a framework that applies drifting to sequences of continuous token representations and directly learns a map from Gaussian noise to text. Unlike existing DLMs that derive the supervision at each position directly from the observed token in a training sequence, Seq-Drifting builds a drift field whose position-wise targets adapt to the current generated context. At each position, attraction guides each output toward a set of contextually plausible token representations, while repulsion discourages collapse across samples and repetition within sequences. The generator learns from this drift field during training and produces all tokens jointly in one pass at inference. Empirically, Seq-Drifting achieves a generative perplexity of 36.01 on LM1B in one step and performs competitively in both unconditional and conditional generation. Experiments on translation, summarization, and reasoning further demonstrate the applicability of the framework beyond open-ended generation. These results suggest that drifting over token sequences offers a promising path toward effective one-step text generation. Our code is available at https://github.com/jyliu-ai/Seq-Drifting.
papers.title_zh: 通过 Seq-Drifting 的一步文本生成
papers.abstract_zh: 扩散语言模型并行生成 token，但仍然需要多个采样步骤才能生成高质量的文本。在本文中，我们研究模型能否学习在一次前向传播中生成整个序列。我们提出 Seq-Drifting，这是一个将 drifting 应用于连续 token 表示序列，并直接学习从高斯噪声到文本的映射的框架。与现有的 DLM 不同——它们在每个位置直接从训练序列中观测到的 token 推导监督信号——Seq-Drifting 构建了一个漂移场，其逐位置目标会适应当前生成的上下文。在每个位置，吸引力将每个输出引导向一组在上下文上合理的 token 表示，而排斥力则抑制样本间的坍缩和序列内的重复。生成器在训练期间从该漂移场中学习，并在推理时一次前向传播中联合生成所有 token。在实证上，Seq-Drifting 在 LM1B 上一步实现了 36.01 的生成困惑度，并在无条件生成和条件生成中均具有竞争力。在翻译、摘要和推理上的实验进一步证明了该框架在开放式生成之外的适用性。这些结果表明，对 token 序列进行 drifting 为有效的单步文本生成提供了一条有前景的路径。我们的代码可在 https://github.com/jyliu-ai/Seq-Drifting 获取。

papers.title: Mind the Spatial Gap: A Benchmark for Geospatial Reasoning and Constrained Spatial Editing
papers.summary: Understanding and manipulating spatial relations is fundamental to AI systems that reason about physical environments and construct grounded world models. However, existing evaluations of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) for spatial reasoning rely predominantly on static question-answering (QA) over small-scale or synthetic scenes, rarely probing whether models can modify spatial configurations while satisfying explicit geometric constraints. We introduce GeoSpatialBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate an escalating progression of spatial cognition, ranging from spatial relation understanding and geometric reasoning to constrained spatial editing. Grounded in real-world urban data across six geographically diverse cities, GeoSpatialBench evaluates a comprehensive taxonomy of 28 topological, directional, metric, and ordering relations across structured GeoJSON and map image modalities, with ground-truth references and constraints verified via GIS operations. Our empirical evaluation across frontier MLLMs uncovers a stark spatial gap: structured GeoJSON consistently outperforms map images, with multimodal combinations offering no reliable gain over GeoJSON alone, and while models show reasonable competence on qualitative topological and ordering, performance drops on quantitative metric relations. Crucially, editing performance on ordering relations declines relative to QA, and most failed edits violate at least one specified spatial constraint. These results highlight a gap between passively recognizing spatial relations and actively manipulating geometric configurations. GeoSpatialBench provides an open, rigorous diagnostic testbed to benchmark these spatial limitations, laying essential empirical groundwork for physically grounded world models and embodied spatial AI.
papers.title_zh: 留意空间鸿沟：面向地理空间推理与受约束空间编辑的基准
papers.abstract_zh: 理解和操作空间关系，对于推理物理环境并构建有根据的世界模型的人工智能系统而言是基础性的。然而，现有的针对空间推理的多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）评估主要依赖于在小规模或合成场景上的静态问答（QA），很少探究模型是否能够在满足明确几何约束的同时修改空间配置。我们提出 GeoSpatialBench，一个旨在评估逐步升级的空间认知进程的基准，其范围从空间关系理解与几何推理一直延伸到受约束的空间编辑。GeoSpatialBench 以横跨六座地理上多样化的城市的真实世界城市数据为基础，评估了一套涵盖 28 种拓扑、方向、度量和排序关系的综合分类体系，跨越结构化 GeoJSON 与地图图像两种模态，并配有通过 GIS 操作验证的真值参考与约束。我们针对前沿 MLLMs 的实证评估揭示出一个明显的空间鸿沟：结构化 GeoJSON 始终优于地图图像，多模态组合相较于单独使用 GeoJSON 并未提供可靠增益，并且尽管模型在定性拓扑与排序关系上表现出尚可的能力，其在定量度量关系上的性能却出现下降。至关重要的是，排序关系上的编辑性能相对于问答有所下降，且大多数失败的编辑都违反了至少一项指定的空间约束。这些结果凸显出被动识别空间关系与主动操作几何配置之间的差距。GeoSpatialBench 提供了一个开放、严谨的诊断性测试平台，用以对这些空间局限性进行基准测评，为物理上有根据的世界模型与具身空间人工智能奠定了至关重要的实证基础。

papers.title: OGPO: Offline Goal-conditioned Policy Optimization for Recoverable Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown strong promise in robotic manipulation, yet their post-training still predominantly relies on trajectory-level supervised imitation over robot demonstrations. While effective for learning feasible actions, this paradigm supervises policies to reproduce expert actions at each step, biasing them toward demonstration-specific action paths and providing limited guidance for recovering toward task-progress states once execution deviates from demonstrated trajectories. To address this limitation, we propose OGPO, an Offline Goal-conditioned Policy Optimization framework for recoverable VLA post-training. Instead of treating offline demonstrations merely as step-wise action labels, OGPO adaptively relabels trajectories with semantic key states and constructs goal-conditioned process rewards to optimize the policy for reaching these task-progress states. In this way, OGPO shifts VLA post-training from trajectory-level action imitation to key-state reachability learning, enabling policies to acquire a more robust ability to complete goal states from feasible off-demonstration states without requiring additional online interaction. Experiments on LIBERO and MetaWorld show that OGPO consistently improves VLA policy performance over standard supervised fine-tuning. Moreover, evaluations on LIBERO-Plus and our proposed LIBERO-ReAct, a mid-execution perturbation benchmark, further demonstrate that OGPO achieves stronger robustness and goal-directed recoverability under distribution shifts and recoverable off-demonstration states.

papers.title: DeFiRank: Federated Pairwise Ranking for Governance in Decentralized Financial Networks
papers.summary: Existing governance approaches in decentralized financial networks rely on manual review processes conducted by human committees, which introduces subjective bias, creates a scalability bottleneck under high network volume, and fails to capture complex behavioural patterns and evolving network dynamics. To address these limitations, we propose \name, a federated learning-based pairwise ranking framework in which multiple institutions collaboratively train a ranking model without sharing their private transaction data. This collaborative learning enables the model to capture network-wide behavioural patterns that signify strong network participation and directly contribute to the network effect, including diversity of counterparties, usage of multiple applications, and frequency of transactions. The proposed system ranks providers based on the authenticity of their actions, promoting genuine contributors and demoting those exhibiting suspicious behaviour. We evaluate \name\ on a real-world blockchain transaction dataset. Results demonstrate that the federated approach achieves ranking performance modestly below the centralized baseline (NDCG@15: $\approx$0.87 vs.\ $\approx$0.92) while preserving data privacy and matching its ranking stability (Kendall $τ$: $\approx$0.70 for both regimes), producing reliable governance decisions, including provider promotion and demotion (648 and 39 unique providers, respectively), without requiring centralized access to sensitive transaction data.

papers.title: AI-Mediation in Retail Markets: Revenue Effects and Assortment Optimization
papers.summary: AI shopping assistants increasingly influence which products consumers consider. We study retail assortment planning under AI mediation, where a retailer chooses a catalog, an AI intermediary forms a customer-facing shortlist, and the customer chooses from that shortlist according to a multinomial logit model. We consider both deterministic mediation, in which the AI follows a fixed segment-specific ranking, and stochastic mediation based on the Plackett-Luce model. Empirically, we construct a dataset of product rankings from leading AI models, estimate Plackett-Luce ranking models, and evaluate their predictive performance on held-out assortments. Combining these estimates with synthetic customer preferences, we find that accounting for AI mediation can materially change optimal assortments and revenue. Across the tested capacity configurations, ignoring mediation yields mean revenue losses between 2.52% and 11.37% relative to the PL optimum. A much simpler deterministic plug-in, based only on the ordering of fitted AI utilities, performs substantially better, with mean losses of at most 0.53%. Motivated by this performance, we study assortment optimization under deterministic mediation. We characterize its computational complexity and show that, for any fixed number of customer segments, the problem admits a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme.

papers.title: Teaching neural decoders with language
papers.summary: Brain-computer interfaces decode neural activity, yet class-label supervision (CLS) leaves relationships among classes implicit. We propose Language as Supervision (LaS), which aligns neural features with natural-language class descriptions through learned projections and predicts classes using candidate text prototypes. We evaluate seven encoder architectures with independently trained models for visual, motor, and speech decoding from scalp and intracranial recordings. LaS improves speech-decoding accuracy by up to 17.15~pp over matched CLS baselines. Its representations support candidate-set reuse and label-supervised subject and session adaptation, while LaS enables conditional unseen-frequency decoding in steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) responses. Correct class-description correspondence supports this generalization, and dual-sided attribution visualization shows neural and textual contributions to the same class-matching score. These findings suggest that text descriptions can serve as general-purpose references for learning and interpretation in neural decoding.

papers.title: Collaborative Learning and Reasoning over Model Slices
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) excel across diverse tasks, benefiting from knowledge priors, in-context reasoning, and test-time computation. Despite these strengths, single-model reasoning remains vulnerable to error propagation, as later steps depend on the model's earlier outputs, leaving reasoning blind spots difficult to independently reassess. To address this limitation, we develop \textit{collaborative learning}, encompassing the construction of heterogeneous collaborators and the learning of effective cross-model collaboration. Specifically, \textit{model slicing} replaces a large model with smaller, heterogeneous models under a comparable parameter budget, enabling prior reasoning to be reassessed across distinct model parameterizations. \textit{Pyramid supervision} combines protocol distillation with step-level supervision to refine reasoning and interaction decisions throughout collaboration. We evaluate our approach across four task categories: multi-hop question answering, mathematical reasoning, code generation, and open-ended constrained generation. The trained heterogeneous models achieve comparable or better task performance than the original large model and established multi-agent baselines, including reinforcement-learning-based methods, while also achieving higher inference efficiency than the multi-agent baselines and exhibiting differentiated collaboration patterns across tasks. These findings show that learned collaboration turns model heterogeneity into complementary reasoning capabilities.
papers.title_zh: 基于模型切片的协作学习与推理
papers.abstract_zh: 大型语言模型（LLMs）在各类任务中表现出色，这得益于知识先验、上下文内推理以及测试时计算。尽管具备这些优势，单模型推理仍然容易受到错误传播的影响，因为后续步骤依赖于模型较早的输出，从而留下难以独立重新评估的推理盲点。为了解决这一局限，我们提出了协作学习，其包括构建异构协作者以及学习有效的跨模型协作。具体而言，模型切片在可比的参数预算下用更小的异构模型替代一个大模型，使先前的推理能够在不同的模型参数化之间被重新评估。金字塔监督将协议蒸馏与步骤级监督相结合，以在整个协作过程中改进推理和交互决策。我们在四个任务类别上评估我们的方法：多跳问答、数学推理、代码生成以及开放式约束生成。训练后的异构模型取得了与原始大模型和现有多智能体基线（包括基于强化学习的方法）相当或更好的任务性能，同时还实现了比多智能体基线更高的推理效率，并展现出跨任务差异化的协作模式。这些发现表明，学习到的协作将模型异构性转化为互补的推理能力。

papers.title: Learning More by Training Less: Uncertainty-Guided Progressive Contraction for Efficient Reasoning Post-Training
papers.summary: Large language models have achieved remarkable advances in complex reasoning. However, scaling reasoning post-training with ever-larger corpora can substantially increase training cost without proportional performance gains. In this study, we therefore ask: how far can reasoning supervision be compressed without sacrificing capability? To this end, we propose an uncertainty-guided progressive contraction framework that concentrates supervision and optimization on the reasoning trajectories most valuable for learning. Specifically, rather than treating a teacher-generated chain-of-thought (CoT) as a single realized path, we construct uncertainty-profiled reasoning supervision by building Monte Carlo reasoning trees around intermediate reasoning states to expose process-level uncertainty. This uncertainty first contracts the original corpus into a compact teacher-informed pool. A second, learner-aware contraction then performs online routing during SFT, concentrating optimization according to the student's evolving learning state. Together, the two stages progressively contract both supervision and optimization, substantially reducing the student training budget. Experiments across diverse reasoning benchmarks and LLM families show that our method uses as little as 0.22% of the optimization budget of full-data SFT, over 450x less training exposure, while maintaining or improving reasoning performance. Notably, our framework generalizes well across heterogeneous student families, black-box teachers, and weak-to-strong transfer. This indicates that it is not only a way to accelerate training but can also enhance reasoning capability.
papers.title_zh: 训练更少，学到更多：不确定性引导的渐进收缩用于高效推理后训练
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型在复杂推理方面已取得显著进展。然而，用越来越大的语料库扩展推理后训练，会大幅增加训练成本，却无法带来成比例的性能提升。在本研究中，我们因此提出：在不牺牲能力的情况下，推理监督可以被压缩到什么程度？为此，我们提出一个不确定性引导的渐进收缩框架，将监督和优化集中在对于学习最有价值的推理轨迹上。具体而言，我们没有将教师生成的思维链（chain-of-thought, CoT）视为单一已实现的路径，而是通过围绕中间推理状态构建蒙特卡洛推理树，来构造具有不确定性画像的推理监督，以揭示过程级不确定性。这种不确定性首先将原始语料库收缩为一个紧凑的、由教师信息引导的池。第二个、感知学习者的收缩随后在 SFT 期间执行在线路由，根据学生不断演变的学习状态来集中优化。这两个阶段共同逐步收缩监督和优化，大幅减少学生模型的训练预算。在多种推理基准和 LLM 系列上的实验表明，我们的方法仅使用全数据 SFT 优化预算的 0.22%，训练暴露量减少超过 450 倍，同时保持或提升推理性能。值得注意的是，我们的框架在异构学生模型系列、黑盒教师以及弱到强迁移中均能很好地泛化。这表明，它不仅是一种加速训练的方法，还能够增强推理能力。

papers.title: MathVis: Can AI Reason through Drawing? A Benchmark for Mathematical Figure Generation
papers.summary: This paper introduces MathVis, a benchmark designed to evaluate LLMs' ability to visualize frontier mathematical problems and perform diagram-assisted reasoning. The benchmark consists of 512 tasks, each comprising a mathematical statement, a reference diagram, executable TikZ or SVG code, a Gold Intermediate Representation (IR), atomic rubrics, and error codes. Through rigorous evaluation, GPT-6-Astra, Claude Fable 5, and Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview achieve pass@1 scores of 31.25%, 26.56%, and 22.85%, respectively. We found that although the tasks require visualization, LLMs produce outputs dominated by formal languages, symbols, and graphics programs, rather than explicit diagram-mediated reasoning. Furthermore, while the solutions generated by LLMs may contain all the necessary elements, they are often visually confusing to humans. Ultimately, this benchmark aims to visualize mathematical problems and promote research on enabling LLMs to simplify their reasoning via visual diagrams.

papers.title: SmartSalesBench: A Resistance-Aware Multi-Turn Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Sales Agents
papers.summary: We present SmartSalesBench, the first multi-turn conversational benchmark explicitly designed to evaluate large language model (LLM) sales agents against psychologically grounded, resistant buyer personas. Existing task-oriented dialogue benchmarks assume cooperative users and measure task completion; SmartSalesBench inverts this assumption, placing agents against personas programmed to resist and challenge across conversations of up to twenty turns. The benchmark includes five agent profiles, twelve buyer personas, fifteen smartphone products across six price tiers, and four controlled experiments with 3 iterations totaling 13,680 sessions. Both sales-agent and buyer persona generations are grounded through retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). We introduce nine evaluation metrics grouped into three tiers: primary outcome metrics (CR, BRS, RIR), secondary quality metrics (SMS, PFS, ETI), and exploratory metrics planned for future reporting (ITS, ARI, SPI). Our evaluation combines automated LLM-as-judge scoring with internal human assessment (n = 50, \k{appa} = 0.71, Pearson r = 0.81 with BRS).
papers.title_zh: SmartSalesBench：一个用于评估 LLM 销售智能体的抗性感知多轮基准
papers.abstract_zh: 我们提出了 SmartSalesBench，这是首个明确设计用于评估大语言模型（LLM）销售智能体在与具有心理学依据的抗拒型买家角色交互时表现的多轮对话基准。现有的任务导向对话基准假设用户是合作的，并衡量任务完成情况；SmartSalesBench 颠倒了这一假设，让智能体面对被设定为在长达二十轮的对话中进行抗拒与挑战的角色。该基准包含五个智能体档案、十二个买家角色、横跨六个价格档位的十五款智能手机产品，以及四项受控实验，各进行 3 次迭代，总计 13,680 个会话。销售智能体与买家角色的生成均通过检索增强生成（RAG）加以锚定。我们引入了九项评估指标，划分为三个层级：主要结果指标（CR、BRS、RIR）、次要质量指标（SMS、PFS、ETI），以及计划在未来报告中使用的探索性指标（ITS、ARI、SPI）。我们的评估将自动化的 LLM 作为评判者的评分与内部人工评估相结合（n = 50，\k{appa} = 0.71，与 BRS 的 Pearson r = 0.81）。

papers.title: Beyond Semantic IDs: Finite-Beam Reachability and Continuous-Query Generation in Generative Recommendation
papers.summary: Generative recommendation (GR) of social media platforms commonly retrieves items by autoregressively decoding discrete Semantic IDs (SIDs) with finite-width beam search. This work examines how this output interface constrains whether held-out targets enter finite returned lists, while distinguishing catalog-wide scoreability from empirical top-K support. We introduce two continuous-query paradigms: CQG-Single generates one retrieval query in a single pass, and CQG-AR autoregressively generates continuous residual updates, retaining step-wise decoding while removing the SID item-token vocabulary, code lookup, and discrete beam expansion. These designs thereby eliminate the SID-specific reachability constraint induced by finite-beam decoding and avoid the technical challenge of aligning a discrete SID vocabulary with the pretrained backbone's vector space. Both methods make every encoded item directly scoreable through dense or approximate-nearest-neighbor retrieval. Under a unified protocol with valid-prefix constrained decoding, CQG-Single exceeds the TIGER-style baseline in all seven runs while using 55.3% as many trainable parameters. CQG-AR remains comparable on ML-1M and is numerically stronger on Beauty and Sports datasets. A controlled depth ablation further shows that additional continuous refinement does not monotonically improve shallow accuracy. These findings motivate decoupling output representation, autoregressive modeling, and retrieval budget when evaluating generative recommendation systems.

papers.title: Work2Skill: Capturing Human GUI Experience for Reusable Agent Skill Induction
papers.summary: Computer-use agents can perform increasingly complex GUI tasks, yet unfamiliar software and workflows requiring human domain knowledge remain challenging. Human demonstrations convey procedural knowledge through the same GUI interaction space, but reuse requires interpreting actions in context and separating workflow rules from task-specific details. We thus introduce Work2Skill, a framework that captures human GUI experience for reusable agent skill induction. WorkRecorder provides the framework's infrastructure for collecting this experience, aligning screen recordings, mouse and keyboard events, and available accessibility-tree information. Using WorkRecorder, we construct WorkDemo-350, the first synchronized multimodal dataset of human desktop GUI demonstrations for reusable agent skill induction and downstream evaluation. Its 350 demonstrations are screened for completeness and task success. We then propose an agentic skill-induction method that inspects evidence on demand to produce reusable skills capturing workflow rules, step dependencies, and completion checks. When the same four execution models are equipped with skills induced by each method under shared execution settings, Work2Skill achieves the highest scores and success rates. Mean score improvements over the corresponding No Skill baseline are 4.67--10.54 points on MyPCBench Bounded Action and 3.11--7.50 points on a 286-task subset of OSWorld-Verified. Our code and data are available at https://github.com/china-qijizhifeng/Work2Skill.

papers.title: Benchmarking Embedding Geometries and Clustering Algorithms for Unsupervised Patent Claim Classification
papers.summary: Prior-art retrieval systems are structurally organized around classification codes, making cross-code discovery difficult. This paper asks if an unsupervised representation trained on patent text can recover relevant connections that code-restricted search cannot, and if hyperbolic space helps. We trained a hyperbolic and a matched Euclidean Variational Autoencoder (VAE) on 45,000 US patents (96 runs, 6 seeds). The hyperbolic model retrieves genuinely cross-category prior art 52% more often than the Euclidean model (18.76% vs. 12.34% of top-10 results, 3,000 queries). This represents a practical gain for the motivating search problem. The hyperbolic model agrees less with official classification (NMI 0.2392 vs. 0.3206), which we explain geometrically: the two measures capture different goals, and only one aligns with prior-art search needs. In a study of 10 technology domains (50,000 more patents), we find that a domain's classification breadth--the number of distinct CPC subgroups spanned--predicts approach performance (Pearson r=-0.642, p=0.045, N=10), and that patents per subgroup is an even stronger predictor (r=0.715, p=0.020). This provides a checkable signal for practitioners to determine where the method is most valuable. We report all findings with statistical transparency and release a complete, 91-test automated implementation.

papers.title: Hindsight Structured Advice Distillation: Steering Executor Agents with Advisors Trained on Their Failures and Task Characteristics
papers.summary: Language-model agents are used for specialized work such as financial research, healthcare and law. Such agents are often capable enough for a task but still miss its details. In finance, for example, these details include which filing reports a figure or how a company discloses a metric. Retraining the agent to learn these details is expensive, and often impossible when the agent is a closed or shared system. Writing the missing know-how into the agent's prompt makes the prompt long and identical for every input, although different inputs need different guidance. We propose to learn to generate this guidance instead. A small advisor model reads each input and writes structured advice, which is appended to the prompt of a frozen executor. The advisor is trained with hindsight, following work on distillation with privileged information. On a training pool with graded answers, we analyse the executor's failures, run it under several strategies to see which one worked on each input, and let a teacher that sees the grades and the traces write the advice that would have helped. The advisor then learns, by supervised fine-tuning, to write that advice from the input alone. Because the student is a separate small model rather than the executor, it is cheap to train and adds little latency. We call this approach hindsight structured advice distillation (HSAD). On FrontierFinance, a public benchmark of expert-written financial research queries, an 8B advisor raises the qualification rate of Samaya's proprietary research agent, which already leads the benchmark's leaderboard, from 52.9% to 56.6%. This is above the agent's own high-effort configuration, at 37% lower cost per query. We study the generalization of the proposed approach, and in particular show that HSAD also improves results on WebShop, BIRD text-to-SQL and ExpertLongBench.

papers.title: Scaling Empowered Agents
papers.summary: Empowerment measures the capacity of an agent to actively control its environment. In this work, we explain the connection between skill learning and empowerment. While skill learning is not empowerment, we introduce a simple scalable recipe for empowerment maximization: empowerment corresponds to the number of executable skills from a state, so maximizing empowerment corresponds to reaching states that are good starting points for many skills. Our recipe applies to arbitrary underlying skill learning methods. Whereas most prior work on empowerment looks at tabular settings, this recipe enables us to study empowerment at a scale where we can realize theoretically-predicted but empirically-elusive properties of empowerment (e.g., gathering resources, environment modification, survival). Experiments show that empowerment maximization unlocks interesting emergent properties, such as building a house in Crafter. Website and code at \href{https://empowerment-geometry.github.io/scaling-empowerment/}{this https url}.

papers.title: Provenance-Aware Belief Updating in Human-AI Feedback Loops
papers.summary: In repeated human-AI interaction, a single observation can be quoted, summarized, and returned to a model as multiple reports, making repetition look like independent corroboration. We study whether language models can use supplied report lineage to update according to evidence provenance rather than report count. We introduce Latent Quotient Evidence Training (LQET), a relational objective that combines sparse Bayesian supervision with constraints that encourage stable predictions when reports add no new evidence and consistent updates to the same new evidence across relay histories. On a controlled binary benchmark, LQET reduces new-evidence update RMSE by 41-44% and log-odds drift after eight relay steps by 89-91% relative to task-only training across Qwen3-4B and Phi-4-mini, with three paired training seeds per backbone. The gains extend to a closed-loop simulation in which model confidence controls how many relayed reports re-enter the model's context in later rounds. By grounding belief updates in supplied provenance, LQET offers a route toward dynamic human-AI systems in which influence follows new evidence, not the number of times the same evidence returns.

papers.title: EmbodiedCLBench: Evaluating Continual Learning for Self-Evolving Embodied Agents
papers.summary: Continual learning requires models to accumulate past experience and transfer it to new tasks. Despite substantial research on continual learning, existing work remains largely confined to non-embodied settings, without extending to embodied environments. To address this gap, we introduce EmbodiedCLBench, the first benchmark in embodied simulation for evaluating the continual learning capability of self-evolving agents. With compositional generalization as the core evaluation principle, our benchmark evaluates whether agents can first learn from basic tasks and then recombine the acquired skills to solve complex, unseen advanced tasks. Based on EmbodiedCLBench, we conduct extensive experiments across multiple agent harnesses and learning methods, revealing consistent limitations and distinctive behaviors. Our results show that while advanced tasks can be hardly solved under zero-shot setting, the experience from basic tasks enables consistent improvement. Such benefit from the experience remains stable even if the task complexity increases. However, this improvement does not scale accordingly with the number of learning samples, and current agents cannot extract meaningful information from additional experience. Collectively, our findings highlight continual learning as a fundamental yet underexplored capability, and our benchmark offers valuable resources for designing effective self-evolving agents in embodied environments. Our code and dataset are available at https://pku-value-lab.github.io/EmbodiedCLBench-homepage.

papers.title: Travel Back To Move Forward: Retrospective Exploration and Evolving for Long Horizon Agents
papers.summary: Large language model agents increasingly operate in long-horizon environments where early mistakes can trigger cascading failures and trap agents in dead-end trajectories. Agents must therefore be able to proactively recover from such states and turn their exploratory experience into guidance for subsequent decisions. We introduce ReTRAIL, a framework that enables agents to rewind the environment to earlier states while preserving valid progress and carrying forward knowledge learned from abandoned exploration. The environment state moves backward while the agent's knowledge continues to move forward. ReTRAIL trains a shared policy with two complementary signals: State-Anchored GRPO compares alternative continuations from revisited states to improve execution, while a branch-advancement reward guides reflection through the progress of subsequent exploration. Experiments across four interactive benchmark MineSweeper, Sokoban, ALFWorld and ScienceWorld show that simply adding a rewind primitive provides limited benefit and can even degrade performance. In contrast, ReTRAIL enables agents to rewind from unproductive states and use insights from abandoned branches to guide subsequent exploration. These results demonstrate the value of coupling environment rewinding with experience reuse within an ongoing task for long-horizon task solving. The code is available at https://github.com/whi497/ReTRAIL.
papers.title_zh: 回溯以向前：面向长时程智能体的回顾式探索与演化
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型智能体越来越多地在长时程环境中运行，在这些环境中，早期错误可能引发级联失败，并使智能体陷入死胡同轨迹。因此，智能体必须能够主动从此类状态中恢复，并将其探索经验转化为后续决策的指导。我们提出 ReTRAIL，一个使智能体能够将环境回退到较早状态，同时保留有效进展并向前传递从被放弃探索中学到的知识的框架。环境状态向后移动，而智能体的知识继续向前推进。ReTRAIL 使用两个互补信号训练一个共享策略：状态锚定的 GRPO 比较从重访状态出发的不同延续，以改进执行，而分支推进奖励通过后续探索的进展来引导反思。在四个交互式基准 MineSweeper、Sokoban、ALFWorld 和 ScienceWorld 上的实验表明，仅仅添加一个回退原语带来的收益有限，甚至可能降低性能。相比之下，ReTRAIL 使智能体能够从无成效状态回退，并利用来自被放弃分支的洞见来指导后续探索。这些结果表明，在正在进行的任务中将环境回退与经验复用耦合起来，对于长时程任务求解具有价值。代码可在 https://github.com/whi497/ReTRAIL 获取。

papers.title: LongHarness: Advancing Agentic Reasoning over 100M-Token Corpora via Stateful Evidence Management
papers.summary: Corpus-level long-context reasoning requires agents to acquire and integrate evidence across document collections that exceed their context windows. Existing agent harnesses enable incremental access to these corpora, but acquired evidence and evolving conclusions often remain entangled in a growing interaction history. This implicit state management can lead to two coupled failure modes: unbounded exploration, where retrieval expands the interaction history without resolving decision-relevant information gaps, and evidence-state drift, where previously acquired evidence or subsequent corrections fail to inform the current conclusion. We present LongHarness, a model-agnostic harness that makes the interaction between acquired evidence and evolving conclusions explicit. Its core mechanism, Evidence-Conclusion Coevolution, uses unresolved conclusions to guide exploration toward missing information, while newly acquired evidence strengthens or revises the conclusions that directed the search. LongHarness couples this process with Evidence Lifecycle Management, which keeps accumulated evidence current and traceable throughout the interaction. Together, these mechanisms focus retrieval on remaining information needs and keep conclusions aligned with current evidence. We evaluate LongHarness on OfficeQA Pro V1 and V2, AA-LCR, and LongBench v2 using GLM-5.3-Flash and Qwen3.8-Flash. Compared with direct reasoning using the same backbone, LongHarness improves GLM-5.3-Flash exact match on OfficeQA Pro from 15.8% to 60.2% on V1 and from 4.4% to 61.1% on V2. Against state-of-the-art agent harnesses, it surpasses Claude Code by 12.0 percentage points on V1 and Codex by 18.9 points on V2. With Qwen3.8-Flash, LongHarness reaches 61.7% on V1, outperforming Claude Code by 8.3 points and Codex by 12.0 points.

papers.title: Attention Sees, MLP Refuses: Tracing the Attention-to-MLP Safety Pathway in LLMs
papers.summary: Safety-aligned large language models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to jailbreaks and can over-refuse benign requests. Understanding these failures requires distinguishing harmfulness recognition from the computation that writes refusal. We reframe this as a pathway question and make it measurable on residual-stream updates in decoder-only Transformers, separating the harmfulness information a module update exposes from the change it produces in readable refusal evidence. Across 18 Base-Instruct pairs spanning Qwen, Llama, and Gemma, harmfulness is decoded more readily from attention updates, particularly in early layers, whereas MLP updates contribute more strongly to harm-selective refusal writing in aligned models. Post-training strengthens MLP refusal writing in all 18 pairs without systematically improving harmfulness decodability, while positive MLP writing becomes more concentrated in deeper layers after post-training. Across six reasoning-enabled models, harmfulness remains decodable during reasoning while strong refusal writing concentrates at answer onset, a pattern that persists with reasoning disabled. Causal interventions further support this pathway: resetting downstream MLP updates to their clean values substantially reduces the refusal shift caused by upstream attention interventions. Building on these findings, we introduce Sentinel, which combines an attention-derived perception score P with an MLP-derived decision score D. Their joint profiles characterize jailbreaks and over-refusals, and conditional routing with both signals achieves a lower aggregate error rate than single-signal routing and evaluated fixed reminders across eight models.
papers.title_zh: 注意力看见，MLP 拒绝：追踪 LLM 中的注意力到 MLP 安全通路
papers.abstract_zh: 安全对齐的大语言模型（LLM）仍然容易受到越狱攻击，并且可能过度拒绝良性请求。理解这些失败需要区分有害性识别与写出拒绝的计算。我们将其重新表述为一个通路问题，并在仅解码器 Transformer 的残差流更新上使其可测量，分离一个模块更新所暴露的有害性信息与其在可读拒绝证据中产生的变化。在涵盖 Qwen、Llama 和 Gemma 的 18 个 Base-Instruct 对中，有害性更容易从注意力更新中解码出来，尤其是在早期层，而 MLP 更新在对齐模型中对伤害选择性拒绝写出的贡献更强。后训练在所有 18 对中都增强了 MLP 拒绝写出，却没有系统性地提升有害性可解码性，而正向 MLP 写出在后训练后变得更加集中于更深层。在六个启用推理的模型中，有害性在推理过程中仍可解码，而强拒绝写出现在答案开始时集中，这一模式在禁用推理时仍然存在。因果干预进一步支持这一通路：将下游 MLP 更新重置为其干净值，会显著减少由上游注意力干预引起的拒绝偏移。基于这些发现，我们引入 Sentinel，它结合了注意力导出的感知分数 P 和 MLP 导出的决策分数 D。它们的联合画像刻画了越狱和过度拒绝，而在八个模型上，使用这两个信号的条件路由比单信号路由和所评估的固定提醒实现了更低的总体错误率。

papers.title: SWEAR: Section-Wise Efficient Audio Reasoning via Self-Rated Difficulty
papers.summary: Recent work on large audio-language models (LALMs) explores adaptive reasoning to balance accuracy and efficiency. However, existing approaches often rely on coarse-grained difficulty estimation, overlooking the diverse factors that determine reasoning effort. We address this limitation by deriving five-dimensional difficulty scores and compressed reasoning traces from complementary offline assessments. Based on this characterization, we propose SWEAR, a difficulty-aware reasoning framework that learns difficulty signals during supervised fine-tuning and uses reinforcement learning to adapt reasoning allocation across reasoning stages. Experiments on MMAU-test-mini and MMAR show that SWEAR improves accuracy while substantially reducing generated tokens, shortening reasoning for easy instances without sacrificing performance on difficult ones.

papers.title: When Faster Decisions Do Not Make Better Agents: An Empirical Study of Jev in Agent Workflows
papers.summary: AI agents depend on repeated decisions to accomplish tasks, with large language models (LLMs) commonly serving as their core decision makers. The recent emergence of Jev offers an opportunity to make these decisions faster and at lower cost. However, it remains unclear whether such local savings can be translated into efficient and reliable task completion. In this paper, we investigate this efficiency transfer across five agents in two representative application settings, embodied tasks in ALFWorld and mobile app use in AndroidWorld. Across 4,500 task executions, we jointly evaluate task effectiveness, decision-level and task-level resource use, and execution behavior. Experimental results show that Jev integration substantially reduces decision cost and latency across all five agents, with task-level gains varying by workflow. Task success remains close to baseline levels on ALFWorld and declines more substantially in two mobile agents. Auxiliary reasoning and additional interactions absorb decision savings, while failed recovery and premature completion limit successful delivery. Mean cost per successful outcome increases in one agent even as spending per attempt falls. These findings highlight the importance of preserving progress, supporting recovery, and verifying completion when integrating efficient decision models into agent workflows. Their practical value should be assessed through successful task delivery, recovery behavior, and resources per delivered outcome.
papers.title_zh: 当更快的决策并不能造就更优的智能体：Jev 在智能体工作流中的实证研究
papers.abstract_zh: AI 智能体依赖重复决策来完成任务，而大语言模型（LLM）通常充当其核心决策者。近期出现的 Jev 为更快、成本更低地做出这些决策提供了机会。然而，此类局部节省能否转化为高效且可靠的任务完成仍不清楚。本文在两个代表性应用场景中考察了这种效率迁移，涉及五个智能体：ALFWorld 中的具身任务与 AndroidWorld 中的移动应用使用。在 4,500 次任务执行中，我们联合评估了任务有效性、决策级与任务级资源使用以及执行行为。实验结果表明，集成 Jev 在全部五个智能体上都大幅降低了决策成本与延迟，而任务级收益则因工作流而异。在 ALFWorld 上，任务成功率仍接近基线水平，而在两个移动智能体中下降更为明显。辅助推理与额外的交互吸收了决策节省，而失败的恢复与过早完成则限制了成功交付。尽管单次尝试的开销下降，但在一个智能体中，每个成功结果的平均成本反而上升。这些发现凸显了在将高效决策模型集成到智能体工作流时，保持进展、支持恢复以及验证完成的重要性。其实际价值应通过成功任务交付、恢复行为以及每个已交付结果的资源消耗来评估。

papers.title: VETR: Execution-Grounded Self-Improving Agent for Symbolic Graphics Reasoning
papers.summary: Visual agents for symbolic graphics reasoning depend on executable world representations, yet continued improvement remains bottlenecked by ambiguous supervision from final renders. Recent agentic systems refine scenes through repeated interaction, but they lack mechanisms to recursively extract actionable evidence from execution traces, overlooking which proposed symbolic edits survived, disappeared, or interfered during program execution. To address this, we propose VETR (Verified Execution Trajectories for Refinement), a framework that enables agentic recursive self-improvement over executable world representations for symbolic graphics reasoning. Within each task, VETR retains aligned program/render records with bounded runtime observations and introduces an execution refiner that compiles observed writes and state changes into constrained alternative programs. The refiner validates their endpoints and preservation conditions against captured runtime state; the ordinary visual verifier then assesses goal relevance. Repair construction makes no additional language-model calls, but can require additional executions. Evaluations on BlenderGym (280 tasks) and BlenderBench (27 released tasks) with GPT-5.6-luna and Qwen3.8-27B show that VETR consistently outperforms existing refinement strategies, including BlenderAlchemy and VIGA. Controlled ablations evaluate the contributions of execution refinement and role-asymmetric evidence organization under fixed generator-interaction caps.

papers.title: Does Location Matter? A Black-Box Causal Audit Reveals Model-Dependent Audio Grounding in LALM Hallucination
papers.summary: Large audio-language models (LALMs) frequently exhibit object hallucination, affirming absent sounds. The dominant mitigation, Audio-Aware Decoding (AAD), contrasts logits under real audio against an all-zero "blank" waveform, flagged by prior review as out-of-distribution. We introduce a black-box causal test that isolates the claimed evidence itself: localize a claim's evidence region via CLAP similarity, remove it by spectral gating, and compare against a random-window control across a 2x2x2 grid on three LALMs. On Qwen2-Audio-7B, localized ablation's raw AUROC trails blank's (0.613 vs. 0.721); this is a duration confound, not a localization failure, since blank removes the entire clip versus the grid's 2-4 s. Holding duration fixed, localization beats random removal at every cell on both models. Raw detection value remains model-dependent, especially on Audio Flamingo 3. The same evidence corrects decoding: contrastive decoding combining blank and language-prior contrasts, gated and ensembled, raises Qwen2-Audio accuracy from 57.1% to 71.9%, beating AAD alone. A unified causal-grounding profile does not transfer between models, indicating different grounding regimes. The source code and a detailed report of our findings, including identified limitations, are available at https://github.com/khalooei/causa.

papers.title: DRYLAB-Bench: Benchmarking the Biosecurity Risk of Agentic LLM Mutation Design
papers.summary: As large language models (LLMs) acquire advanced biological design capabilities, they offer substantial research benefits but simultaneously introduce severe dual-use risks, such as engineering enhanced pathogens or drug-resistant bacteria. While biosecurity frameworks recognize these threats, the actual risk of LLMs executing dangerous biological modifications remains unquantified, particularly when augmented with specialized biological design tools (BDTs). Existing evaluations primarily assess hazardous knowledge possession rather than practical application, overlook risk amplification from BDTs, and rely on unreliable, expensive, or hazardous validation methods. To address these gaps, we introduce DRYLAB-Bench (Design Risk Yielded by LLM Agent in Biodesign), the first comprehensive benchmark evaluating the high-risk biological mutation design capabilities of LLM agents. Moving beyond basic question-answering, DRYLAB-Bench tasks agents with 30 genuinely hazardous mutation-design scenarios distilled from biosecurity guidelines. It evaluates models in a multi-round, tool-augmented environment where LLMs orchestrate BDTs to iteratively refine candidates. Crucially, it scores designs directly against 187,695 empirical wet-lab measurements from ProteinGym and ViroGym using our proposed Biosecurity Risk Score (BRS), quantifying risk-associated effects while enabling scalable and safe ground-truth verification. Evaluations of 15 frontier models reveal substantial baseline threats: without tools, 67.6% of one-shot designs exceed the average measured variant, and 21.4% reach the highest-risk decile. Equipping models with BDTs significantly amplifies this risk, raising the pooled risk by \(ΔBRS=+0.116\) and the top-decile share to 23.5%. Code: https://github.com/drylab-bio/DRYLAB-Bench
papers.title_zh: DRYLAB-Bench：对智能体式 LLM 突变设计的生物安全风险进行基准测试
papers.abstract_zh: 随着大型语言模型（LLM）获得先进的生物设计能力，它们提供了可观的研究收益，但同时也引入了严重的两用风险，例如工程化增强的病原体或耐药细菌。尽管生物安全框架认识到这些威胁，但 LLM 执行危险生物修饰的实际风险仍未量化，尤其是在借助专门的生物设计工具（BDT）增强时。现有评估主要评估危险知识的掌握程度，而非实际应用，忽视了 BDT 带来的风险放大，并依赖于不可靠、昂贵或危险的验证方法。为弥补这些空白，我们提出 DRYLAB-Bench（由生物设计中的 LLM 智能体产生的设计风险），这是首个评估 LLM 智能体高风险生物突变设计能力的综合基准。超越基本的问答，DRYLAB-Bench 为智能体布置了 30 个从生物安全指南中提炼出的真正危险的突变设计场景。它在多轮、工具增强的环境中评估模型，其中 LLM 编排 BDT 以迭代地改进候选方案。关键的是，它使用我们提出的生物安全风险评分（BRS），将设计直接与来自 ProteinGym 和 ViroGym 的 187,695 项实证湿实验测量结果进行评分比较，从而量化与风险相关的效应，同时实现可扩展且安全的真值验证。对 15 个前沿模型的评估揭示了大量基线威胁：在没有工具的情况下，67.6% 的单次设计超过了平均实测变体，21.4% 达到最高风险十分位。为模型配备 BDT 会显著放大这一风险，使汇总风险提高 \(ΔBRS=+0.116\)，并将最高十分位占比提高到 23.5%。代码：https://github.com/drylab-bio/DRYLAB-Bench

papers.title: Locate, Judge, Read: Role-Specialized Tool Agents over a Knowledge-Point Index for Open-Domain Multimodal Document QA
papers.summary: Question answering over large heterogeneous document collections requires first finding the right passages and then reading them, yet current retrieval-augmented agents give one model both kinds of tools and let it schedule itself. We present KnowForge, a pipeline separated by job: a hybrid-retrieval knowledge-point index; a Locator agent that can only search; a code-scheduled bridge judge that forces the missing second hop; a typed, size-bounded evidence pool that merges every search's ranking; a Deep Reader agent that can only read text, images and tables; and a synthesizer with a format checker. With a self-hosted Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (3B active), KnowForge reaches F1 47.5 on the full open-domain M3DocVQA (2,441 questions, 3,368 PDFs), +11.0 over the published M3DocRAG system and +7.1 over one-shot retrieve-and-answer on the same index and model, and 53.5 with DeepSeek-V4-Flash. On MultiHop-RAG it reaches 73.5 accuracy, above the strongest published RAG and GraphRAG results (71.2); on the single-document MMLongBench-Doc it lifts the same model from 34.8 to 47.0, level with GPT-4o reading page images (46.3). Per-job ablations on the full benchmarks attribute the gain: the Deep Reader is worth 3.8, 9.8 and 0 points on the three corpora, tracking how visual each is; merging both agents into one with all tools and twice the rounds loses 1.9 F1 because it keeps searching instead of reading; a round-budget sweep shows a step at four Locator rounds and a plateau beyond; query latency scales with model calls rather than corpus size. We serve the three indexed benchmarks as read-only knowledge bases (free registration) and release all prompts and the runner code: https://github.com/metask-ai/knowforge-bench

papers.title: Looking Ahead and Back: Anticipatory Generative Modeling for Road-Network Trajectories
papers.summary: Trajectory generation underpins urban applications such as traffic management and urban planning. Within road networks, vehicle movement along road segments is largely deterministic, whereas transitions at intersections are critical--multiple outgoing paths may appear equally plausible, yet they can lead to substantially different downstream routes. Existing generative methods such as diffusion models simulate location sequences and fail short of next transition selection, even producing trajectories that drift off the road network. To fill this gap, we advocate a fundamental shift: moving beyond location simulation toward behavior modeling on the road network. In this paper, we revisit trajectory generation through the lens of generative route planning, and introduce a new graph-constrained generative paradigm, Anticipatory Generative Modeling, which resolves next transition selection by incorporating the Anticipation of how the future route may unfold toward the destination. Concretely, we propose a novel generative model named Foresight that formulates a probabilistic model for an "anticipate--select--update--re-anticipate" loop that enables longer-term foresight while continuing sequential generation along the historical trajectory. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Foresight wins state-of-the-art baselines.
papers.title_zh: 前瞻与回顾：面向路网轨迹的预期式生成建模
papers.abstract_zh: 轨迹生成支撑着交通管理与城市规划等城市应用。在路网中，车辆沿路段的移动在很大程度上是确定性的，而交叉口处的转移则至关重要——多条驶出路径可能看起来同样合理，但它们却可能导致显著不同的下游路线。现有的生成方法（如扩散模型）模拟位置序列，未能完成下一转移的选择，甚至会产生偏离路网的轨迹。为填补这一空白，我们倡导一种根本性转变：从位置模拟走向路网上的行为建模。在本文中，我们以生成式路径规划的视角重新审视轨迹生成，并提出一种新的图约束生成范式——预期式生成建模（Anticipatory Generative Modeling），它通过纳入对未来路线可能如何朝目的地展开的预期（Anticipation），来解决下一转移的选择问题。具体而言，我们提出了一种名为 Foresight 的新型生成模型，它为“预期—选择—更新—再预期”这一循环构建概率模型，从而在沿历史轨迹继续序列生成的同时实现更长期的前瞻。大量实验表明，Foresight 优于最先进的基线方法。

papers.title: DP-MIND: Differentially private memory-guided Long context Inference
papers.summary: LLM-as-a-Service has become a dominant paradigm for accessing large language models without requiring local deployment. However, the process raises severe privacy concerns when user queries may include sensitive or confidential contexts. Differential privacy (DP) provides a principled approach to protecting such inputs, but existing DP inference methods are primarily designed for short- or moderate-context settings and struggle with million-token-scale inputs due to limited context capacity and severe utility degradation under DP perturbation. In this paper, we propose DP-MIND, a memory-guided framework that scales differentially private inference to million-token contexts. DP-MIND enables private long-context inference by locally perturbing the input and processing it chunk by chunk with a compact memory that preserves task-relevant information across the sequence. To make this memory robust to DP noise, we optimize the memory construction policy directly on perturbed inputs using reinforcement learning, guided by both final answer correctness and memory consistency. We further recover perturbation-corrupted answer spans through a local denoising module without exposing the original context to the external model. We provide theoretical privacy analysis of DP-MIND and further conduct extensive empirical analysis across multiple long-context benchmarks with context lengths up to the million-token scale, demonstrating that DP-MIND consistently outperforms existing DP and long-context inference baselines in both scalability and utility.
papers.title_zh: DP-MIND：差分隐私记忆引导的长上下文推理
papers.abstract_zh: LLM-as-a-Service 已成为无需本地部署即可访问大语言模型的主导范式。然而，当用户查询可能包含敏感或机密上下文时，这一过程会引发严重的隐私担忧。差分隐私（DP）为保护此类输入提供了一种有原则的方法，但现有的 DP 推理方法主要针对短上下文或中等上下文设置设计，并且由于上下文容量有限以及 DP 扰动下效用严重退化，难以处理百万 token 规模的输入。在本文中，我们提出 DP-MIND，一种记忆引导框架，可将差分隐私推理扩展到百万 token 上下文。DP-MIND 通过在本地扰动输入，并使用一种紧凑记忆逐块处理输入，从而在整个序列中保留任务相关信息，实现私有长上下文推理。为使该记忆对 DP 噪声具有鲁棒性，我们使用强化学习直接在扰动输入上优化记忆构建策略，并由最终答案正确性和记忆一致性共同指导。我们进一步通过本地去噪模块恢复被扰动破坏的答案片段，而无需将原始上下文暴露给外部模型。我们提供 DP-MIND 的理论隐私分析，并进一步在多个长上下文基准上进行了大量实证分析，上下文长度最高达到百万 token 规模，证明 DP-MIND 在可扩展性和效用方面均持续优于现有的 DP 和长上下文推理基线。

papers.title: Competence-Aware Orchestration for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
papers.summary: LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) have emerged as a promising paradigm for enhancing complex reasoning through role specialization and collaboration, yet a key challenge remains: how can collaboration be adapted to a backbone's competence on the current query? This problem matters because more collaboration is not always better--richer coordination may help on difficult cases, but it also incurs additional token cost and redundant interactions. We propose a two-stage competence-aware framework for automatic MAS orchestration. It first models the LLM backbone's task-conditioned competence for the current query, and then uses this signal to adapt role activation and the communication graph. Across six benchmarks, our method achieves an average score of 93.81%. Experiments with six LLM backbones of varying competence levels further show that our method adjusts collaboration according to the inferred competence: for higher-competence backbones, it improves average accuracy from 87.22 to 89.97 while reducing token cost by 36.26%; for lower-competence backbones, it yields a further average gain of 4.58 points over existing methods. The same trend also holds on unseen backbones.

papers.title: VIGOR: Verifiable Industrial Geometry Optimization and Repair in Scene Programs
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly generate structured layouts and executable scene programs from natural-language instructions. However, executability does not imply engineering feasibility: an industrial scene program may execute successfully while its final state still violates coupled boundary, collision, clearance, aisle, or structural constraints. We identify this mismatch as the executability-engineering-feasibility gap, where locally plausible placements can remain globally infeasible because corrections to one device may introduce violations elsewhere. To make this gap measurable in a controlled setting, we construct an execution-grounded industrial scene-program dataset with 1,749 constructible scenarios, complete executable programs, and 94 final-state geometric checks per scenario. We further propose VIGOR, which combines supervised scene-program generation with execution-grounded verification and staged geometric refinement. Supervised fine-tuning establishes complete program generation, local projection resolves independently correctable violations, and joint conflict-graph repair coordinates residual multi-object conflicts while preserving structural relations. Experiments show that VIGOR achieves 96.86% Complete Feasibility and an Overall score of 91.20, outperforming the strongest evaluated baseline by 10.42 points in Overall. These results show that, under controlled industrial layout conditions, reliable scene-program generation requires not only executable programs, but also explicit verification and coordinated resolution of coupled engineering constraints.
