papers.title_zh: VIGOR：场景程序中可验证的工业几何优化与修复
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型（LLMs）越来越多地从自然语言指令生成结构化布局和可执行的场景程序。然而，可执行性并不意味着工程可行性：一个工业场景程序可能成功执行，但其最终状态仍然违反耦合的边界、碰撞、间隙、通道或结构约束。我们将这一不匹配识别为可执行性—工程可行性鸿沟，其中局部看似合理的放置可能在全局上仍然不可行，因为对一个设备的修正可能会在其他地方引入违规。为了在受控环境中使这一鸿沟可度量，我们构建了一个基于执行的工业场景程序数据集，包含 1,749 个可构造场景、完整的可执行程序，以及每个场景 94 项最终状态几何检查。我们进一步提出 VIGOR，它将监督式场景程序生成与基于执行的验证以及分阶段的几何精化相结合。监督微调建立了完整的程序生成，局部投影解决了可独立纠正的违规，联合冲突图修复在保持结构关系的同时协调残余的多物体冲突。实验表明，VIGOR 实现了 96.86% 的完全可行性以及 91.20 的总分，在 Overall 指标上以 10.42 分的优势超过最强的评估基线。这些结果表明，在受控的工业布局条件下，可靠的场景程序生成不仅需要可执行的程序，还需要对耦合工程约束进行显式验证与协调求解。

papers.title: Quality, Not Just Outcome: A Structural Scoring Framework for Selecting Coding-Agent Trajectories for Supervised Fine-Tuning
papers.summary: Open coding agents are commonly trained through supervised fine-tuning on interaction trajectories whose final patches pass the benchmark test suite. However, this outcome-level filtering criterion ignores process quality: trajectories that eventually succeed may still contain inefficient interaction patterns such as repetitive file inspection, unstable tool usage, or delayed modification behavior, all of which become part of the imitation target. We propose TQS (Trajectory Quality Score), a structural scoring framework for coding-agent trajectories that operates directly on trajectory structure, requires no LLM judge, and runs in linear time. TQS characterizes trajectory quality through structural signals organized around structured convergence: information focus, intent--action alignment, and policy dynamics. Using 155,144 successful trajectories from a public open-license corpus, we rank trajectories by TQS and fine-tune coding agents on filtered subsets. Models trained on top-ranked trajectories consistently outperform those trained on random or bottom-ranked subsets on SWE-Bench-Verified. Our results suggest that process-level trajectory quality is an important factor in coding-agent supervision and that structural trajectory filtering provides an effective and scalable alternative to LLM-based data selection.

papers.title: RoleWorld: Knowledge Transfer in World Modeling with Functional Role Abstractions
papers.summary: World models enable large language model (LLM) agents to anticipate action effects and make informed decisions. For generalization, it is desirable for such world models to transfer efficiently to new environments with similar interaction structure and underlying dynamics. Recent approaches encode world dynamics as symbolic rules or executable programs, whose compositional structure in principle affords transfer, but still organize such knowledge around environment-specific objects. To address this limitation, we introduce RoleWorld, a symbolic world modeling approach which uses reusable prototypes and environment-specific parameter values as functional role abstractions to represent how objects behave in interactions. From interaction trajectories, a teacher LLM extracts role prototypes and executable transition rules defined over role instances, together with a skill that guides the actor LLM to use role information in decision making. In a target world, without the teacher, the actor uses this skill together with its current role assignments and parameter estimates, and actively tests a role instance hypothesis through interaction when its uncertainty affects the current decision. Feedback from each action refines role assignments and estimates parameter values online, with no LLM parameter updates and the transition rules held fixed. Experiments on MARS benchmark show that RoleWorld enables robust generalization across environments with significantly altered object behavior, suggesting that functional role abstractions can serve as an effective component for knowledge transfer in world modeling. Project Page: https://future-item.github.io/RoleWorld.
papers.title_zh: RoleWorld：使用功能性角色抽象在世界建模中进行知识迁移
papers.abstract_zh: 世界模型使大语言模型（LLM）智能体能够预测动作效果并做出明智决策。为了实现泛化，期望此类世界模型能够高效迁移到具有相似交互结构和底层动力学的新环境。近期方法将世界动力学编码为符号规则或可执行程序，其组合式结构原则上支持迁移，但仍围绕环境特定对象来组织这些知识。为解决这一局限，我们提出了 RoleWorld，一种符号世界建模方法，它使用可复用原型和环境特定参数值作为功能性角色抽象，来表示对象在交互中的行为方式。从交互轨迹中，教师 LLM 提取角色原型以及定义在角色实例上的可执行转移规则，还提取一项指导行动者 LLM 在决策中使用角色信息的技能。在目标世界中，没有教师时，行动者使用该技能及其当前角色分配和参数估计，并在其不确定性影响当前决策时，通过交互主动检验角色实例假设。每次动作的反馈都会在线细化角色分配并估计参数值，且不更新 LLM 参数并保持转移规则固定。在 MARS 基准上的实验表明，RoleWorld 能够在对象行为发生显著改变的环境中实现稳健泛化，这表明功能性角色抽象可以作为世界建模中知识迁移的有效组成部分。项目页面：https://future-item.github.io/RoleWorld.

papers.title: AdaC-GRPO: Towards Mastering Long-Horizon Visual Sudoku Puzzles via Adaptive Curriculum Learning
papers.summary: While reinforcement learning with verifiable reward (RLVR) enhances reasoning in large language models, its efficacy in long-horizon multimodal tasks remains underexplored. Visual Sudoku puzzles pose a representative challenge, requiring multi-step deductive reasoning over both local constraints and global dependency chains. To this end, we introduce FG-Sudoku, a fine-grained benchmark categorized by grid size and required deductive steps. Evaluations reveal that frontier MLLMs fail on complex long-range dependencies (e.g., 9*9 puzzles). During post-training, this near-zero success rate causes severe reward sparsity, halting standard RLVR. We propose Adaptive Curriculum Group Relative Policy Optimization (AdaC-GRPO) to overcome this. Unlike rigid or prior-based schedules, AdaC-GRPO dynamically constructs training batches by tracking the model's "Zone of Proximal Development" via online rollout accuracy. Experiments demonstrate that AdaC-GRPO enables Qwen2.5-VL-7B to approach the performance of Gemini-2.5-Flash while bridging 62.2% of the overall accuracy gap to Gemini-2.5-Pro, with its generalizability further validated across InternVL-3.5 and Qwen3-VL.
papers.title_zh: AdaC-GRPO：通过自适应课程学习迈向掌握长时程视觉数独谜题
papers.abstract_zh: 尽管具有可验证奖励的强化学习（RLVR）增强了大语言模型的推理能力，但其在长时程多模态任务中的有效性仍未得到充分探索。视觉数独谜题构成了一项具有代表性的挑战，要求对局部约束和全局依赖链进行多步演绎推理。为此，我们引入了 FG-Sudoku，一个按网格大小和所需演绎步数分类的细粒度基准。评估表明，前沿多模态大语言模型（MLLM）在复杂的长程依赖关系上失败（例如，9*9 数独谜题）。在后训练期间，这种接近零的成功率导致严重的奖励稀疏性，使标准 RLVR 无法进行。我们提出了自适应课程组相对策略优化（AdaC-GRPO）来克服这一问题。与僵化的或基于先验的调度不同，AdaC-GRPO 通过在线 rollout 准确率追踪模型的“最近发展区”，动态构建训练批次。实验表明，AdaC-GRPO 使 Qwen2.5-VL-7B 能够接近 Gemini-2.5-Flash 的性能，同时弥补了其与 Gemini-2.5-Pro 之间总体准确率差距的 62.2%，其泛化能力还在 InternVL-3.5 和 Qwen3-VL 上得到进一步验证。

papers.title: JANUS: Enhancing Long-Horizon Autonomous Research with Co-Evolving World Models
papers.summary: Long-horizon autonomous research has shown promise in accelerating scientific progress through sustained cycles of hypothesis generation, implementation, and validation. However, this Generate-Execute-Feedback paradigm relies on reactive trial-and-error, where costly and time-consuming executions introduce severe feedback delays, throttling evolutionary progress under explosively expanding search space. To address this challenge, we propose JANUS, a framework that unifies future outcomes forecasting and past experience reflection through a Predict-Verify-Evolve loop driven by a co-evolving world model. Within an evolving graph, the research agent proposes candidates while world model scores them by forecasting value improvement, information gain, and exploration utility, then accordingly selects, refines, or prunes branches prior to execution. After receiving ground-truth feedback, JANUS distills experience into evolving skills: hierarchical skills for research agent, exploration-strategy skills for world model, and their coordination protocols. This mechanism enables continual co-evolution: the research agent sharpens candidate generation while the world model refines its predictive judgment over extended horizons. Extensive evaluations on MLS-Bench-Lite and real research tasks demonstrate that JANUS significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving both higher evolving efficiency and ceiling.

papers.title: Forgetting is Not Always Bad: A Neuro-Inspired Memory Repair Mechanism for Poisoned LLM Agents
papers.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents are highly vulnerable to memory-poisoning attacks. Existing defenses primarily rely on external modules for either static memory isolation or continuous online auditing, resulting in low memory efficiency and high computational overhead. To address these limitations, inspired by neuroscientific mechanisms that weak reactivation can destabilize memories and induce decay in the absence of reinforcement, we propose an agent-intrinsic training-free memory repair framework, DREAM (Dynamic Reactivation for Engram Attenuation in Memory), that enables selective functional forgetting of poisoned memories. Specifically, DREAM implements a three-stage pipeline: perturbation-induced implicit reactivation to reveal the structural fragility of malicious memories, adaptive anomaly diagnosis based on multi-dimensional activation patterns to detect topological anomalies, and a dynamic memory repair module that selectively suppresses harmful memories while reinforcing benign ones. Extensive experiments across diverse attackers and real-world tasks demonstrate that DREAM reduces attack success rates by over 95\% against backdoor poisoning while preserving strong benign utility. DREAM also achieves competitive robustness against injection attacks. In terms of runtime and token consumption, DREAM achieves up to a 2.13$\times$ speedup and a 37.7\% reduction in token consumption compared with A-MemGuard. Furthermore, DREAM also achieves a task success rate of 92.96\% on poisoned multi-agent systems.
papers.title_zh: 遗忘并不总是坏事：一种面向被投毒 LLM 智能体的神经启发式记忆修复机制
papers.abstract_zh: 大型语言模型（LLM）智能体极易受到记忆投毒攻击。现有防御主要依赖外部模块进行静态记忆隔离或持续在线审计，导致记忆效率低和计算开销高。为了解决这些局限性，受神经科学机制启发——弱再激活可在缺乏强化的情况下使记忆不稳定并诱导其衰退——我们提出了一种智能体内在的免训练记忆修复框架 DREAM（Dynamic Reactivation for Engram Attenuation in Memory），其能够实现对被投毒记忆的选择性功能性遗忘。具体而言，DREAM 实现了一个三阶段流程：扰动诱导的隐式再激活，以揭示恶意记忆的结构脆弱性；基于多维激活模式的自适应异常诊断，以检测拓扑异常；以及一个动态记忆修复模块，其选择性抑制有害记忆，同时强化良性记忆。在多种攻击者和真实世界任务上的大量实验表明，DREAM 在抵御后门投毒时可将攻击成功率降低超过 95\%，同时保持强大的良性效用。DREAM 还针对注入攻击实现了有竞争力的鲁棒性。在运行时间和 token 消耗方面，与 A-MemGuard 相比，DREAM 实现了高达 2.13$\times$ 的加速以及 37.7\% 的 token 消耗减少。此外，DREAM 在被投毒的多智能体系统上还实现了 92.96\% 的任务成功率。

papers.title: BoundaryEvo: Data-Model Co-Evolution at the Capability Boundary for Long-Chain Reasoning Distillation
papers.summary: Distilling long-chain reasoning trajectories from large teacher models provides an effective way to improve the reasoning ability of small language models. However, existing methods typically select a fixed training set before distillation, overlooking that the usefulness of a reasoning example changes as the student evolves. This mismatch becomes especially costly when only a small number of teacher trajectories can be used for training. Besides, examples already mastered provide little new supervision, while examples far beyond the capability of student may be difficult to learn from. Training data should therefore adapt as model capability evolves, yet reliable data selection is difficult when the student is initially weak. To address these challenges, our key idea is to first establish the basic reasoning capability and then adapt the training data to the evolving capability boundary of the student. We propose BoundaryEvo, a two-stage data--model co-evolution framework. In Capability Priming, we directly distill a small set of teacher-generated long reasoning trajectories without using a separate model to judge and filter them, allowing the student to acquire an initial reasoning capability before capability-aware data selection. In Capability-Boundary Co-Evolution, we repeatedly select questions that the current student has not mastered but the expert can reliably solve, and update the training data as the student evolves. With only 1,000 training examples, BoundaryEvo consistently outperforms static and dynamic data selection baselines across 11 reasoning benchmarks, raising the original Qwen3.5-4B accuracy from 62.9 to 75.3 on IMO-AnswerBench and from 26.8 to 46.0 on AMO-Bench. The code and data will be made publicly available.

papers.title: Masked Diffusion Language Agents for Tool-Integrated Chemical Reasoning
papers.summary: Designing tool-integrated reasoning agent systems for complex chemical tasks remains a fundamental challenge. Although recent chemical agents have demonstrated promising performance through the integration of external tools, they are still built on the autoregressive paradigm, which is inherently constrained by causal attention and left-to-right generation. As a result, they often struggle with bidirectional molecular understanding, global coordinated tool planning and multi-source evidence integration. To address this challenge, we introduce ChemDiffAgent, the first masked diffusion language agent for tool-integrated chemical reasoning. It reformulates chemical reasoning as iterative denoising over interleaved reasoning and tool-use trajectories, enabling tool-use decisions to be jointly determined under full-trajectory context and thereby better aligning the agent's decision boundary with its knowledge boundary. We further analyze how this paradigm benefits agentic reasoning through harder infilling subproblems during training and flexible arbitrary-order decoding during inference. Then we develop a two-stage post-training framework, comprising agentic supervised fine-tuning and variance-reduced preference optimization, to enhance tool-use and reasoning capabilities. We also construct a comprehensive benchmark covering six chemistry tasks across both single-turn and multi-turn tool-use scenarios. Under matched budgets and evaluation, ChemDiffAgent consistently outperforms autoregressive agents, achieving an overall improvement of approximately 20%. Notably, our 8B model achieves performance comparable to, in some cases surpassing, significantly larger frontier models, such as GPT 5.5 and Claude Opus 4.7. Code is available at https://github.com/bilemond/ChemDiffAgent.
papers.title_zh: 面向工具集成化学推理的掩码扩散语言智能体
papers.abstract_zh: 为复杂化学任务设计工具集成的推理智能体系统仍然是一项根本性挑战。尽管近期的化学智能体通过集成外部工具展现出了有前景的性能，但它们仍然构建于自回归范式之上，而该范式本质上受限于因果注意力和从左到右的生成。因此，它们往往难以应对双向分子理解、全局协同的工具规划以及多源证据整合。为应对这一挑战，我们提出 ChemDiffAgent，这是首个用于工具集成化学推理的掩码扩散语言智能体。它将化学推理重新表述为对交错进行的推理与工具使用轨迹进行迭代去噪，使得工具使用决策能够在全轨迹上下文下被联合确定，从而更好地使智能体的决策边界与其知识边界对齐。我们进一步分析了这一范式如何通过训练期间更困难的填充子问题以及推理期间灵活的任意顺序解码来有益于智能体式推理。接着，我们开发了一个两阶段后训练框架，包括智能体式监督微调和方差缩减的偏好优化，以增强工具使用和推理能力。我们还构建了一个全面的基准，涵盖单轮和多轮工具使用场景下的六项化学任务。在匹配的预算和评估下，ChemDiffAgent 持续优于自回归智能体，取得了约 20% 的总体提升。值得注意的是，我们的 8B 模型达到了与显著更大的前沿模型（如 GPT 5.5 和 Claude Opus 4.7）相当的性能，在某些情况下甚至超越了它们。代码可在 https://github.com/bilemond/ChemDiffAgent 获取。

papers.title: AlphaNIST: Emergent Assembly Skills from Binary Task Rewards
papers.summary: The NIST Assembly Task Board #1 remains a challenging benchmark for learning-based methods in robotic manipulation. Over short horizons, it demands precise, contact-rich control of small, tight-fitting parts. Over long horizons, it requires recovery and coordination across extended action sequences. Demonstrations, task decomposition, and dense progress rewards have enabled research advances by providing guidance on how to assemble. But how much of the strategy must be specified? The progression from AlphaGo to AlphaGo Zero showed that RL at scale can discover superhuman strategies without prescribing how to win. AlphaNIST asks whether a sparse binary task reward and task diversity admitted by this task-agnostic reward can similarly let a robot discover how to assemble. In simulation, we train a single policy from scratch across all 20 assembly tasks on the NIST Assembly Task Board #1, reaching 98.2% overall training success without demonstrations, progress shaping, scripted primitives, or per-task tuning. The framework also trains policies to complete ten assembly pairs in a single episode without a prescribed order, with task success rewarded only when all ten pairs are simultaneously complete. The learned policies discover dexterous and planning-like behaviors: choosing grasps for later assembly, using surrounding geometry to reorient parts, and preparing one part, assembling another, then returning to finish the first without an explicit planner. For videos, see our website: https://alpha-nist.github.io/

papers.title: SWE-Critix: Post-Training Generalist Verifiers for Assessing Coding-Agent Trajectories
papers.summary: Coding agents are increasingly deployed for end-to-end software engineering tasks, where a readily available oracle evaluator that defines the success criteria is often absent. This motivates verifications for coding agents that can reliably judge and explain their behavior. However, verification is non-trivial as coding agents are increasingly capable of solving long-horizon software engineering tasks. Their execution trajectories can be extremely long, containing hundreds of iterative interactions with code repositories and external tools. Existing verifiers either rely on general-purpose LLMs without specialized training or train dedicated critics that predominantly focus on producing scalar rewards, highlighting the relatively limited exploration of training-based generalist verification. We introduce SWE-Critix, a post-training pipeline for training generalist verifiers of coding-agent trajectories. Given a task and its execution trajectory, the learned verifier predicts the completion label and generates a natural-language analysis that explains its judgment. Our pipeline combines supervised fine-tuning (SFT) with reinforcement learning (RL) and trains a series of 30B models on trajectories from CodeForge-Preview. On a held-out test set, SWE-Critix improves classification accuracy from 57% for the base Qwen3-30B-A3B reasoning model to 66% after SFT and 78% after RL. We release our models, datasets, and training code to facilitate further research.

papers.title: RegulaTutor: A Theory-Informed Framework for Long-Term Personalized Learning
papers.summary: Long-term personalized tutoring requires language models to translate a learner's evolving history into appropriate instructional support. Existing LLM-based tutoring systems use memory and retrieval to personalize responses, but the pedagogical rationale linking historical evidence to teaching strategies is not always explicit. We introduce RegulaTutor, a theory-informed framework for long-term personalized tutoring that connects historical evidence, learner interpretation, and learner-facing instruction. Guided by self-regulated learning (SRL) research, its tutoring harness operationalizes a cognitive, affective, metacognitive, and motivational (CAMM) framework for deriving evidence-supported learner interpretations and teaching policies. The resulting policies retain links to their supporting evidence and are updated as new observations arrive. This staged workflow also supports systematic refinement through PairRoute, an offline procedure that uses intermediate execution records to distinguish harness, model, and mixed failures. PairRoute proposes and evaluates targeted harness revisions, then constructs reviewed stage-level supervision for confirmed model failures remaining under the selected harness. We focus this refinement on historical evidence acquisition, which underpins personalized instruction and allows outputs to be checked against learning records and reference answers. RegulaTutor improves historical-evidence accuracy, learner diagnosis, and judged teaching quality on average across evaluated model configurations. PairRoute results show an endpoint improvement in standalone-model historical-evidence accuracy over the refinement trajectory. Together, these results highlight RegulaTutor's potential to support lifelong personalized education through instructional policies that evolve with learner histories and targeted improvements to the tutoring system.

papers.title: Web$hell: A Unified Interface for Agentic Web Access
papers.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents are becoming direct users of the open web. As they take on increasingly complex and information-intensive tasks, effective web access is becoming a core capability for agentic problem solving. Existing approaches have advanced agentic web access through different access models, including search-augmented agents, browser-based agents, and, more recently, filesystem-based agents. Nevertheless, as users expect agents to complete long-horizon, end-to-end tasks, they increasingly need to conduct broad information gathering, perform browser actions, and revisit acquired evidence within a single trajectory. Yet our preliminary analyses reveal that existing access models struggle to meet these demands. They primarily support either information gathering or browser interaction, while combining their capabilities can involve substantial costs or performance trade-offs. To this end, we present Web\$hell, an interface that unifies web access under a single access model. Using a common schema defined by WebContract, WebCompiler compiles live webpages into addressable information and action objects. These objects are maintained in WebCache and handled through a shared set of operations, providing agents with consistent, operable, and persistent web access. Through extensive experiments across web search, web navigation, and deep research benchmarks, we show that Web\$hell achieves strong task performance at lower cost. Our results further indicate the importance of interface design for effective web access, with Web\$hell opening new possibilities for more capable and efficient LLM agents on the web.
papers.title_zh: Web$hell：面向智能体网页访问的统一接口
papers.abstract_zh: 大型语言模型（LLM）智能体正在成为开放网络的直接用户。随着它们承担日益复杂且信息密集的任务，有效的网页访问正成为智能体问题求解的核心能力。现有方法已经通过不同的访问模型推进了智能体网页访问，包括搜索增强型智能体、基于浏览器的智能体，以及最近出现的基于文件系统的智能体。然而，随着用户期望智能体完成长时程、端到端任务，它们越来越需要在单一轨迹内进行广泛的信息收集、执行浏览器操作，并重新访问已获取的证据。然而，我们的初步分析揭示，现有访问模型难以满足这些需求。它们主要支持信息收集或浏览器交互中的一种，而将其能力结合起来可能涉及显著成本或性能权衡。为此，我们提出 Web\$hell，一个在单一访问模型下统一网页访问的接口。使用由 WebContract 定义的通用模式，WebCompiler 将实时网页编译为可寻址的信息和动作对象。这些对象维护在 WebCache 中，并通过一组共享操作进行处理，为智能体提供一致、可操作且持久的网页访问。通过在网页搜索、网页导航和深度研究基准上的大量实验，我们表明 Web\$hell 以更低成本实现了强劲的任务性能。我们的结果进一步表明接口设计对于有效网页访问的重要性，Web\$hell 为网络上更强大、更高效的 LLM 智能体开辟了新的可能性。

papers.title: Local Diagnostics of Learned Event Representations for Anomaly Detection at the HL-LHC
papers.summary: Anomaly detection, the identification of collision events that deviate from Standard Model expectations, is one of the most promising model-agnostic strategies for new-physics searches at the Large Hadron Collider. Searching for rare events in learned low-dimensional representations removes the need to commit to hand-crafted observables a priori, but sacrifices the immediate physical interpretation those observables provide. For anomaly detection to enter a discovery pipeline, flagged events must therefore be diagnosed locally, both to distinguish potential new physics from mismodeling or detector effects and to identify observables for targeted follow-up searches. We evaluate supervised and self-supervised neural embedding strategies on COLLIDE-2V, a 750-million-event dataset simulated under realistic High-Luminosity LHC conditions, using the reconstruction error of an autoencoder trained in the learned latent space as the anomaly score. Across the configurations and benchmark signals considered, supervised objectives, which exploit simulation process labels during training, generally outperform their self-supervised counterparts and, in their best configurations, improve on an autoencoder trained directly on kinematic features, raising the signal efficiency at 10% background acceptance on all held-out processes. We further introduce a local diagnostic pipeline that fits a Gaussian Mixture Model to the SM latent space, profiles each component through high-level observables without process labels, localizes the flagged events, and ranks observables by their local discriminating power. The ranking recovers the defining kinematics of the held-out processes, while correlating the anomaly score with the same observables quantifies how closely the score tracks them, revealing cases where the most discriminating observable is not the one the score follows most closely.

papers.title: Rollout-Time Intervention: Unlocking Agentic Reinforcement Learning Beyond Policy Limits
papers.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a key paradigm for improving large language model (LLM) agents, enabling stronger reasoning, planning, and tool-use in interactive environments. However, existing agent RL methods remain fundamentally constrained by an on-policy reasoning bottleneck: when tasks exceed the model's current capability boundary, effective trajectories become extremely sparse and training often collapses. We introduce Rollout-Time Intervention (RTI), a technique designed to elicit successful trajectories beyond the policy's intrinsic exploration capacity. RTI operates by leveraging reward-side evidence (i.e., evaluation rubrics) during rollout to convert erroneous trajectories into successful ones, providing effective learning signals for tasks that the policy rarely solves on its own. Although intervention trajectories are inherently off-policy, we find that they can effectively guide policy optimization when trajectories with excessive distributional shifts are filtered out. Extensive experiments across five benchmarks demonstrate that RTI consistently outperforms RL baselines, enabling the post-trained policy to approach the performance of substantially stronger contemporary LLMs and, more importantly, transcend its original capability boundary. The code is available at https://github.com/Alibaba-NLP/qqr.
papers.title_zh: Rollout 时干预：解锁超越策略极限的智能体强化学习
papers.abstract_zh: 强化学习（RL）已成为改进大语言模型（LLM）智能体的关键范式，使其能在交互环境中实现更强的推理、规划和工具使用。然而，现有的智能体 RL 方法仍然从根本上受限于同策略（on-policy）推理瓶颈：当任务超出模型当前能力边界时，有效轨迹变得极其稀疏，训练常常崩溃。我们提出 Rollout 时干预（Rollout-Time Intervention, RTI），这是一种旨在激发超出策略内在探索能力的成功轨迹的技术。RTI 通过在 rollout 期间利用奖励侧证据（即评估评分标准）来将错误轨迹转化为成功轨迹，从而为策略自身很少能解决的任务提供有效的学习信号。尽管干预轨迹本质上是异策略（off-policy）的，但我们发现，当过滤掉分布偏移过大的轨迹后，它们可以有效指导策略优化。在五个基准上的大量实验表明，RTI 始终优于 RL 基线，使后训练后的策略接近明显更强的当代 LLM 的性能，更重要的是，超越其原始能力边界。代码可在 https://github.com/Alibaba-NLP/qqr 获取。

papers.title: Agentic Large Language Models
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have taken the world by storm. Their ability to communicate with us in our own language, and to reason about our world, has made them a favorite tool for writing, answering questions, and much more. Their answers already influence our decisions and our actions. What would happen if LLMs themselves could act in the world directly? What would happen if LLMs could interact with each other? Agentic LLMs combine the power of large language models with the ability to act in the real world. In this book we will discuss how agentic LLMs work, how they act, how they interact, and what this means for us, as users.
papers.title_zh: 智能体大语言模型
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型（LLMs）已经风靡全球。它们能够用我们自己的语言与我们交流，并对我们的世界进行推理，这使它们成为写作、回答问题以及更多任务中备受青睐的工具。它们的回答已经在影响我们的决策和我们的行动。如果大语言模型本身能够直接在世界中行动，会发生什么？如果大语言模型能够相互交互，会发生什么？智能体大语言模型将大语言模型的能力与在现实世界中行动的能力结合在一起。在本书中，我们将讨论智能体大语言模型如何工作、如何行动、如何交互，以及这对我们作为用户意味着什么。

papers.title: SqueezeBench: Saturation-Resilient Evaluation of Mathematical Capability
papers.summary: AI systems are making rapid progress in mathematics, but this progress is hard to measure. Benchmarks of solved problems saturate, and in benchmarks of open problems each problem can be resolved for the first time only once. We present SqueezeBench, a benchmark that is resilient to saturation: a success raises the bar instead of removing the problem. Each problem fixes an integer function $f(n)$ whose values are known only for small $n$, and the benchmark keeps a lower and an upper record on it. A record is a computable Lean function with a machine-checked proof that it bounds $f$. A submission proposes a new function and proves that it bounds $f$, that it is no worse than the current record at any $n$, and that it is strictly better at some $n$. Once accepted, it becomes the record that the next submission has to beat. The system thus chooses the bound as well as its proof, and it may improve the record at a single $n$ or its growth rate. At every $n$, the gap between the two records shows how far the certified bounds are from determining $f(n)$. Every proof is checked by two independent Lean kernels, so no referee needs to check the mathematics. The checks also reject a function that computes $f$ by exhaustive search at small $n$, and a maintainer only reads the submitter's report and looks for such a search at larger $n$. We release ten problems from extremal combinatorics with twenty proved initial records and the admission tools. As a baseline, agents based on a frontier language model, with at most one hour per record, had 82 submissions accepted and improved every record, without going beyond the published literature. Agents based on two newer models then started from these records, had 60 more submissions accepted and improved 19 of the 20 records again. For eight of the ten problems, at least one record is still asymptotically behind the best published bound.

papers.title: A Local Agentic AI Framework to Generate Edge Case Scenarios for Safety Assurance
papers.summary: Generating edge case scenarios is crucial for training, testing and safety assuring autonomous systems. This identifies hazardous failures to increase system reliability and robustness, ensures the system can still function safely on the boundaries of its operational design domain and learns the expected system behaviour for these edge cases. The rapid advancement in the generation and analysis capabilities of language models (LMs) has expanded their applicability and recent work has investigated LM scenario generation. However, many recent approaches rely on human-in-the-loop or rule-based strategies. This restricts the LM's ability to generate diverse and edge case scenarios; the long tail of the distribution. Our work uses local LMs in a laptop-based agentic AI framework for adaptive scenario generation. This is cheap, fully-controlled, ensures data privacy and security. It uses think, act, observe, update, and continue loops with lightweight JSON encoding to generate scenarios. We use the system requirements, system description and environment description as knowledge bases in contextual prompts for an LM to ensure scenario realism. A second, independent LM critiques each scenario using domain specific criteria so it can be refined. The refined scenarios are run in simulation and evaluation metrics collected. These metric scores are analysed and similar scenarios are created for edge cases (exploitation) or novel scenarios are generated to explore the scenario space. Post-hoc clustering using metric scores and thematic-type analysis of the rich-text scenario descriptions produced by the LM pinpoints functional gaps and their triggering conditions. This creates traceable evidence for the safety assurance case. Our work highlights the potential of a flexible and adaptive local agentic AI framework for automating edge case generation and producing traceable safety assurance evidence.

papers.title: Branching On-Policy Distillation
papers.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) provides teacher supervision on student-generated trajectories, but a single trajectory realizes only one continuation at each decision, limiting supervision coverage under a finite sampling budget. We propose BranchOPD (Branching On-Policy Distillation), which selects informative decision points using student uncertainty and teacher-student disagreement, resamples student-policy continuations from shared prefixes, and applies token-level teacher supervision to both main trajectories and branches. BranchOPD operates at token-level decisions in mathematics and within-turn decisions in agent tasks. Shared-prefix reuse reduces student-generated token costs by approximately 19% on ALFWorld and 31% on WebShop relative to seven independent trajectories. We also introduce protocol-boundary repair (PBR), which uses targeted supervision under protocol constraints to mitigate repetition and wasted generation. BranchOPD outperforms Vanilla OPD and Multi-Rollout OPD (n=7) across all evaluated benchmarks, with gains over Vanilla OPD of 18.55 percentage points in mean mathematics accuracy over 16 sampled answers (avg@16) and 13.8 points in mean ALFWorld ID/OOD success. Mechanistic analyses and selection ablations show that branching at uncertain decisions expands subsequent behavior coverage and outperforms random selection and turn-initial branching.

papers.title: Humanize MLE Agents: Multi-Agent Session Alternation Beyond Single-Agent Limits
papers.summary: Existing LLM-based agent approaches for long-horizon machine learning engineering (MLE) often use context engineering, implemented through custom harnesses that manage tools, skills, and accumulated experience. However, we find that as single-session execution lengthens, the agent's reasoning intensity declines alongside slowing progress, summarized as long-horizon deceleration, and the benefits of these custom harnesses vanish as the underlying model improves, summarized as harness staleness. These findings suggest that their benefits may not persist across versions, which motivates a workflow-level approach in which agents build on one another's work across sessions. We model these alternating agent sessions as a context-reset semi-Markov decision process (CR-SMDP) and establish sufficient conditions for alternation to exceed single-agent reference limits, derive an explicit experiment-budget bound, and characterize when session caps preserve this advantage. Guided by this analysis, we introduce Humanize MLE Agents (HMA), which alternates two agents on a shared workspace, limits each session to at most k experiments and resets the context between sessions, without additional task-specific harness or prior knowledge supplements. Across 75 Kaggle tasks in MLE-bench, HMA reaches a state-of-the-art any-medal rate of 78.2%, exceeding the strongest open-source baseline by 8.0 points with a quarter of its time budget. Moreover, among six configurations spanning five heterogeneous agent pairs, HMA improves any-medal rate over the constituent baselines by 6.4 points on average, demonstrating cross-pair generality. A supplementary case on kernel optimization reaches 878 cycles, within 1.6% of the community leaderboard leader, demonstrating applicability beyond MLE.

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Multimodal Language Model with Heterogeneous Evidence Integration for Clinical Prognosis
papers.summary: Clinical prognosis requires integrating structured measurements, physiological waveforms, longitudinal history, and population context. We introduce PRISM (Population-Retrieved Inference for Structured Multimodal Prognosis), a multimodal language model that combines per-feature numerical tokenization, recency-weighted aggregation of longitudinal ECGs, and a dual-modality population memory bank. Retrieval operates in representation space: the model receives mean-pooled embeddings of similar training-cohort encounters, while no individual retrieved record enters the prompt. On the 1,443-task MDS-ED benchmark, PRISM achieves AUROCs of 86.2% for diagnosis, 93.1% for deterioration, 91.8% for ICU admission, and 92.8% for mortality. These results use a 96-hour pre-arrival window unavailable to reported baselines. With benchmark-window inputs only, PRISM reaches 0.8895 AUROC, compared with 0.8937 for UniPACT and 0.8889 for MDS-ED. A matched-input compact fusion model using the same five evidence streams and frozen encoders reaches 0.7652 AUROC, versus 0.9092 for PRISM. Replacing numerical EHR encoding with text serialization reduces AUROC by 3.66 points; removing pre-arrival history reduces it by 1.97 points; and zeroing retrieval reduces it by 0.99 points. Genuine retrieval outperforms random-neighbor retrieval by 0.97 macro-average points, although a paired task-level sign test does not establish a uniform advantage (p=0.067). On the external MC-MED cohort, supervised fine-tuning reaches 0.8611 AUROC, compared with 0.8227 for locally trained gradient boosting and 0.7841 for source-only PRISM. These results support structure-aware multimodal integration and supervised external adaptation.

papers.title: Causal Effect Identifiability in Causal Abstractions: A Strict Hierarchy of Criteria
papers.summary: Identifying causal effects from observational data typically requires a fully specified causal graph, an assumption that is often unrealistic in complex or high-dimensional settings. Causal abstractions address this limitation by retaining only partial causal information, thereby defining equivalence classes of compatible causal graphs. In this paper, we study causal effect identifiability directly at the level of these graph collections, rather than at the level of individual causal diagrams. We formalize several notions of identifiability in this setting and organize them into a hierarchy that clarifies their relationships and differences. In particular, we establish that a causal effect may be identified over a collection of graphs without admitting a single causal derivation that holds uniformly across all compatible graphs. These results help reveal gaps and clarify ambiguities in the existing literature.

papers.title: Beyond Domain-Routed Supervision: Cross-Teacher Guarding for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
papers.summary: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) extends on-policy distillation (OPD) by routing domain-specific data to specialized teachers, integrating their capabilities through dense token-level supervision on student-generated trajectories. However, domain routing only distinguishes the supervision sources for different domains; updates from all domains still act on shared parameters. When teachers differ substantially in response style and domain expertise, supervision that is effective in isolation may still lead to persistent gradient conflicts and capability degradation during joint optimization. To address this challenge, we propose Cross-Teacher Guarding for MOPD (Road MOPD), which introduces non-routed teachers as auxiliary cross-domain critics on the same student trajectories and coordinates multi-teacher supervision through token-level credit assignment and gradient updates. Specifically, cross-teacher-guided credit assignment uses teacher agreement to strengthen token-level corrections jointly supported by the teachers and attenuate conflicting signals; preventive multi-teacher gradient projection uses auxiliary gradients from the same trajectories to constrain potentially conflicting updates and adaptively controls projection strength to retain target-domain learning signals. In experiments, Road MOPD mitigates degradation in the disadvantaged domain, gains over 5 percentage points under high conflict, and improves overall performance in low-conflict and three-domain settings.

papers.title: MAGMA-Bench: Evaluating Long-Horizon Embodied Agents under Dynamic Tasks and Execution Failures
papers.summary: Long-horizon embodied agents must maintain task-relevant information, coordinate heterogeneous robots, and adapt their decisions as execution unfolds. Existing benchmarks investigate dynamic task execution and embodied multi-agent coordination, but provide limited evaluation of their intersection. We introduce MAGMA-Bench, an architecture-agnostic benchmark for persistent task reasoning in dynamic multi-robot environments. MAGMA-Bench evaluates agents across increasing task horizons and controlled online perturbations, including execution failures, task interruptions, and mission updates, with scenarios requiring coordination across robots with heterogeneous capabilities. It uses a structured skill-level interface to separate task-level reasoning from perception and low-level control. We evaluate locally deployable open-weight planners, multi-agent state-tracking strategies, and frontier models. Even the strongest evaluated models fail on a substantial fraction of clean episodes, and their success rates decrease further under online perturbations. Supervised adaptation greatly improves a small model, but performance remains substantially lower on longer and multi-robot missions. We release the benchmark, 261,646 task-level training examples, and an architecture-agnostic expert-trace generation pipeline.

papers.title: Constructing Pareto Frontiers of Optimal Reasoning Termination Methods for Overthinking in Reasoning Models
papers.summary: Reasoning models can benefit from test-time scaling, but continued reasoning may become ineffective or harmful, a phenomenon termed overthinking. Evaluations against full thinking compare accuracy and token usage but lack references for overthinking severity and strategies' theoretical mitigation potential. To characterize overthinking at the model-task level, we first introduce Step-wise Truncation Probing (STP), repeatedly generating answers from multiple retained prefixes along each fixed sampled reasoning trajectory. Using each trajectory's earliest measured position attaining maximum empirical accuracy as a reference, we define Overthinking Ratio and Accuracy Degradation as the fraction of thinking tokens generated afterward and the accuracy decrease from this reference to full thinking, respectively. Secondly, we then formulate dynamic routing, fixed budgets, and dynamic early exit within a unified framework to quantify the theoretical mitigation potential of different termination strategies. Based on this unified framework, we use the complete STP measurements to construct a token-accuracy Pareto frontier for each strategy under a common normalized thinking-token budget. We further develop OTBench, a reusable benchmark built from the STP process, which produced 70.5B reasoning tokens and the corresponding probing measurements across six models and four benchmark groups.

papers.title: MENTOR: Learning from Failure with On-Policy Pedagogical Intervention
papers.summary: Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) is a key driver for Large Reasoning Models, but it is vulnerable to "zero-reward collapse", a training failure where a sudden increase in task difficulty causes the learning signal to vanish. We argue that the conventional approach of discarding these failed trajectories is wasteful, as they contain valuable diagnostic information about the model's cognitive gaps, a bright side that can be leveraged for recovery. Existing solutions, however, often regress to static, "off-policy-style" interventions like pre-defined hint libraries or perform post-hoc refinement, failing to provide the adaptive, forward-looking guidance needed to escape the collapse. To address this, we propose a paradigm shift towards on-policy pedagogical intervention and introduce MENTOR, a multi-agent framework that acts as a live mentor. MENTOR diagnoses the root cause of failure in real-time and dynamically generates targeted, instructional prompts to guide the learning agent's next attempt. As a plug-and-play module, MENTOR integrates seamlessly into existing policy optimization pipelines like GRPO without modifying the training infrastructure. Extensive experiments on math and code generation show that MENTOR effectively mitigates zero-reward collapse, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines. Notably, it achieves massive average relative gains of up to 78.3% on Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct over its base model.

papers.title: Humanize Olympiad Agents: A Multi-Session Workflow for Olympiad Problem Solving with Solve, Review, Wiki, Verify
papers.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents are rapidly improving on long-horizon scientific and olympiad tasks. Recent systems have produced a Lean-formalized resolution of the Navier--Stokes problem and autonomous solutions to four open questions in the Erdős Conjectures database. Yet neither system releases both its underlying model and complete inference stack. More broadly, a single agent session remains brittle on difficult problems: early errors can propagate, missing domain knowledge can stall progress, and apparent success can mask a misinterpretation or weakening of the original task. We introduce HOA (Humanize Olympiads Agent), an open, flow-level framework that coordinates multiple agent sessions through three complementary feedback channels. First, an independent reviewer evaluates each candidate and provides actionable feedback. Second, a structured wiki supplies task-specific knowledge that may be missing or unreliable in model pretraining. Third, a verifier checks generated Lean proofs against trusted challenge statements. With GPT-5.6 Sol, HOA achieves perfect scores on the IMO, IPhO, and IOI 2026, near-full marks on the IChO 2026 problem set, and solves all 672 problems (100%) on PutnamBench. On the Lean-Eval leaderboard, HOA ranks first, solving 251 of 304 problems (82.6%). We further evaluate HOA with open models. Using Kimi-K3, HOA achieves full scores on the IMO, IPhO, and IOI, and a gold-level score of 97.1% on the IChO. These results closely match the closed-source GPT-5.6 Sol + /Goal baseline on the IMO and IPhO, while exceeding it on the IChO and IOI, demonstrating that systematic feedback can help bridge substantial differences in base-model capability.
papers.title_zh: 拟人化奥林匹克竞赛智能体：一种用于奥林匹克问题求解、包含求解、评审、Wiki 与验证的多会话工作流
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型（LLM）智能体在长时程科学与奥林匹克竞赛任务上正在迅速进步。近期的系统已经给出了 Navier--Stokes 问题的 Lean 形式化解答，并自主解决了 Erdős 猜想数据库中的四个开放问题。然而，这两个系统都没有同时公开发布其底层模型和完整的推理栈。更广泛地说，单一智能体会话在面对困难问题时仍然十分脆弱：早期错误会传播扩散，领域知识的缺失会使进展停滞，而表面上的成功可能掩盖对原始任务的误解或弱化。我们提出 HOA（Humanize Olympiads Agent），一个开放的、流程级框架，它通过三条互补的反馈通道来协调多个智能体会话。首先，一名独立的评审者评估每个候选解答并给出可操作的反馈。其次，一个结构化的 wiki 提供任务特定的知识，这些知识在模型预训练中可能缺失或不可靠。第三，一个验证器将生成的 Lean 证明与可信的赛题陈述进行核对。在使用 GPT-5.6 Sol 时，HOA 在 IMO、IPhO 和 IOI 2026 上取得满分，在 IChO 2026 题集上取得接近满分的成绩，并在 PutnamBench 上解决了全部 672 道问题（100%）。在 Lean-Eval 排行榜上，HOA 排名第一，解决了 304 道问题中的 251 道（82.6%）。我们进一步使用开放模型评估 HOA。使用 Kimi-K3 时，HOA 在 IMO、IPhO 和 IOI 上取得满分，并在 IChO 上取得 97.1% 的金牌级分数。这些结果在 IMO 和 IPhO 上与闭源的 GPT-5.6 Sol + /Goal 基线十分接近，同时在 IChO 和 IOI 上超过该基线，表明系统性反馈有助于弥合基础模型能力上的显著差异。

papers.title: Learning Size Independent Constraint Models from Input Data and Positive and Negative Example Solutions
papers.summary: In this paper we describe a Constraint Acquisition Tool that generates size independent constraint programs from input data and positive and negative example solutions of multiple problem instances. The system finds size specific models based on typical constraint patterns over global and binary constraints, then generalizes the models to a size independent model that can be run on unseen input data. The system produces MiniZinc code as well as a textual description of the model. We evaluate the tool on the example problems of the PTHG21 Challenge and show the feasibility of the approach.

papers.title: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Automated Tuning of Specialized Neural Network Models
papers.summary: Many machine learning approaches are two-level: an expert selects a class of methods, within this class the choice of key components is critical and usually manual. This paper addresses the automatic tuning of these components and proposes a framework transferable across models of different nature. The multi-agent large language model (LLM) framework has three roles---analyst, coder, and recorder~---with an experiment log and a sandboxed execution environment. Unlike systems that optimize the entire ML script or search architectures in a discrete space, the framework operates over an open but semantically narrow space: the agent generates code only for the specified components, leaving the overall network structure unchanged. The approach is validated in two directions: tuning a classification spiking neural network with correlation learning, and solving high-order differential equations with Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN). Across five tasks---spiking classification on MNIST and Digits, and boundary-value problems for the generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equation (GNLSE) and Kuramoto--Sivashinsky (KS) equations---the agent outperforms the baselines: classification accuracy is 13 percentage points (MNIST) and 6 percentage points (Digits) higher; the error against the analytical single-soliton solution is reduced approximately 2491-fold; the invariant-preservation error drops approximately 325-fold in the selected GNLSE run with a Gaussian perturbation and by more than 100-fold on average over repeated initializations; and the mass drift drops 14-fold for the KS problem with a Gaussian perturbation. The framework thus tunes key components on tasks of different nature without changing its internal structure.
papers.title_zh: 一种用于专用神经网络模型自动调优的多智能体 LLM 系统
papers.abstract_zh: 许多机器学习方法具有两个层级：专家选择一类方法，而在该类方法内部，关键组件的选择至关重要且通常需要人工完成。本文研究这些组件的自动调优，并提出一个可跨不同性质模型迁移的框架。该多智能体大语言模型（LLM）框架具有三个角色——分析者、编码者和记录者——并配有实验日志和沙箱化执行环境。与优化整个机器学习脚本或在离散空间中搜索架构的系统不同，该框架在一个开放但语义狭窄的空间上运行：智能体仅为指定组件生成代码，保持整体网络结构不变。该方法在两个方向得到验证：调优一个采用相关学习的分类脉冲神经网络，以及使用物理信息神经网络（PINN）求解高阶微分方程。在五个任务——MNIST 和 Digits 上的脉冲分类，以及广义非线性薛定谔方程（GNLSE）和 Kuramoto--Sivashinsky（KS）方程的边值问题——上，该智能体优于基线：分类准确率分别高出 13 个百分点（MNIST）和 6 个百分点（Digits）；相对于解析单孤子解的误差约降低 2491 倍；在选定的带有高斯扰动的 GNLSE 运行中，不变量保持误差约下降 325 倍，并且在重复初始化上平均下降超过 100 倍；对于带有高斯扰动的 KS 问题，质量漂移下降 14 倍。因此，该框架在不改变其内部结构的情况下，对不同性质任务中的关键组件进行调优。

papers.title: A Step Harder, Not a Step Too Far: The Benefits and Limits of Curriculum Difficulty Progression in GRPO
papers.summary: Curriculum learning typically organizes training samples from easy to hard. In GRPO, medium-difficulty samples are attractive for online selection because they are more likely to yield informative group-relative learning signals, and prioritizing them can improve training efficiency. However, it remains unclear whether persistently selecting such samples also leads to the strongest final model performance, or whether training can benefit from progressing toward harder samples. Meanwhile, sample difficulty changes as the policy evolves, so fixed difficulty estimates can become misaligned with the current policy. We therefore re-estimate sample difficulty under the current policy and, inspired by the easy-to-hard principle of curriculum learning, design and evaluate a staged curriculum that progressively shifts the active difficulty band toward harder samples. Experiments on GSM8K show that persistent medium-difficulty selection does not achieve the strongest observed performance. Across three random seeds, progressing to a moderately harder difficulty band improves test accuracy to $0.6591 \pm 0.0077$, compared with $0.6449 \pm 0.0024$ for the fixed-medium curriculum. However, further progression to a harder difficulty band reduces accuracy to $0.6405 \pm 0.0053$. These results show that staged difficulty progression can outperform persistent medium-difficulty selection, but its benefit is non-monotonic. Effective GRPO curricula can therefore benefit from progressing beyond medium difficulty, while avoiding excessive progression toward overly difficult samples.}

papers.title: A Baseline Assessment for the Agentic Web Technology Stack
papers.summary: The fast pace in which protocols, frameworks, and technologies are being proposed for LLM-based agents results in a complex scenario for anyone aiming to create state-of-the-art AI solutions. Without an assessment on how different protocols, frameworks, and libraries work together to compose an Agentic Web solution, developers and organizations face different challenges (e.g., skilling, governance, infrastructure) even before becoming part of the Agentic Web ecosystem. In this context, we propose a system for performing Agentic Web evaluations called MASTIF (Multi-Agent System TestIng Framework) and present a baseline assessment of Agentic Web technologies, including 3 LLMs, 3 protocols, and 4 agent implementation frameworks, against 300 Mind2Web benchmark tasks. Results suggest that selecting a task-specific technology stack may result in gains of task completion rate, efficiency score, and social value stability scores; and reductions in verbosity and time to complete tasks. With the presented results, we expect to present a baseline in terms of metrics and results for this complex and fast evolving scenario for those aiming at designing, assessing, and developing multi-agent systems.

papers.title: Adaptive DHiSparse: Speculative Decoding over a Load-Adaptive KV Hierarchy
papers.summary: Long-context serving runs out of KV memory before the hardware reaches its useful throughput. HiSparse stores history in host memory and fetches only the selected entries, but it uses one cache budget at every load and does not handle draft-model speculative decoding such as DSpark and DFlash2. We present Adaptive DHiSparse, which supports speculative decoding over hierarchical sparse KV and adapts residency to load. It protects the required working set, retains additional history while GPU memory is spare, and recovers the rest through exact fused retrieval. DSpark and DFlash2 keep their proposal and acceptance rules: queries share missing-row retrieval, draft KV uses a window-bounded ring, and verification staging is reused across layer groups. At 100K context and concurrency 128, GLM-5.3 with DFlash2 delivers 793 output tokens/s per decode GPU, 1.45$\times$ HiSparse and 1.27$\times$ non-speculative adaptive serving. Held to the same latency bounds as HiSparse, it sustains up to 4$\times$ the concurrency and 2.3 to 3.7$\times$ the output, depending on the per-token bound. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at 500K context and concurrency 512, Adaptive DHiSparse with DSpark delivers 1.85$\times$ the output of resident serving with DSpark. In a load step, optional residency reduces host fetches from 14.2% to 1.4% of selected rows at low load and releases memory under pressure.

papers.title: A Privileged Teacher That Only Scores Cannot Search: Critique-Conditioned On-Policy Self-Distillation for Reasoning
papers.summary: On-policy self-distillation promises to replace the sparse outcome signal of verifiable-reward RL with dense token-level credit: a teacher conditioned on the reference solution scores the student's own rollout, and the resulting distributional shift is distilled back into the policy. We investigate whether this scoring signal actually contains corrective credit. Using gold error spans in student rollouts, we test the two signals consumed by self-distillation objectives, the full-distribution KL and the token log-ratio, for two properties: whether they localize errors and whether they push probability away from erroneous student tokens. They exhibit neither of these properties nor can they reliably distinguish correct from incorrect rollouts within the same problem. We argue that this failure is structural: locating an error in a reasoning trace is itself a search problem, while a scoring teacher is never explicitly asked to perform that search. The same model, with the same privileged information, localizes errors substantially better when allowed to generate a critique. This forms the motivation for \emph{critique-conditioned self-distillation}: first generate a critique of the current rollout, then condition the scoring teacher on that critique. The resulting signal localizes errors, is corrective within error spans, and shifts probability toward tokens that initiate backtracking such as ``Wait'', ``But'', and ``Actually''. We further show that the critique is useful both at test time, where resuming a wrong rollout with the critique in context converts math problems the model cannot solve by sampling, and in cold-start GRPO, where it provides an advantage signal on prompts for which verifiable rewards alone provide none.

papers.title: UkrMeme: Multimodal Explainable Persuasion Detection in Ukrainian Memes
papers.summary: Memes play a central role in modern online communication, especially in contexts of political conflict where visual and textual cues combine to convey persuasive messages. We study persuasive technique detection in Ukrainian memes using vision-language models (VLMs). We introduce UkrMeme, a dataset of 200 organically produced Ukrainian wartime memes annotated for persuasion techniques, and PTM-UA, a Ukrainian translation of a subset of the Propaganda 950 benchmark that preserves original visual content while translating meme text. We evaluate VLMs in a zero-shot prompting setup across image, text, and multimodal inputs using hierarchical F1 metrics. Finally, we compare Layer-wise Relevance Propagation (LRP) and model-generated token attributions and analyze the semantic categories of evidence emphasized by each explanation method.

papers.title: Studying Comics at Scale with Artificial Intelligence: The PAGE Framework and Three Studies of American Comics and Japanese Manga
papers.summary: Comics are one of the great visual records of the twentieth century: hundreds of thousands of pages in which a mass readership saw its leaders, its wars and its heroes. Most of this record has never been studied as a whole; comics scholarship proceeds one book at a time. We argue that artificial intelligence, including generative models, can change this to the benefit of the medium itself. We propose PAGE, a framework that makes artificial intelligence an instrument for comics research. It parses every scan into panels, text and a bibliographic record; annotates each page with a vision-language model that follows a written codebook, as a human coder would; grounds samples of these readings in human annotation; and explains change across an archive, with estimates controlled for publisher and genre. We demonstrate the framework on 3,929 American comic books (1938--1956) and 87 volumes of Japanese manga, in three studies, each resting on a different capability. The first pairs text search with visual reading to recover how a mass medium portrayed political power. The second measures the page's visual form across an industry and recovers the hand of individual artists. The third follows who speaks across two comics traditions, checked against human annotation. Beyond research, the same instruments can make archives searchable by what is drawn, open comics to blind and low-vision readers, and help preserve fragile collections and credit uncredited artists. We outline a research agenda in which artificial intelligence strengthens the study, preservation and reach of the medium.

papers.title: X-AgentRed: Red-Teaming Personal Agents in Evolving Multi-Service Ecosystems
papers.summary: Personal agents increasingly connect to services across the web and applications by using tools. As the effects of their actions accumulate and interact across services, unintended or harmful outcomes can arise when agents fulfill benign user requests. Proactively identifying these compositional failures requires systematically exploring diverse cross-service paths. Existing red-teaming methods often simply prompt LLMs to identify potentially harmful paths from task and environment descriptions or decompose harmful objectives specified by humans or LLMs into seemingly benign action combinations. However, generation is biased toward patterns learned during training, potentially favoring familiar tool combinations and leaving novel cross-service interactions underexplored. To address this, we propose X-AgentRed, a self-evolving red-teaming framework that discovers harmful tool call paths through a graph of tool dependencies and expands and refines them using execution feedback. By analyzing each tool's effects, potential harms, and preconditions for execution, the red-teaming agent constructs a directed graph that captures how one tool's effects can satisfy another's execution preconditions. Recipes sampled from this graph are instantiated as realistic scenarios in which agents can produce harmful outcomes. Execution feedback enables self-improvement by diversifying paths that produce harm through tool substitution and refining preconditions at blocked steps in unsuccessful paths to enable further execution. Across four frontier agentic models, X-AgentRed achieves $1.77\times$ the harmful path rate of STAC and explores a more diverse set of tools, yielding $2.99\times$ the tool coverage on average.

papers.title: RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics
papers.summary: As AI agents increasingly rely on external tools, accurate retrieval is essential for reliable behavior. Existing methods optimize semantic relevance but largely ignore tool availability during execution. To address this gap, we propose RATED (Reliability-Aware Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics), a retrieval framework that combines robust semantic matching with dynamic reliability adaptation. RATED employs a frozen dual-encoder with contrastive fine-tuning for semantic matching, and a lightweight contextual bandit module that re-ranks candidates based on real-time execution feedback. This design enables rapid adaptation to runtime tool failures without expensive model retraining. We introduce EcoAgent, a benchmark of 5,172 real-world tools and over 210,000 query-tool pairs for offline retrieval and dynamic reliability evaluation. Experimental results demonstrate that RATED achieves a 52.2% relative MRR improvement over the ToolLLM API retriever on real-world queries, and reduces fault selection rate from 86.2% to 2.9% under severe API outage scenarios with a 30% failure rate, while incurring negligible latency overhead of less than 1 ms over encode-only inference. The code and dataset are available at https://github.com/Elliotes/EcoAgent.

papers.title: Can Language Models Play the Wikipedia Game?
papers.summary: Language models increasingly support or automate information retrieval from document collections too large to index. This task is difficult when it requires specialist linguistic or scientific knowledge. We used the Wikipedia Game to test language models on an analogous information retrieval task. In the game, players must reach a target article using only article links. We compared sentence embedding models and LLMs across five Wikipedia languages and five academic-literature datasets. We construct very large local graphs of Wikipedia pages and of paper citations using OpenAlex and provide code to build and navigate them. This allows the study of language models' navigation capabilities without relying on third-party APIs. We compared the models with human and TF-IDF benchmarks. The Wikipedia Game format enables robust comparisons across techniques, languages, and domains. No model significantly outperformed humans, although the best models (GPT-o3 mini, GPT-4o, QwQ:32B, and DeepSeek-R1:70B) achieved comparable success. Performance and rankings varied across languages and topics, with implications for practitioners utilising these techniques.

papers.title: VortexSynth: Profile-guided benchmark reconstruction for GPU architecture research
papers.summary: GPU architecture research requires representative benchmarks that can execute on new designs. However, many vendor-tailored workloads and library kernels cannot run directly on research architectures because their implementations are closed-source or rely on programming models unsupported by the target architecture. Migrating existing kernels requires manual effort to adapt their implementations and validate their behavior. This creates a need to automate workload migration to target platforms. We present VortexSynth, a framework that uses profile-guided benchmark reconstruction to construct GPU benchmarks from reference workloads. Our workflow selects hot kernels through profiling, synthesizes implementations in the target programming language, verifies output equivalence, and measures profile differences using a translated proxy implementation. The resulting profile signature gap is supplied to an agent for iterative refinement. We evaluate the method on Vortex, an open-ISA GPGPU, using robotics as the application domain. All active kernel pairs pass both output-equivalence checks, and the case studies show that iterative refinement can reduce profile distance.

papers.title: CacheFlex: Direct Software-Managed Access to Higher-Level Cache for Scalable Vector Support
papers.summary: Wider vector/SIMD lanes multiply compute throughput, but cache improvements remain challenging. We identify L1 data cache capacity as the most impactful parameter for performance and efficiency. L1 capacity is constrained by pipeline coupling and latency requirements; private L2 offers an order of magnitude more capacity but is inaccessible from software. This work proposes CacheFlex, an ISA and microarchitecture co-design that enables software-managed, direct access to private L2 SRAM by allowing runtime conversion of parts of L2 into a scratchpad memory (SPM). Through a lightweight ISA extension, software explicitly controls data placement and lifetime within the L2. CacheFlex integrates into an out-of-order pipeline with cross-domain memory consistency and OS context-switch support, with merely 2.02% area overhead relative to the L2 in a post-layout 12 nm implementation. We prototype CacheFlex based on the Armv8-A SVE ISA, model it in gem5, and evaluate it using optimized general matrix multiplication (GEMM) kernels with diverse model-derived shapes, FlashAttention-based fused attention, and full-layer workloads from LLaMA-3.2-1B and BERT-Base in the prefill phase. As the vector length (VL) scales from VL = 4 (512-bit) to VL = 16 (2048-bit), CacheFlex's kernel-level geometric-mean speedup and memory-subsystem energy reduction grow from 1.12x and 26% to 1.44x and 40%, respectively, bridging the widening gap between per-instruction data demand and memory performance. On full transformer layers combining CacheFlex with FlashAttention, the design delivers up to 1.78x speedup and 45% memory-subsystem energy savings (BERT-Base, sequence length T=4096, VL = 16; LLaMA-3.2-1B: 1.64x and 38%). CacheFlex is complementary to hardware prefetching, and its benefit grows as vector width and peak compute throughput increase for compute-intensive AI kernels.

papers.title: TPCS: A Cycle-Level Simulation Paradigm with Native Execution Semantics for RTL Modeling and Generation
papers.summary: The growing diversity of domain-specific architectures and microarchitectural designs demands fast and accurate evaluation methods during early design stages. However, existing approaches suffer from a fundamental trade-off: high-level simulators offer speed but lack fidelity, while RTL-based tools provide accuracy at the cost of significant simulation overhead. This gap limits efficient pre-RTL microarchitecture exploration. Therefore, we propose Transaction-Pruned Cycle Simulation (TPCS), a novel modeling and simulation framework. It serves as a unified intermediate abstraction spanning microarchitecture modeling, cycle-accurate simulation, and synthesizable RTL implementation. TPCS organizes combinational logic as transaction-based function invocations and leverages host CPU control flow to naturally prune inactive logic, eliminating the need for explicit event scheduling or signal tracking. This enables cycle-accurate simulation with significantly improved performance. TPCS preserves structural correspondence with RTL and supports automatic generation of synthesizable designs. TPCS achieves 36$\times$-42$\times$ speedups over parallel Verilator on SMP systems and 3.4$\times$-7.2$\times$ over single-threaded Verilator on accelerators, with cycle-level waveform agreement on the evaluated traces. The generated RTL demonstrates comparable timing and area to handcrafted implementations, with relative changes of -4.7\% to +2.6\% in clock period and -3.3\% to +4.0\% in standard-cell area. By bridging the abstraction gap between high-level modeling and RTL design, TPCS enables a unified and agile pre-RTL workflow, allowing efficient microarchitecture exploration with both high performance and implementation fidelity.

papers.title: Hardware-in-the-Loop Demo of a Cooperative Intersection where Cars don't Stop
papers.summary: The road transportation sector is undergoing a radical transformation, working for a future where all vehicles will be autonomous and connected. A key challenge in this vision concerns intersections, which will no longer rely on traffic lights or traditional right-of-way rules. Instead, algorithms and communication protocols will be employed to optimize traffic flow. In this context, we are developing a testbed where cars equipped with wireless connectivity exchange information with a remote controller and coordinate their maneuvers. As the vehicles navigate through different types of intersections with various routes, they communicate with the controller, adjusting their speed to pass through intersections without stopping. This demo specifically showcases a hardware-in-the-loop (HiL) implementation of such intelligent intersection, using the SUMO traffic simulator to emulate vehicle positions. Real hardware and software components, which are designed for use in vehicles and roadside infrastructure, are employed to enable real-time data exchange of contextual and control information, running the cooperative coordination algorithm.

papers.title: Anechoic: Onsager-Corrected Parallel Annealing for Sub-0.1 ms Dense Max-Cut on an FPGA
papers.summary: Ising machines solve combinatorial optimization problems by annealing a network of spins. On dense problems, the least expensive hardware step updates all spins at once: stochastic cellular automata (SCA) decide every spin in parallel and read couplings only for the spins that flip. Such synchronous updates create an echo: the previous state of each spin returns to it through its neighbors. On K2000, a Max-Cut benchmark on a 2,000-node complete graph, two-thirds of all flips undo the same spin's flip one step earlier. This paper presents Anechoic, an FPGA Ising machine that subtracts this echo from every decision. Dynamical mean-field theory identifies the echo as an Onsager reaction; its one-step strength is the number of spins whose flip probability is strictly between 0 and 1, divided by twice the temperature. The decision logic already flags these spins, so the correction costs one population count per step; a temperature-scaled form needs none. An RTL engine executes a dense 2,000-spin step in 18.1 cycles plus 0.14 per flip, so every saved step and flip saves time. Both forms find better K2000 cuts at every step budget than five published binary-spin algorithms at their papers' settings. Twelve engines at 250 MHz on an AMD Alveo V80 reach a cut of at least 33,000 with 99% probability in 0.05 ms, 5.2 times faster than the fastest published hardware, at 5.4 mJ per solution; with 2-bit couplings, the temperature-scaled form is also faster than uncorrected SCA on 49 of 51 G-set graphs. On an NVIDIA GH200 GPU, the same engine is 2.3 times slower and needs 8.0 times more energy per solution, though its 240 concurrent anneals give 2.3 times the throughput. As a GlobalFoundries 22 nm ASIC at 1.25 GHz, twelve engines would reach the target in about 10 microseconds, 26 times faster than the fastest published hardware. The code is available at https://github.com/skethz/anechoic.

papers.title: A Hybrid and Hierarchical Ray Tracing Method for Efficient 3D Gaussian Rendering
papers.summary: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) is a powerful representation for real-time neural reconstruction and rendering. While existing 3DGS systems rely on rasterization for efficiency, recent work explores ray tracing to enable secondary lighting, highly distorted cameras, and depth-of-field effects. However, compared with rasterization, ray-traced 3DGS introduces three major challenges: (1) the highly non-uniform spatial distribution of massive numbers of Gaussian primitives creates severe load imbalance; (2) neighboring pixels often generate rays with highly similar traversal paths, leading to substantial redundant traversal overhead; and (3) supporting both Gaussian and triangle primitives yields heterogeneous intersection workloads that are not well matched to existing GPU architectures. We present H2-Ray, a hybrid and hierarchical ray tracing architecture for efficient 3D Gaussian rendering. H2-Ray introduces three techniques. Load-Balanced Spatial BVH (LB-SBVH) partitions the scene into uniform grids and uses density-aware representations to convert an imbalanced global workload into balanced local traversal units. Ray-Cluster Path Reuse (RCPR) lets a proxy ray share traversal state with neighboring rays to amortize redundant traversal. The Unified Intersection Engine (UIE) supports mixed Gaussian and triangle intersections through a mode-multiplexed datapath that shares 40% of its floating-point units across both primitive types. Across 8 scenes, H2-Ray achieves a geometric-mean speedup of 3.77x and a maximum speedup of 9.26x over RaySplats on the NVIDIA RTX A5000, combining a cycle-accurate model of the modified RT Core with measured CUDA timings.

papers.title: Mesh-Native Tokenisation: Retrofitting Foundation Models to Unstructured Data
papers.summary: Physics foundation models are an increasingly popular approach for building versatile emulators for spatiotemporal systems. They require tokenisation layers that lift physical field data into a latent representation suitable for dynamic processing. A typical choice for this layer is a convolutional encoder, which lifts field information in a locality-aware way and can be trained very efficiently. However, this choice cannot be applied to a large class of scientific computing problems where data are represented on unstructured meshes, for example simulations on domains with curved boundaries. Such data typically require graph neural network architectures, which are more expensive to train and, in the form currently used, encode information differently from their CNN counterparts, thus limiting the portability of physics emulators between these data regimes. In this work we introduce Mesh-Native Convolution (MNC), a locality-aware tokenisation layer that encodes unstructured mesh-based data in a way that is analogous to CNNs. This approach leads to models that can be trained once on mesh data and then deployed to arbitrary unstructured meshes, even if these are irregular, with minimal retraining. We show that this tokenisation approach can be used to retrofit grid-pretrained foundation models efficiently on unstructured meshes and provide theoretical results to confirm the consistency of this approach with classical CNN encoders. We demonstrate the favourable performance of this retrofitting approach, which in many cases reaches acceptable accuracy even in zero-shot deployment, and outperforms existing baselines after only a few epochs of fine-tuning, thus providing an efficient bridge between the two data regimes.

papers.title: SWE-Duel: Towards a Self-Scaling Arena for Coding Agents
papers.summary: Static coding benchmarks are fixed at release. Over time their tasks leak into training data, and stronger agents eventually saturate them. We argue that a benchmark should instead aim to be self-scaling: its tasks and oracles are created at evaluation time, so no content exists in advance to leak, and its difficulty is set by the participating agents rather than fixed at release. We introduce SWE-Duel, an arena in which two coding agents evaluate each other over mirrored Red-Blue turns. In each turn, the Red agent works on a real repository across three context-isolated sessions. It proposes and implements a new feature with feature tests, then embeds a subtle bug in that feature along with sealed bug-triggering tests. The resulting pull request is admitted only if (1) it passes the feature tests and the repository's existing tests while failing exactly the bug tests, and (2) a fresh session of the same agent can repair the bug blind, which rules out unsolvable tasks. The Blue agent then reviews the pull request without being told a bug exists. It wins only if its revision passes all three test suites, and then the two agents swap roles. We run a tournament among 11 model-harness participants on 15 repositories in five languages for 1,500 turns. The leaders win in different ways. GPT-5.5 with Codex CLI ranks first as the strongest solver, repairing 98.3% of the defects it reviews. Claude Opus 4.8 with mini-swe-agent ranks second as the strongest task author, with a 27.3% Red win rate. Finally, within one model family, tasks written by the newest version defeat a fixed-reference solver far more often than those of older versions (42.9% vs. 4.0%), giving preliminary evidence that task difficulty scales with task authoring capability.

papers.title: Contextual Correction of Parallel Draftsfor Speculative Decoding
papers.summary: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model inference by using a lightweight drafter to propose multiple tokens that are subsequently verified in parallel by the target model. Recent diffusion-based drafters make this paradigm particularly attractive: deep attention-based neural backbones provide strong predictions, while drafting multiple future positions in parallel avoids the sequential cost of autoregressive generation. This parallelism, however, comes at a cost. Tokens within a draft block are predicted without access to the realized identities of preceding draft tokens, removing intra-block dependencies that would naturally be available under autoregressive generation. We introduce DCOCO (DFlash Contextual Corrector), a lightweight mechanism that restores these dependencies while preserving parallel drafting. Rather than committing to each position's top prediction, DCOCO retains multiple candidate tokens and evaluates their contextual compatibility across adjacent draft positions in parallel, enabling contextually informed token selection at low additional cost. Across four verifier backbones and ten benchmarks, DCOCO achieves the highest average throughput in every evaluated configuration, spanning greedy and stochastic decoding with and without extended reasoning, with speedups of up to 6.6x over vanilla decoding. Its advantage persists under concurrent serving: DCOCO outperforms the strongest competing method by 6-23% across 4-32 concurrent requests, while other sequential correctors fall below uncorrected DFlash at these loads. These results demonstrate that recovering intra-block dependencies through parallel contextual scoring delivers consistent acceleration across decoding regimes and serving loads.
papers.title_zh: 面向推测解码的并行草稿的上下文校正
papers.abstract_zh: 推测解码通过使用轻量级草稿器提出多个 token，随后由目标模型并行验证这些 token，从而加速大语言模型推理。最近的基于扩散的草稿器使这一范式尤其具有吸引力：深度基于注意力的神经骨干网络提供强预测，同时并行草拟多个未来位置避免了自回归生成的顺序成本。然而，这种并行性是有代价的。草稿块内的 token 在预测时无法访问前序草稿 token 的已实现身份，从而移除了在自回归生成下本可自然获得的块内依赖关系。我们引入 DCOCO（DFlash Contextual Corrector），一种轻量级机制，它在保持并行草拟的同时恢复这些依赖关系。DCOCO 不承诺每个位置的最高预测，而是保留多个候选 token，并并行评估它们在相邻草稿位置上的上下文兼容性，从而以低额外成本实现上下文感知的 token 选择。在四个验证器骨干网络和十个基准测试上，DCOCO 在每种评估配置中都实现了最高的平均吞吐量，涵盖带和不带扩展推理的贪婪解码与随机解码，相对于原始解码的加速最高可达 6.6 倍。它的优势在并发服务下依然存在：在 4-32 个并发请求中，DCOCO 比最强的竞争方法高出 6-23%，而其他顺序校正器在这些负载下低于未校正的 DFlash。这些结果表明，通过并行上下文评分恢复块内依赖关系，可以在不同解码模式和服务负载下带来一致的加速。

papers.title: CLUE: A Contrastive Learning Framework for Unsupervised Event Type Induction and Annotation
papers.summary: Event ontology is the foundational framework for defining events in a dataset. Event type induction generally involves domain experts who define guidelines for creating event types and their names based on the dataset's domain and scope. However, this process is resource-intensive in terms of annotation costs and is prone to human biases.
