To alleviate the need for manual event ontology creation, we propose the CLUE framework for event type induction, naming, and annotation. Our main contributions in this work are: 1) designing a novel joint embedding representation for expressing both the verb-centric view and the semantic view of events; 2) event type induction using contrastive loss guided clustering; 3) event naming and refinement. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at https://github.com/PratikMaitra/CLUE.

papers.title: One Model to Loop Them All: Elastic Latent Recurrence for Language Models
papers.summary: A latent recurrent language model applies a shared block of layers repeatedly, so one checkpoint can trade inference compute for accuracy by changing the loop count. At one loop, however, such models typically fall well short of a non-recurrent model of the same size, a one-loop tax that makes a separate non-recurrent model the better choice whenever latency matters. We present Elastic Latent Recurrence (ELR), a recipe for training looped language models without this tax. At one loop, an ELR model costs the same to serve as a non-recurrent model of the same size and, trained on the same data, reaches similar accuracy. Each additional loop then buys more accuracy for more inference compute. Three choices make this work: a gated state update with a learned step size, loop counts mixed within each optimizer update, and conditioning each pass on its loop index and budget. The first two preserve one-loop accuracy, and the third lowers loss at every additional loop. Mixed depths can be introduced late in pretraining to limit the added training cost, and with zero-initialized conditioning added at the switch, this late schedule reaches lower loss than mixed-depth training from scratch. In MoE models, reusing first-loop expert routes on later loops cuts mixed-depth update time by 11.7% with no measurable change in accuracy. At inference, keeping only the last loop's attention KV cache holds attention KV memory at its one-loop level while retaining most of the gain from additional loops. On 4B dense and 30B-A3B MoE hybrid models, ELR at one loop is 0.52 points below and 1.04 points above its matched baseline on a ten-task average, and four loops add 7.25 and 4.75 points. Carried through post-training, the recipe yields Koi-4B, a single checkpoint that scores an estimated 18 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at one loop, matching Qwen3.5-4B, and 29 at four loops.

papers.title: Reflective Prompt Optimization of a Deep-Research Agent: A Topic-Disjoint, Multi-Seed Protocol for Measuring Transferable Gains and Prompt-Level Overfitting
papers.summary: Prompt optimization is an attractive alternative to reinforcement learning for adapting language-model agents, since it is cheap and produces human-readable artifacts. On factual tasks, however, it carries a failure mode that scalar-reward reinforcement learning does not. An optimizer that reads the training examples can write their answers into the prompt, so an in-distribution gain may be memorization rather than transferable behaviour. We apply reflective prompt evolution (GEPA) to the two system prompts of a multi-agent deep-research agent and evaluate it under a topic-disjoint split in which no topic is shared across train, validation, and test. Held-out citation reward rises by 0.079, from 0.702 to 0.781, with a bootstrap 95\% confidence interval of [0.051, 0.107], and the gain replicates across three seeds (mean 0.107). Nearly half of the winning prompt is a memorized answer key, yet a controlled ablation shows this content earns no reward even on the exact training questions it encodes. The large validation-minus-held-out gap is therefore small-sample selection under a noisy judge, not memorization. Varying the verifier isolates what makes the gain transfer. Decomposed per-dimension feedback is the causal ingredient, and collapsing it to a single scalar reward makes held-out transfer negative. The gain persists under an out-of-family judge and is largely reproduced by a hand-written version of the discovered recipe. Credible evaluation of prompt optimizers therefore requires held-out topics, multiple seeds, and verifier ablations. We release the candidate prompts, lineage diffs, figures, tables, and analysis.

papers.title: Self-Preservation in Language Models
papers.summary: Continual learning (CL) seeks to adapt pretrained models while preserving prior capabilities. Yet the tasks supplied for preservation cover only part of what a model knows, while forgetting can extend beyond them. Recent work shows that language models can supplement this limited evidence by generating useful replay without access to their original training data. This raises a question about self-preservation: can a model help choose preservation targets that protect its own capabilities more broadly? To study this question, we organize task descriptions and their examples into Task Banks, whose entries can be selected and combined to guide replay generation by a frozen model. Continual instruction tuning with Qwen models of varying sizes yields three findings. First, the new task and learning rate shape which prior capabilities degrade, while tracking previously correct answers reveals losses that average accuracy can conceal. Second, generated replay reduces forgetting on tasks outside the bank. Combining partial banks strengthens this protection, improving mean retention of previously correct answers over either bank alone across the tested sizes. Third, the model can also help choose replay targets: selection informed by the new task improves mean held-out retention over random selection at 4B, with similar new-task gains, although smaller models show no corresponding advantage. Under a fixed example budget, however, replacing new-task examples with replay improves preservation at the cost of smaller new-task gains. Together, these findings show that models can support broader self-preservation by generating replay data and, in some settings, choosing which tasks to replay.

papers.title: GeopoliticalQA: Benchmarking Retrieval and Generation over Intelligence Reports
papers.summary: Geopolitical and strategic intelligence reports constitute a rich source of expert knowledge and have increasing value in the current political climate, but their heterogeneity and analytical complexity pose challenges for retrieval-augmented question answering. We introduce a benchmark for grounded question answering over 415 open-source geopolitical and strategic intelligence reports, comprising 5,525 document-grounded question-answer pairs spanning factual, inferential, comparative, and risk-oriented questions. We propose a document-aware generation pipeline that profiles reports before generating questions and validate dataset quality through expert annotation and an LLM-as-judge protocol. Using the benchmark, we evaluate 15 retrieval systems and six open-weight LLMs for RAG. We find that models perform similarly on document-level retrieval, while at the harder chunk level retrieval quality is not driven by embedding-model scale: bge-m3, a mid-size open encoder matches an order of magnitude larger ones and outperforms commercial embedding APIs. In contrast, answer generation remains challenging even given the gold evidence, particularly for inferential and risk-oriented questions.

papers.title: perturber: A Stateless Service for Semantics-Preserving Text Perturbations
papers.summary: Large language model (LLM) evaluations on clean benchmarks overstate model robustness: real inputs arrive perturbed, and these meaning-preserving variants routinely move model answers. Studying this systematically requires applying perturbations one at a time, reproducibly, and identically wherever they run, yet existing tools couple them to a benchmarking stack rather than packaging them as a reusable transform layer. We present perturber, a stateless service and Python library that applies exactly one semantics-preserving perturbation per call, drawn from a first-party catalog of 68 perturbations across 11 families. It turns on a single primitive, with composition left to the caller chaining calls, so the service and the library produce identical output by construction. We evaluate the tool itself, its correctness, reproducibility, and cost, rather than any model's robustness, measuring meaning-preservation per perturbation rather than assuming it. The demonstration adds a live playground, an introspectable catalog for benchmark selection, and a one-command reproducible evaluation.
papers.title_zh: perturber：一个用于语义保持文本扰动的无状态服务
papers.abstract_zh: 在干净基准上的大语言模型（LLM）评估夸大了模型的鲁棒性：真实输入到达时是受扰动的，而这些保持含义的变体经常改变模型答案。系统地研究这一点需要一次施加一个扰动，可复现地、并且在任何运行的地方都完全相同地施加，然而现有工具将它们与基准测试栈耦合在一起，而不是将它们打包为可复用的变换层。我们提出 perturber，一个无状态服务和 Python 库，每次调用恰好施加一个保持语义的扰动，这些扰动取自一个包含 68 个扰动、跨 11 个家族的第一方目录。它开启一个单一原语，组合留给调用者通过链式调用来完成，因此服务和库在构造上产生相同的输出。我们评估该工具本身，其正确性、可复现性和成本，而不是任何模型的鲁棒性，测量每个扰动的含义保持性，而不是假设它。该演示添加了一个实时游乐场、一个用于基准选择的可内省目录，以及一个单命令的可复现评估。

papers.title: GeoFitBench-LLM: A Benchmark for Assessing Large Language Models' Capabilities in Geospatial Data Requirements Elicitation for Geo-Analytic Tasks
papers.summary: Large language models are becoming central to GeoAI systems, yet their evaluation rarely considers the elicitation of geospatial data requirements. This omission is critical as retrieval oriented geo-analytic tasks cannot be supported reliably without first identifying the necessary datasets and constraints. GeoFitBench-LLM is introduced as a benchmark for assessing whether LLMs can infer the datasets, the supporting resources and the constraints required by geo-analytic requests in natural language. The benchmark is structured around two reasoning dimensions, Spatio-Temporal Relational and Semantic Grounding, reflecting long-standing challenges in geospatial information retrieval and related natural language tasks. Ground truth requirements are encoded in a fixed, provider-independent schema for reproducible evaluation of resource identification and attribute-level specification. Experiments on seven models under minimal prompting indicate that identifying the necessary resources is often achievable, with GPT-5.4 Thinking achieving the best result by recovering the complete set of resources in 66.67% of benchmark requests. Results further indicate that accurate fitness-for-use specification remains more difficult as inferential demands increase.
papers.title_zh: GeoFitBench-LLM：一个用于评估大型语言模型在地理分析任务的地理空间数据需求引出方面能力的基准
papers.abstract_zh: 大型语言模型正日益成为GeoAI系统的核心，然而对其的评估很少考虑地理空间数据需求的引出。这一遗漏至关重要，因为如果不首先识别必要的数据集和约束，面向检索的地理分析任务就无法得到可靠支持。GeoFitBench-LLM被引入作为一个基准，用于评估大型语言模型是否能够推断出自然语言地理分析请求所需的数据集、支持资源和约束。该基准围绕两个推理维度构建，即时序空间关系（Spatio-Temporal Relational）和语义接地（Semantic Grounding），反映了地理空间信息检索及相关自然语言任务中长期存在的挑战。真值需求被编码在一个固定的、与提供者无关的模式中，以实现对资源识别和属性级规范的可复现评估。在最小提示下对七个模型进行的实验表明，识别必要资源通常是可以实现的，其中GPT-5.4 Thinking取得了最佳结果，在66.67%的基准请求中恢复了完整的资源集。结果进一步表明，随着推理需求的增加，准确的适用性（fitness-for-use）规格说明仍然更加困难。

papers.title: Activating the Annotator: Operationalising Lived Experience in Data Annotation
papers.summary: Perspectivist NLP has established that annotator positionality shapes labels for subjective tasks, but the field still lacks methods for operationalising it. Positionality is typically operationalised as a demographic form completed at recruitment: a static attribute recorded once and treated as a covariate, on the assumption that the knowledge it indexes is active when the annotator reads an item. This paper treats that assumption as a design problem and asks whether lived experience can instead be primed by the task itself. We introduce AXLE, a pre-annotation stage in which a scenario vignette anchors a short, axis-guided conversation that is synthesised into a first-person micro-narrative and returned to the annotator before labelling begins. In a 2x2 between-subjects study (104 annotators, 30 items, 1,040 annotations) on ambiguous hate speech spanning immigration, religion and gender, elicitation was associated with higher identity resonance and higher sensitivity to harm. It also increased label entropy and lowered inter-annotator agreement: the stage appears to surface plurality rather than manufacture consensus, which distinguishes it from annotator training, whose success criterion is convergence.

papers.title: Unsupervised Multimodal Reward Modeling
papers.summary: Vision-language reward models are trained on annotated preference pairs, which are expensive to collect, can disagree, and are ranked by benchmark accuracy. We build one with no human preference label: a linear head on an intermediate layer of a frozen Qwen3-VL backbone, trained to score a web caption above a perturbed version of the same caption; labeled data enters only to select the layer. The layer is the decisive choice, worth 5.8 points over the last layer, and one recipe transferred without re-tuning beats or at least matches GPT-4o on three benchmarks at 32B, 6.6 points ahead on VL-RewardBench, from a few thousand parameters at about a thousandth of fine-tuning compute. At an equal pair budget, perturbations teach a frozen head 3 to 5 points more than curated RLAIF-V pairs. Because the backbone is frozen, the objective is convex, and the perturbation sampler specifies the reward, which the benchmark does not identify: two heads trained on disjoint halves of the same perturbations tie on the benchmark and differ by 6.4 points in hallucination judging. Retraining the head on the policy's own verifier-labeled candidates cuts caption hallucination by 5.1 CHAIR points and lifts image-generation pass rate by 5.4, while scoring lower on every reward benchmark. Together, an intermediate-layer probe, free same-image perturbations, and a verifier-driven bootstrap turn give a recipe for multimodal reward modeling that needs no annotator, costs a fraction of fine-tuning, and is specified by the comparisons it is trained on rather than by a benchmark rank.

papers.title: U4RASD at KnowledgeGraphEval-2026: Ontology-Constrained Encoder and LLM Systems for Arabic Relation Extraction
papers.summary: This paper details our submission to KnowledgeGraphEval 2026 Subtask 2 on directed Arabic relation extraction. We explored encoder-based and large language model approaches for predicting one of 40 relations or no_relation from an Arabic sentence and a subject-object pair. Our encoder systems use typed entity markers and separate relation-existence and relation-classification heads, while our LLM systems fine-tune Yehia and Qwen3.5 with QLoRA and ontology-constrained prediction. Our best system, an ensemble of Yehia-RE, Qwen-RE, and TypedPair, achieved a micro-F1 score of 94.06 and ranked 1st in Subtask 2. Yehia-RE (full-vocabulary) achieved 92.98, while the best encoder and Qwen-RE achieved 92.69 and 91.94 respectively. Our results highlight the importance of constrained prediction and complementary modeling approaches for Arabic relation extraction.
papers.title_zh: U4RASD 在 KnowledgeGraphEval-2026：用于阿拉伯语关系抽取的本体约束编码器与 LLM 系统
papers.abstract_zh: 本文详细介绍了我们提交至 KnowledgeGraphEval 2026 子任务 2（定向阿拉伯语关系抽取）的系统。我们探索了基于编码器的方法和大型语言模型方法，用于从阿拉伯语句子和主客体对中预测 40 种关系之一或 no_relation。我们的编码器系统使用类型化实体标记以及独立的关系存在性判断头和关系分类头，而我们的 LLM 系统则使用 QLoRA 和本体约束预测对 Yehia 和 Qwen3.5 进行微调。我们最佳的系统——由 Yehia-RE、Qwen-RE 和 TypedPair 构成的集成系统——取得了 94.06 的 micro-F1 分数，并在子任务 2 中排名第 1。Yehia-RE（全词表）取得了 92.98，而最佳编码器和 Qwen-RE 分别取得了 92.69 和 91.94。我们的结果凸显了约束预测与互补建模方法对于阿拉伯语关系抽取的重要性。

papers.title: MADS: Multi-Agent Dialog Simulation for Robust Conversational Agents
papers.summary: Task-oriented conversational agents remain fragile under realistic conditions, especially when users exhibit non-cooperative behavior. Existing function-calling benchmarks underrepresent adversarial conversation trajectories, thereby limiting the training resources available for developing robust agents. We present MADS (Multi-Agent Dialog Simulation), a synthetic data generation pipeline that produces structured, diverse dialogue trajectories. We inject adversarial conversation, producing validated conversation trajectories that capture realistic, unhappy paths. Using MADS, we construct MADS-Bench: a benchmark spanning six domains, 55 personas, and 1095 conversations, with approximately 66% of conversations containing failure-prone conversation scenarios. We evaluate the robustness of the trained models using a two-stage training approach that combines supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR).

papers.title: DistressBench: Evaluating Multi-Dimensional Crisis Support in Large Language Models
papers.summary: Language models have been adopted faster than evaluation practices that reliably assess their risks, and a growing share of use is affective rather than informational. Within that traffic users disclose suicide and self-harm (SSH) crises. Existing safety benchmarks score models primarily on refusal, but refusal is not the desired behavior here; the conversation requires a substantive supportive response. We introduce DistressBench, 718 English conversations with clinician-authored user turns spanning 23 SSH subcategories, each paired with a task-specific rubric of weighted atomic criteria across seven dimensions of crisis support and a clinician reference response. A model's score is the weighted average over the criteria its reply satisfies, reading directly as the fraction of required care delivered. The best of 25 frontier models satisfies 88.4% of weighted criteria and the median model 71.4%, against 98.7% for clinician references scored on the same criteria. Pooled across all 25 models, in 35.3% of conversations where a model satisfied every criterion for recognizing the crisis, it failed to route the user toward human help. The shortfall concentrates in the dimensions requiring the model to act rather than withhold. Contrasting each dimension's median model against its best separates capability limits from choices: de-escalation reaches 74.6% in the strongest model against a median of 46.0%, and safety disclaimers 84.6% against 8.3%. Multi-turn conversations score below single-turn ones (68.5% against 74.2%). We release the corpus, rubrics, judge calibration labels, and a companion annex of 20 long-horizon red-team transcripts. These results argue for evaluating crisis safety on the care a model delivers rather than on what it declines to say, and for treating de-escalation and resource routing as deployment requirements.
papers.title_zh: DistressBench：评估大语言模型中的多维度危机支持
papers.abstract_zh: 语言模型的采用速度已快于能够可靠评估其风险的评测实践，而且其使用中越来越大的比例是情感性的而非信息性的。在这类流量中，用户会披露自杀与自伤（SSH）危机。现有的安全基准主要依据拒答来给模型打分，但拒答在这里并非期望的行为；此类对话需要的是实质性的支持性回应。我们提出 DistressBench，包含 718 段英文对话，其用户轮次由临床医生撰写，涵盖 23 个 SSH 子类别，每段对话都配有一个任务专属的评分标准，该标准由跨危机支持七个维度的加权原子化准则构成，并配有一份临床医生参考回应。模型的得分是其回复所满足准则的加权平均，可直接解读为所提供必要关怀的比例。在 25 个前沿模型中，表现最好的模型满足了 88.4% 的加权准则，中位数模型为 71.4%，而按同一标准评分的临床医生参考回应为 98.7%。汇总全部 25 个模型来看，在模型满足识别危机的所有准则的对话中，有 35.3% 的对话里模型未能将用户引导至人工帮助。这一不足集中在要求模型采取行动而非有所保留的维度上。将每个维度的中位数模型与其最佳模型进行对比，可将能力上限与选择区分开来：缓和（de-escalation）在最强模型中达到 74.6%，而中位数为 46.0%；安全免责声明为 84.6%，而中位数为 8.3%。多轮对话的得分低于单轮对话（68.5% 对 74.2%）。我们发布该语料库、评分标准、评判校准标签，以及一份包含 20 段长时程红队对话转录的配套附录。这些结果表明，应以模型所提供的关怀而非其拒绝言说的内容来评估危机安全性，并应将缓和与资源引导视为部署要求。

papers.title: People Making Conversation: Evaluating How Naturally Speech Models Converse
papers.summary: A conversational speech model has to decide, at every pause, whether to speak. Existing evaluations test boundary detection, policy adherence, or aggregate statistics, not this decision. We place real-time speech systems at 427 pauses and 482 turn ends from 176 unscripted conversations in Seamless Interaction, give each the conversation so far, and score what it generates against what the person did: whether and how soon it speaks at a pause; its latency, length, and wording at a turn end; and whether it can answer a question about the preceding 30 to 120 seconds. Across six systems, the hosted APIs (GPT Realtime, Gemini 3.1 Flash Live, Grok Voice) respond at almost every pause whichever endpointer they use; only their latency, about 1 to 4 s with silence-based endpointers and about 8 s with semantic turn detection, decides whether the words land inside the pause. The full-duplex models (PersonaPlex, Moshi) are the only systems that regularly stay silent and the only ones that interrupt within a human reaction time. Hosted systems reply longer than the person. Given the history as text, hosted systems recall 41 to 60% of conversation facts under a Claude Opus 5.5 judge and 19 to 26% under a strict word matcher; hearing it as audio, full-duplex models recall 17 to 22% and 12 to 15%. We release the labels, points, harness, and every output.

papers.title: When Charts Deceive Web Agents: A Paired Benchmark for Misleading Visualization-Grounded Tasks
papers.summary: Web agents increasingly browse, interpret, and act on web content on behalf of users. In many realistic workflows, however, the visual evidence they consume is not neutral: charts and dashboards can be misleading, shaping judgments without issuing any explicit malicious instruction. Unlike chart question answering, Web Agents treat charts as intermediate evidence whose misinterpretation can propagate into concrete downstream actions --- a reliability risk that remains underexplored. We introduce MisVisAgentBench, the first paired executable benchmark for evaluating how misleading visualizations affect Web Agent execution. It comprises 280 task instances in matched clean--misleading pairs that differ only in chart evidence. We further provide a diagnostic framework that isolates misleading-induced failures from baseline task difficulty (Zhu et al., 2025) and captures execution-level effects such as extra browsing steps and decision hesitation. Across thirteen vision-language Web Agents, replacing clean charts with misleading counterparts reduces the average task success rate by more than 34 percentage points. Moreover, these failures predominantly follow the targeted misleading action branch, suggesting that deceptive charts systematically redirect rather than randomly disrupt agent decisions. These results reveal that visualization robustness is a critical yet understudied dimension of Web Agent safety and reliability.

papers.title: COFFEQA: Counterfactual-Guided Few-Shot Distillation for LLM Question Answering
papers.summary: Knowledge distillation aims to train a smaller student model to mimic a larger teacher model for resource-constrained environments. However, the process of distillation is typically data-intensive and computationally expensive, particularly for generative tasks. Few-shot distillation offers an alternative by transferring teacher knowledge using limited training samples. However, we observe that few-shot distillation performance is heavily dependent on the choice of these training samples. In fact, we demonstrate that using more uncertain samples near the teacher's decision boundary can significantly deteriorate distillation performance. Motivated by this observation, we propose Counterfactual-guided Few-shot Distillation in Open-book Question Answering (COFFEQA), a novel strategy that aptly uses counterfactuals to provide additional supervision around challenging factual samples. In the generative QA setting, we define a counterfactual as a minimally modified context that induces the teacher to change its response to an alternative answer. We provide geometric insights on how factual-counterfactual pairs can constrain the deviation between the teacher's and student's decision boundaries. We further introduce a new metric, Context Following Difficulty (CFD) that further validates counterfactuals prior to distillation based on agreement with the intended alternative answer and dependence on the modified context. COFFEQA uses CFD-validated factual-counterfactual pairs for few-shot distillation. Experiments across five in-domain and three out-of-domain QA benchmarks using T5 and Qwen2.5 families show that COFFEQA outperforms factual-only distillation baselines under the same few-shot budget. For instance, on TriviaQA, COFFEQA improves over the factual-only baseline by 8.77 average EM points and 9.98 average F1 points under the T5 setting with 32 few-shot pairs.

papers.title: Fear Is Not Always Fear: Variation in Emotion Label Equivalence Across Datasets
papers.summary: Emotion classifiers are routinely applied beyond their training data, on the assumption that same-named labels such as fear or surprise mean the same thing across resources. We test this assumption for five labels shared by GoEmotions, XED, and BRIGHTER, comparing models on identical inputs and under cross-corpus transfer. On the same texts, one fear classifier flags 71% as fearful and another 8%, yet the two largely agree on how the texts rank. Across 30 resource-label comparisons, training-label prevalence explains about half of this kind of scale mismatch, and a fitted intercept removes most of it. What recalibration cannot repair is larger: transferred models lose 55% of native discrimination in aggregate, agreement in ranking between classifiers is only weakly related to that loss, and for surprise the resources disagree about which texts express the emotion. The choice of training resource can therefore change conclusions: on two external tweet collections, BRIGHTER- and XED-trained classifiers give opposite answers about which shows more surprise, even after rank normalization, with intervals excluding zero in both directions. A shared emotion label name does not establish an interchangeable measurement target.

papers.title: Unreliable Narrator Framing as a Cost-effective Mechanism for Satire Explanation of Australian and American Satirical News
papers.summary: Satirical news is a unique form of misinformation: it is intended to be humorous by the original publication source but can be misinterpreted. Explanation of satirical news articles is challenging because recent and local context needs to be incorporated. This is a pilot study that explores explanation generation for satirical news articles from Australia and compares them alongside those from USA. The paper demonstrates that framing explanations on unreliable narrator theory on open-weights models can be a feasible, cost-effective alternative to frontier models. We find that models identify the satirical tropes more accurately on the American source than the Australian one. This work results in a novel dataset and an evaluation benchmark for satirical explanation.

papers.title: Time Delay System for Sequence Modeling
papers.summary: Existing sequence models share a critical limitation: they lack an explicit, interpretable mechanism for content-aware temporal recall. LSTMs compress everything into a single hidden state, thereby losing information about specific past events. Transformers attend to all tokens indiscriminately at quadratic cost, while state-space models like Mamba compress history into a fixed-dimensional state without explicit content-addressable memory. To address this gap, we introduce a novel framework grounded in nonlinear time-delay systems, in which the effective delay is dynamically estimated based on the semantic similarity between current and historical inputs. Our approach features three key innovations: (i) a differentiable semantic lag estimator that computes content-aware soft attention weights over history, producing a weighted historical context and similarity score; (ii) a diagonal state space with closed-form cumulative sum solution, achieving O(1) per-step complexity with no sequential loops; and (iii) an interpretable fuzzy semantic modulation mechanism that learns context-dependent rules for balancing instantaneous processing versus historical recall, where rule centers correspond to prototypical semantic contexts. Experimental results on text classification and generation outperform state-of-the-art methods.

papers.title: Temporal Evidence Forests for Long-Horizon Multi-Party Conversational Memory
papers.summary: Long-term memory has been widely adopted in LLM-based agents to support persistent interaction and personalized assistance. Long-term multi-party interactions, however, accumulate substantially more detailed information, with decisions repeatedly updated and states evolving across participants and interaction stages. Temporal structure is therefore crucial for tracing such memories: relevant information often appears densely within short intervals, while transitions among different states are anchored by a strict temporal order. Existing temporally aware memory frameworks primarily store time as metadata or use temporal signals to guide retrieval over preconstructed memory structures, without using temporal structure to both recover locally concentrated evidence and reconstruct its complete event progression. To address these limitations, we propose T-Mem, a temporal-structure-based memory framework that preserves interactions and organizes query-relevant evidence through two temporal mechanisms. Temporal Evidence Discovery exploits the local concentration of related messages to recover overlooked evidence, while Temporal Memory Structuring models state transitions and supporting relations over time and compresses low-information spans within the resulting forest. Evidence Forest Linearization then serializes the structured evidence for answer generation. Experiments on two long-term multi-party memory benchmarks demonstrate that T-Mem consistently outperforms competitive memory frameworks across LLMs, parameter settings, domains, and query types.

papers.title: Rethinking the Roles of Diffusion and Decoding: Predictive-State Flows for Parallel Language Generation
papers.summary: In continuous diffusion language models (DLMs), latents generated by the diffusion prior are mapped almost deterministically to tokens, either by a decoder or through a token embedding matrix. Unlike in image generation, where visual details can vary continuously, the diffusion prior must capture fine-grained discrete token choices in continuous space, which can make the joint latent distribution difficult to model. We argue that generative roles should instead be divided: the diffusion prior should generate high-level predictive information, while the decoder should resolve the remaining token-level choices. Based on this view, we introduce Predictive-State Flows (PSF), which partitions a sequence into blocks and associates each block with a predictive state computed solely from the preceding context. A rectified-flow prior generates the sequence of predictive states, after which a block-causal decoder generates all blocks in parallel, autoregressively only within each block. This design reduces diffusion from L token-level states to K << L predictive states and reduces token-level sequential depth to L/K. On unconditional OpenWebText generation, a 197M-parameter model with K=8 achieves a generative perplexity of 22.8 at entropy 5.16 using 0.31 TFLOPs per 1024-token document, versus 24.0 and 7.2 TFLOPs for ELF-B with 32 sampling steps. The corresponding measured operating points yield MAUVE@512 of 0.93 and 0.73, respectively. Controlled comparisons further show that content states, which additionally encode their own blocks, yield 8-16% higher generative perplexity than predictive states, and that replacing sampled predictive-state trajectories with a shared mean lowers MAUVE@512 by 0.11. These results suggest that latent design for continuous DLMs should consider not only how compactly text is represented, but also how generative roles are divided between the prior and the decoder.
papers.title_zh: 重新思考扩散与解码的角色：面向并行语言生成的预测状态流
papers.abstract_zh: 在连续扩散语言模型（DLMs）中，由扩散先验生成的潜在变量几乎被确定性地映射为词元，这种映射要么由解码器完成，要么通过词元嵌入矩阵完成。与图像生成中视觉细节可以连续变化不同，扩散先验必须在连续空间中捕捉细粒度的离散词元选择，这会使联合潜在分布难以建模。我们认为，生成角色应当被划分开来：扩散先验应生成高层的预测性信息，而解码器则应解决剩余的词元级选择。基于这一观点，我们提出了预测状态流（PSF），它将序列划分为若干块，并为每个块关联一个仅由前文上下文计算得到的预测状态。一个整流流先验生成预测状态的序列，随后一个块因果解码器并行地生成所有块，仅在每个块内部进行自回归。该设计将扩散从 L 个词元级状态缩减为 K << L 个预测状态，并将词元级的顺序深度缩减为 L/K。在无条件 OpenWebText 生成任务上，一个参数量为 197M、K=8 的模型在熵为 5.16 时取得了 22.8 的生成困惑度，每篇 1024 词元文档仅消耗 0.31 TFLOPs，相比之下，采用 32 个采样步的 ELF-B 则分别为 24.0 和 7.2 TFLOPs。在相应的实测工作点上，二者的 MAUVE@512 分别为 0.93 和 0.73。受控对比进一步表明，内容状态——即额外编码自身所在块的状态——相比预测状态会产生高出 8–16% 的生成困惑度，而将采样得到的预测状态轨迹替换为共享均值会使 MAUVE@512 下降 0.11。这些结果表明，连续 DLMs 的潜在变量设计不仅应考虑文本被表示得多么紧凑，还应考虑生成角色如何在先验与解码器之间进行划分。

papers.title: SEEDS: Preview-Guided Evidence Admission for Search Agents
papers.summary: Search agents extend large reasoning models with multi-round access to external knowledge, yet most existing systems largely conflate retrieving evidence with consuming it. Retrieved documents are commonly incorporated according to fixed or rank-based policies, despite the fact that evidence utility is conditioned on the agent's current reasoning state. Consequently, a lower-ranked candidate may be critical for the current step, while a higher-ranked candidate may provide redundant, irrelevant, or misleading information. We formulate this overlooked problem as evidence admission, which asks, at each search step, which retrieved candidates should be allowed to enter the agent's evolving reasoning context. To enable such selective control, we introduce SEEDS (Selective Evidence Entry During Search), a preview-guided evidence admission framework for search agents. SEEDS first exposes lightweight previews of retrieved candidates and then lets the agent jointly determine which candidates and how many should be fully inspected, conditioned on its current reasoning state. Unlike fixed or adaptive prefix policies, SEEDS can select arbitrary subsets with flexible cardinality, and it can be instantiated directly with an existing reasoning agent or further optimized through learning. Across nine knowledge-intensive QA benchmarks under both local corpus and live web search, SEEDS consistently improves search effectiveness while substantially reducing full-evidence consumption. Experimental analyses show that SEEDS more effectively selects useful candidates beyond the corresponding retrieval prefix. These results establish evidence admission as a complementary dimension of agentic search, separating what information is retrieved from what information is ultimately allowed to shape reasoning.

papers.title: Surfing the Activation Wave: Analyzing the Information and Geometry of LLM Hidden States for Speculative Decoding
papers.summary: Decoder hidden states from different layers of large language models (LLMs) often encode complementary information. However, existing speculative decoding methods typically rely on a small set of target-model layers chosen using fixed, position-based heuristics. Selecting an optimal subset of layers is inherently a combinatorial problem, making exhaustive evaluation infeasible even for moderately deep models. In this work, we present a principled framework for multi-layer hidden-state selection for speculative decoding based on two complementary criteria: informativeness, measured through matrix-entropy analysis, and diversity, quantified using centered kernel alignment (CKA). We investigate layer-wise Shannon entropy, aggregate entropy under hidden-state concatenation, and pairwise CKA dynamics across depth, revealing distinct geometric and informational compartments within decoder representations. Motivated by these findings, we propose entropy and CKA-based layer selection algorithms that favor hidden-state sets that are both highly informative and minimally redundant. As part of this framework, we introduce token-entropy filtering, which removes hidden states associated with low predictive-entropy tokens, thereby improving the quality of layer-selection statistics. In EAGLE3-style speculative decoding, our selected sets outperform fixed baseline choices, including the default $[2, N//2, N-3]$ rule, while providing a clearer explanation of why some defaults can remain competitive. Our results provide a practical recipe for multi-layer hidden-state selection for speculative decoding, insights into the geometry and information in LLM decoder states, and a foundation for extending similar analysis to related applications.
papers.title_zh: 驾驭激活波：分析用于推测解码的 LLM 隐藏状态的信息与几何
papers.abstract_zh: 大型语言模型（LLM）不同层的解码器隐藏状态往往编码互补信息。然而，现有的推测解码方法通常依赖于一小组目标模型层，这些层是通过固定的、基于位置的启发式规则选出的。选择最优的层子集本质上是一个组合问题，即使对中等深度的模型而言，穷举评估也不可行。在本工作中，我们提出了一个用于推测解码的多层隐藏状态选择的原理性框架，其基于两个互补准则：通过矩阵熵分析度量的信息量，以及使用中心核对齐（CKA）量化的多样性。我们研究了逐层的香农熵、隐藏状态拼接下的聚合熵，以及随深度变化的成对 CKA 动态，揭示了解码器表示中不同的几何与信息分区。受这些发现的启发，我们提出了基于熵和 CKA 的层选择算法，其偏好既具有高信息量又具有最小冗余的隐藏状态集合。作为该框架的一部分，我们引入了词元熵过滤，其移除与低预测熵词元相关联的隐藏状态，从而提升层选择统计的质量。在 EAGLE3 风格的推测解码中，我们选出的集合优于固定的基线选择，包括默认的 $[2, N//2, N-3]$ 规则，同时更清晰地解释了为何某些默认设置仍能保持竞争力。我们的结果为推测解码的多层隐藏状态选择提供了实用方案，为 LLM 解码器状态中的几何与信息提供了洞见，并为将类似分析扩展到相关应用奠定了基础。

papers.title: Forecasting Corpus-Sampling Disagreement in Masked Text Reconstruction
papers.summary: If a second text corpus were collected from the same population, how much would a predictor's outputs change? We study this question for masked-text reconstruction using a smoothed predictor built from nearby token-pair counts and evaluated over the full 50,257-token GPT-2 vocabulary. Treating each source document as one observation, we derive a first-order formula for the expected disagreement between predictors fitted to two independent corpora. The formula accounts for variable document length, random context counts, and correlations across token offsets, and it can be evaluated from a separate reference corpus without access to either target corpus. On TinyStories, WikiText-103, and CNN/DailyMail, growing each corpus from 512 to 2,048 chunks of 64 tokens lowers disagreement by only 5--40\%, far short of the 75\% implied by $1/n$ scaling. The forecast tracks this slow decline, which we trace to smoothing of rarely seen contexts. Forecast accuracy depends less on how these correlations are modeled than on the size of the reference corpus: small references systematically underpredict disagreement. A source-split jackknife that uses only reference data reduces this calibration error by 57--59\%. After this correction, a simpler smoothed-multinomial approximation is most accurate when the reference corpus is smaller than the target corpus, and a nonlinear source bootstrap is most accurate when it is larger. Finally, small masked diffusion language models trained on the same corpora show that the count-based forecasts partly identify which inputs are most sensitive to the corpus, but miss the neural models' much faster decline in disagreement.
papers.title_zh: 预测掩码文本重建中的语料采样分歧
papers.abstract_zh: 如果从同一总体中再收集一个文本语料库，预测器的输出会变化多少？我们针对掩码文本重建研究这一问题，使用一个由邻近 token 对计数构建的平滑预测器，并在完整的 50,257-token GPT-2 词表上进行评估。将每个源文档视为一个观测，我们推导出一个一阶公式，用于计算拟合到两个独立语料库的预测器之间的期望分歧。该公式考虑了可变的文档长度、随机上下文计数以及跨 token 偏移的相关性，并且可以在不访问任一目标语料库的情况下，从一个单独的参考语料库中计算得到。在 TinyStories、WikiText-103 和 CNN/DailyMail 上，将每个语料库从 512 个由 64 个 token 组成的块增加到 2,048 个这样的块，仅使分歧降低 5--40%，远低于 $1/n$ 缩放所暗示的 75%。该预测追踪了这种缓慢下降，我们将其归因于对罕见上下文的平滑。预测准确性较少取决于这些相关性如何建模，而更多取决于参考语料库的大小：小的参考语料库会系统性地低估分歧。一种仅使用参考数据的按来源划分的刀切法将这种校准误差降低 57--59%。经过这种校正后，当参考语料库小于目标语料库时，一个更简单的平滑多项近似最准确；而当参考语料库更大时，一个非线性源自助法最准确。最后，在相同语料库上训练的小型掩码扩散语言模型表明，基于计数的预测部分识别出哪些输入对语料库最敏感，但未能捕捉到神经模型快得多的分歧下降。

papers.title: Language Models Have Interpretable Narrative Mechanisms
papers.summary: We investigate whether language models contain internal components that contribute to representing narrativity, the degree to which a text exhibits narrative properties. Across GPT-2-Small, Gemma-2-2B, and Llama-3.1-8B, we identify attention heads, MLP neurons, and sparse autoencoder features whose activations correlate with narrativity. Ablating selected neuron and feature sets increases next-token prediction loss more for high-narrativity than for low-narrativity texts, and reduces the narrativity of open-ended generations. On downstream benchmarks, the largest effects occur in story completion and narrative question answering, although they vary across models and languages; results on confabulation and hallucination benchmarks are mixed. These findings provide causal evidence that selected sets of narrative-associated components contribute to model behaviour, while their internal organisation, relation to narrative theory, and broader functions remain open questions.

papers.title: What Should SFT Learn? Conditional Information Gain for Generalizable Post-Training
papers.summary: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) remains a widely used approach for post-training large language models, because fixed demonstrations can directly introduce desired reasoning strategies and behavioral patterns. Yet forcing a model to imitate externally provided trajectories may also interfere with behaviors already supported by pretraining, limiting generalization beyond the training distribution. Recent dynamic SFT methods mitigate this issue by reweighting token-level supervision according to model-side signals such as predictive probability, prior support, or distributional compatibility. However, model compatibility is not equivalent to learning value: a token that is weakly supported by the current model may either be an undesirable mismatch or precisely the task-specific decision that the demonstration is intended to teach. We propose CIG-SFT, an information-theoretic framework that estimates the task-conditioned information carried by each demonstrated token. Under teacher forcing, we compare the token likelihood from a frozen reference model with and without access to the task input while keeping the gold solution prefix fixed. The resulting conditional information gain quantifies how much the task itself reduces uncertainty about the demonstrated decision. We then convert this information into a KL-regularized projection of the current policy and derive an equivalent scalar-weighted SFT objective whose logit gradient exactly matches that of the projected target. Across mathematical reasoning and code-generation benchmarks, CIG-SFT consistently outperforms standard SFT and recent adaptive fine-tuning baselines, with particularly strong improvements in generalization to challenging evaluation distributions, while requiring neither additional training data nor online rollouts.
papers.title_zh: SFT 应该学到什么？面向可泛化后训练的条件信息增益
papers.abstract_zh: 监督微调（SFT）仍然是大语言模型后训练中广泛使用的方法，因为固定的示范可以直接引入所需的推理策略和行为模式。然而，迫使模型模仿外部提供的轨迹也可能干扰预训练已经支持的行为，从而限制了在训练分布之外的泛化能力。近期的动态 SFT 方法通过依据模型侧信号（如预测概率、先验支持度或分布兼容性）对 token 级监督重新加权来缓解这一问题。然而，模型兼容性并不等同于学习价值：一个当前模型支持较弱的 token 既可能是不良的错配，也可能恰恰是示范所意在教授的任务特定决策。我们提出 CIG-SFT，一个信息论框架，用于估计每个被示范的 token 所携带的任务条件信息。在教师强制下，我们在保持黄金解答前缀固定的同时，比较一个冻结参考模型在有无任务输入情况下的 token 似然。由此得到的条件信息增益量化了任务本身在多大程度上降低了对被示范决策的不确定性。随后，我们将这一信息转换为当前策略的 KL 正则化投影，并推导出一个等价的标量加权 SFT 目标，其 logit 梯度与投影目标的梯度完全一致。在数学推理和代码生成基准上，CIG-SFT 持续优于标准 SFT 和近期的自适应微调基线，在向具有挑战性的评估分布泛化方面提升尤为显著，同时既不需要额外的训练数据，也不需要在线 rollout。

papers.title: Evaluating LLM Creativity through Long-Tail Performance
papers.summary: Creativity benchmarks for large language models (LLMs) vary widely in task and metric design. This raises the question of whether they capture a common notion of creativity. We propose that this shared target can be formalized as task-specific performance in the long tail of a reference input-output distribution, which describes how common input-output pairs are relative to a chosen source of text. We ground this proposition in the novelty-quality product formulation and evaluate it empirically across 15 benchmarks and 26 open-weight models, using n-gram absence from the pretraining data as a novelty proxy. Our results show that creativity benchmarks lie further in the tail regions than standard benchmarks. Moreover, on both creativity and standard benchmarks, model rankings from higher-tail subsets of each benchmark align more closely with human creativity judgments in LM-Arena. Building on these findings, we introduce q@Tail($α$), a lower-cost creativity diagnostic that measures mean task quality on the tail fraction of an existing benchmark. Applying it to creativity-promoting methods reveals substantial room to improve LLM creativity through stronger tail performance.
papers.title_zh: 通过长尾性能评估 LLM 创造力
papers.abstract_zh: 针对大型语言模型（LLM）的创造力基准在任务与指标设计上差异很大。这引出了一个问题：它们是否刻画了一种共同的创造力概念。我们提出，这一共同目标可以被形式化为参考输入-输出分布长尾中的任务特定性能，该分布描述了输入-输出对相对于所选文本来源的常见程度。我们将这一命题建立在新颖性-质量乘积表述之上，并在 15 个基准和 26 个开放权重模型上对其进行实证评估，使用预训练数据中 n-gram 的缺失作为新颖性的代理指标。我们的结果表明，创造力基准比标准基准位于更靠后的尾部区域。此外，在创造力基准和标准基准上，来自每个基准更高尾部子集的模型排名都与 LM-Arena 中的人类创造力判断更一致。基于这些发现，我们引入了 q@Tail($α$)，一种成本更低的创造力诊断方法，它测量现有基准尾部比例上的平均任务质量。将其应用于促进创造力的方法揭示出，通过更强的尾部性能来提升 LLM 创造力仍有很大空间。

papers.title: Evo$^2$: Evolving the Evolver through Weight-Harness Co-Evolution
papers.summary: Self-evolving agents are increasingly used to improve language model systems without human intervention through either weight updates or harness improvements. Existing approaches typically pursue these directions separately: some methods update model weights using self-generated experience, while others rewrite the harness that defines how an agent uses prompts, tools, context, and execution feedback. However, these approaches overlook the relationship between model weights and the agent harness. To connect these processes and ensure effective and smooth agent self-evolving, we propose Evo$^2$, a framework for weight-harness co-evolution. For harness updates, we design a unified dual-role pipeline that a single policy serves as both a Proposer, which writes harness edits, and a Reflector, which diagnoses their effects and guides revision. For weight updates, harness modifications and their execution outcomes guide the training of both the Proposer and the Reflector. We further develop EvoTIDE, a training pipeline that recovers usable trajectories through edit extraction and prefix continuation, then combines SFT with interleaved GRPO across the two roles. Extensive experiments across three coding benchmarks demonstrate that Evo$^2$ significantly outperforms existing self-evolution methods. It achieves 82.1% on Polyglot and 48.3% on SWE-bench Verified, compared with 62.6% and 41.0% for the strongest baseline, respectively. We also show that the evolved harnesses transfer to different tasks without further evolution and rank first in cross-benchmark evaluations. Our dual-role harness improvement framework is also able to extend to self-evolution with proprietary models, improving a GPT-5-mini agent's performance from 24.4% to 48.3%. These results demonstrate the applicability of the framework Evo$^2$ across domains and its broad transferability across models and tasks.

papers.title: RAMP: Recurrent Adaptive Mixed Precision for Efficient Prefill in Recurrent-Depth Language Models
papers.summary: Recurrent-depth language models improve inference-time reasoning by repeatedly applying a shared network to refine internal representations, but the additional recurrent computation also increases inference cost. This overhead is particularly pronounced during long-context prefill, where the full input sequence is repeatedly processed across recurrent depth. Weight-and-activation quantization offers a natural way to accelerate this computation through lower-precision arithmetic, yet repeatedly applying quantized computation introduces numerical perturbations that accumulate along the recurrent trajectory. We systematically analyze how such errors propagate across recurrent depth and show that quantization errors introduced earlier are attenuated by more subsequent recurrent steps and therefore have a smaller effect on the final representation. Matched-budget experiments strongly support this prediction, showing that placing quantized computation earlier in recurrent depth consistently yields the best fidelity. Based on this insight, we introduce RAMP (Recurrent Adaptive Mixed Precision), which performs early recurrent refinement using low-precision weight-and-activation computation and restores high precision for terminal refinement. Across context lengths up to 4K, RAMP preserves near-full-precision prefill quality while achieving up to 1.16x end-to-end first-prefill speedup on an NVIDIA H100, corresponding to a 13.9% latency reduction.

papers.title: CoBe: A Benchmark For Conversational Counterfactual Text Editing
papers.summary: Counterfactual text editing is the ability to revise a given text in light of a hypothetical change while preserving facts not causally affected by that change. When asked what would have happened if a doctor had not recommended surgery, the model output should retain the patient's medical history and modify only the consequences of the decision. This requires causal understanding: a model must determine, without being explicitly instructed to, what events are affected by the hypothetical change and what should remain fixed. This skill is central to human reasoning, especially in safety-critical domains like healthcare or law. By contrast, the task of associational text generation merely generates text statistically associated with the altered condition. In the medical example, an associational response might make the patient's symptoms less severe because milder cases correlate with no surgery. Such responses produce a plausible scenario, but not the counterfactual version of the given one. Prior counterfactual-text datasets do not clearly separate these modes of reasoning. We introduce the Counterfactual Benchmark (CoBe), a testbed for models' zero-shot ability to counterfactually edit a given textual scenario when prompted to do so in a conversationally natural way. CoBe contains 2000 questions spanning healthcare, science and engineering, business, and everyday scenarios. We test a suite of frontier and smaller models, with frontier systems achieving an average score of $58.05\%$. Our findings indicate that models frequently default to associational generation rather than preserving the causal structure of the original scenario. Moreover, performance does not scale consistently with either model size or output token length, suggesting that the failure may reflect model training objectives rather than insufficient model capacity.

papers.title: CliQ-RRG: Clinical-Knowledge Guided Disease-aware Visual-Textual Alignment for QA-Style Radiology Report Generation
papers.summary: Radiology reports are essential for diagnostic reasoning and patient care, yet their manual preparation is time-consuming and cognitively demanding. Automatic radiology report generation (RRG) offers a scalable alternative, but existing models often produce lengthy, unstructured narratives that overlook diagnostic cues and multi-view information. We present Clinical-Knowledge Guided Disease-aware Visual-Textual Alignment for QA-Style Radiology Report Generation (CliQ-RRG), a unified two-stage framework for interpretable and clinically grounded reporting. In Stage 1, CliQ-RRG employs a Disease-aware Visual-Textual Alignment module that aligns image and text representations using predicted disease embeddings, reinforced by a Prior-Guided Attention Module (PrAM) to capture multi-view dependencies across current and prior scans. In Stage 2, GraphRAG-guided retrieval augments intermediate textual representations with graph-grounded clinical evidence, and a large language model restructures them into concise, interpretable question-answer (QA) pairs with diagnostic summaries. Experiments on two public chest X-ray benchmarks demonstrate that CliQ-RRG consistently outperforms prior methods across both lexical and clinical metrics, generating accurate and clinically coherent QA-style radiology reports. Code is available at: https://github.com/chandravardhan-singh-raghaw/CliQ-RRG.
papers.title_zh: CliQ-RRG：临床知识引导的疾病感知视觉-文本对齐用于问答式放射学报告生成
papers.abstract_zh: 放射学报告对于诊断推理和患者护理至关重要，但其人工准备既耗时又对认知要求很高。自动放射学报告生成（RRG）提供了一种可扩展的替代方案，但现有模型往往生成冗长、无结构的叙述，忽略了诊断线索和多视图信息。我们提出面向问答式放射学报告生成的临床知识引导疾病感知视觉-文本对齐（CliQ-RRG），这是一个用于可解释且具有临床依据的报告生成的统一两阶段框架。在第一阶段，CliQ-RRG采用疾病感知视觉-文本对齐模块，该模块使用预测的疾病嵌入来对齐图像和文本表示，并由先验引导注意力模块（PrAM）增强，以捕获当前扫描和先前扫描之间的多视图依赖关系。在第二阶段，GraphRAG引导的检索用基于图的临床证据增强中间文本表示，而大语言模型将其重构为简洁、可解释的问答（QA）对，并附带诊断摘要。在两个公开胸部X射线基准上的实验表明，CliQ-RRG在词汇指标和临床指标上均持续优于先前方法，能够生成准确且临床连贯的问答式放射学报告。代码可在以下网址获取：https://github.com/chandravardhan-singh-raghaw/CliQ-RRG。

papers.title: KV-Repurpose: A Testbed for Evaluating Non-Prefix KV-Cache Reuse
papers.summary: KV-cache reuse in large language model serving is commonly limited to exact prompt prefixes, preventing reuse when the same retrieved document appears after different system prompts, conversation histories, or dynamic metadata. We present KV-Repurpose, an open-source, vLLM-based system for developing and evaluating segment-wise KV-cache reuse beyond exact prefixes. The system combines cache-aware segment scheduling, prompt construction, capacity management, workload generation, and runtime monitoring. Experiments on long-context benchmarks show that naive segment reuse largely preserves output quality for single-document question answering and summarization, while exposing clear limitations in cross-document reasoning. Under a Zipfian RAG-style workload in which 20% of requests share a fixed prefix, KV-Repurpose achieves a substantially higher token-level cache hit rate than prefix caching at the same 30 GB cache capacity, 63.9% versus 3.3%, resulting in lower TTFT. Even with 1 TB of cache capacity, prefix caching reaches only a 17.9% hit rate in this workload. Source code is available under the Apache-2.0 license at https://github.com/taiga333/eval-kv-repurpose.
papers.title_zh: KV-Repurpose：评估非前缀 KV 缓存复用的测试平台
papers.abstract_zh: 在大语言模型服务中，KV 缓存复用通常仅限于精确的提示前缀，当同一检索文档出现在不同的系统提示、对话历史或动态元数据之后时，就无法进行复用。我们提出 KV-Repurpose，一个基于 vLLM 的开源系统，用于开发和评估超越精确前缀的分段式 KV 缓存复用。该系统结合了缓存感知的段调度、提示构建、容量管理、工作负载生成和运行时监控。在长上下文基准上的实验表明，朴素分段复用大体上能保持单文档问答和摘要的输出质量，同时暴露出在跨文档推理中的明显局限。在一种 Zipfian RAG 风格工作负载下，其中 20% 的请求共享一个固定前缀，KV-Repurpose 在相同的 30 GB 缓存容量下实现了显著高于前缀缓存的 token 级缓存命中率，63.9% 对 3.3%，从而降低了 TTFT。即使缓存容量达到 1 TB，前缀缓存在该工作负载中也只能达到 17.9% 的命中率。源代码在 Apache-2.0 许可下可在 https://github.com/taiga333/eval-kv-repurpose 获取。

papers.title: From 2.1M Hours of Raw Broadcast Audio to Finnish Speech SSL: Confidence Filtering and Architectural Analysis at Scale
papers.summary: Broadcast archives offer scale and diversity for self-supervised learning (SSL) but contain substantial noisy, non-speech, and multilingual content. Prior work typically relies on voice activity detection or language identification (LID) to extract speech, ensuring presence rather than quality. Whether and how to filter unlabeled speech by quality for SSL, particularly from noisy broadcasts, remains underexplored. We present a large-scale Finnish SSL study starting from 2.1M hours of unconstrained broadcast audio. We propose automatic speech recognition (ASR) confidence as a proxy for pretraining data quality and show 3-7% relative WER improvements over LID-based filtering despite a smaller training set. We further address the lack of controlled architectural comparisons in speech SSL by evaluating Transformer, Macaron-Net, Conformer, and E-Branchformer at matched parameter budgets. Our models improve upon prior Finnish SSL baselines, particularly at Base scale and out-of-domain.

papers.title: BenCoDiC: A Large-Scale Contextual Cyberbullying Corpus for Bengali Political News Discourse FULL VERSION
papers.summary: Cyberbullying is a growing concern in online communities, yet existing Bengali corpora remain limited in contextual information, annotation transparency, scale, accessibility, and support for multidimensional analysis, thereby hindering robust detection and comprehensive study of harasser behaviors and networks. To address these gaps, we introduce the Bengali Contextual and Diverse Cyberbullying (\textit{BenCoDiC}) corpus, a publicly available contextual cyberbullying resource for Bengali political news discourse comprising 50,250 textual instances collected from 100 YouTube videos and their associated discussions. The corpus preserves caption--comment--reply relationships and is organized through a nine-dimensional star schema covering users, videos, textual content, context, time, engagement, political parties, target identities, and language categories. Five AI chatbots were initially evaluated for annotation but did not meet the predefined reliability criterion. Consequently, a two-tier human annotation process with expert verification was adopted, achieving Fleiss' $κ=0.86$ and Krippendorff's $α=0.86$. Statistical analyses characterize the corpus, while transformer-based experiments show that incorporating conversational context yields modest but consistent improvements over isolated-text classification. \textit{BenCoDiC} supports context-aware cyberbullying detection and perpetrator-oriented behavioral and network analysis. The corpus is available at https://github.com/bencodic/BenCoDiC-Corpus.

papers.title: Neurograf v1: An End-to-End Romanian-First Language Model Family
papers.summary: We present Neurograf v1, an experimental end-to-end Romanian-first language-model pipeline developed to investigate the feasibility of training language models from scratch for a lower-resource European language. The pipeline comprises RoSfera, a 635 GB Romanian corpus containing 175.7 million documents; an 80k byte-level BPE tokenizer; five decoder-only models ranging from 160M to 6B parameters, trained on 131 billion tokens; three instruction-tuned assistants; and two contrastively trained embedding models. Training and evaluation were conducted using computing infrastructure at ELI-NP/IFIN-HH. The model family exhibits consistent scaling of validation loss and increasing Romanian factual and cultural knowledge with model size. On the 1,000-question WWTBM benchmark, Neurograf-6B achieves 69.89% accuracy on Romanian-context questions, while Neurograf-3.2B reaches 67.38%. Compute-optimal analysis yields a parameter-scaling exponent of approximately 0.423. Neurograf v1 serves as an experimental demonstrator rather than a production system. The study identifies practical challenges involving diacritic preservation, corpus quality, data composition, and tokenization efficiency, while demonstrating the feasibility of developing Romanian-first base models, instruction-following assistants, and semantic embedding models within a unified training pipeline.

papers.title: SOAR: Source-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Precise Credit Assignment for Search Agents
papers.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) for search agents often suffers from evidence fabrication, a failure mode where agents bypass external information ($E_{ext}$) and fabricate an incorrect answer. We argue that this fabrication arises from an over-reliance on unreliable internal knowledge ($E_{int}$) as shortcuts due to the inherent opacity of reasoning trajectories. To address this, we propose SOAR (SOurce-Aware Reinforcement learning), a paradigm that transforms monolithic reasoning into source-explicit trajectories. SOAR (i) disentangles $E_{ext}$ and $E_{int}$ into parallel, observable streams via a Source-Aware Workflow, and (ii) incorporates Source-Consistent Reward to guide the policy evolution. By making information-source attribution explicit, SOAR enables precise credit assignment between different knowledge streams. Evaluations show that SOAR outperforms baselines on 3B and 7B backbones by 7.3% and 5.4%, while reducing evidence fabrication by 74.8%. These confirm that SOAR significantly improves performance on knowledge-intensive benchmarks while effectively mitigating evidence fabrication, fostering more faithful and grounded reasoning with enhanced robustness.

papers.title: Scaling Agentic Data for Long-Horizon Terminal Intelligence
papers.summary: Terminal agents are moving beyond local operations toward completing real-world professional tasks. Short trajectories can demonstrate commands and tool calls, but they do not fully show how agents accumulate evidence through exploration, use it to inform judgments, continually adjust strategies based on feedback, and turn intermediate results into final deliverables. High-quality long-horizon trajectories capture these agentic behavioral patterns and their connections within a single problem-solving process, providing richer experience for sustained autonomous work. However, environment synthesis may complete or simplify the key work underlying these patterns in advance and thus remove the need for exploration, implementation, and verification that the agent was meant to perform. To address this, we introduce TerminalHorizon, a fully automated data synthesis engine for long-horizon terminal agents. Starting from real-world professional work, it uses independent execution to identify key work omitted during construction and uses the resulting evidence to guide environment reconstruction. To extend these patterns across stages, it progressively expands tasks under the same goal, introducing new requirements that build on prior results and call for further exploration and improvement. Using this engine, we construct 1.5K task environments and perform supervised fine-tuning of Qwen3.5-27B on the resulting dataset to obtain TerminalHorizon-27B. We achieve substantial performance gains on all 12 benchmarks spanning coding-agent tasks, agentic tasks in real-world production settings, and general reasoning. Multiple RSI case studies, each with a 12-hour research budget, further demonstrate the model's ability to continue experimenting beyond an initial solution, improve its methods based on feedback, and retain effective improvements in its final deliverables.

papers.title: PreSTO: Predictive Subtree Prefetching for Fast LLM Power Sampling
papers.summary: Power sampling improves large language model (LLM) reasoning at test time by sampling from a sharpened version of the base model's distribution. Its sampler, PowerMH, is slow because its Metropolis--Hastings (MH) updates are sequential: each accept/reject decision sets the state from which the next proposal is generated. Prior work reduces this cost by changing the sampler or the model (e.g., sequential Monte Carlo, approximate lookahead, distillation). We propose Predictive SubTree Prefetching (PreSTO), which accelerates PowerMH by prefetching future proposals and provably leaves its MH transition kernel unchanged. PreSTO views future MH outcomes as a tree of accept/reject decisions: in each model call, it generates the proposals of a \textit{prefetched subtree} of this tree in one batch, then follows the realized path with the original MH acceptance rule. We also observe that MH reaches only a sparse, nearly unary part of each prefetched subtree, we further design a \textit{predictive traversal rule} that chooses the subtree to maximize the predicted number of completed transitions. Across seven datasets and five base LLMs, PreSTO achieves median speedups of $1.71\times$, $1.91\times$, and $2.33\times$ on PowerMH and its follow-ups EntropyCut and MultiTryMH, respectively; on the first two, it makes a median of $3.9\times$ fewer model calls, each only $2.1\times$ longer. On LCB V6 with Qwen3.5-9B, the predictive traversal rule is a further $1.25\times$--$1.37\times$ faster than the default breadth-first traversal.
papers.title_zh: PreSTO：用于快速 LLM 幂采样的预测性子树预取
papers.abstract_zh: 幂采样（Power sampling）通过在测试时从基础模型分布的锐化版本中采样，提升了大语言模型（LLM）的推理能力。其采样器 PowerMH 很慢，因为它的 Metropolis--Hastings（MH）更新是顺序进行的：每个接受/拒绝决策都会设定用于生成下一个提议的状态。先前的工作通过改变采样器或模型（例如，序贯蒙特卡洛、近似前瞻、蒸馏）来降低这一成本。我们提出预测性子树预取（Predictive SubTree Prefetching，PreSTO），它通过预取未来提议来加速 PowerMH，并可证明地使其 MH 转移核保持不变。PreSTO 将未来的 MH 结果视为一棵接受/拒绝决策树：在每次模型调用中，它一次性批量生成该树的一个预取子树的提议，然后按照原始 MH 接受规则沿着实际实现的路径前进。我们还观察到，MH 仅到达每个预取子树中稀疏、近乎一元的部分，因此我们进一步设计了一种预测性遍历规则，用于选择子树以最大化预测的已完成转移数量。在七个数据集和五个基础 LLM 上，PreSTO 在 PowerMH 及其后续方法 EntropyCut 和 MultiTryMH 上分别实现了 $1.71\times$、$1.91\times$ 和 $2.33\times$ 的中位加速比；在前两者上，它使模型调用次数的中位数减少 $3.9\times$，每次调用仅变长 $2.1\times$。在 Qwen3.5-9B 的 LCB V6 上，预测性遍历规则比默认的广度优先遍历进一步快 $1.25\times$--$1.37\times$。

papers.title: SharP: Soft and Hard Prompt-Guided Augmentation with LLM for Low Resource Fake News Detection
papers.summary: Fake news detection under low resource conditions is challenged by the scarcity of labeled data and the difficulty of capturing subtle deceptive patterns. In this work, we focus on low resource fake news detection, where only a small labeled set is available for training, while evaluation is performed under a fixed and unchanged test protocol. This setting is motivated by costly, ambiguous fact-checking and emerging topics and domains that are poorly covered by existing benchmarks. Existing data augmentation methods, such as synonym substitution, generative adversarial networks, and large language model (LLM)-based generation, often produce fluent but overly generic content, lacking the task-specific relevance needed for accurate detection. To address this, we propose SharP, a boundary-aware text generation framework guided by soft and hard prompts, which leverages LLMs as tools adapted to produce task-specific synthetic samples. SharP employs a dual prompt mechanism: hard prompts provide structured guidance and factual constraints, while soft prompts introduce learned semantic patterns from the data. These two types of prompts are combined to guide the generation process, enabling the model to produce samples that closely align with the characteristics of news. To further enhance detection performance, we incorporate a boundary-aware strategy that steers generation toward areas where the classifier is less confident, helping to clarify subtle distinctions between real and fake content. In addition, we adopt a dual objective optimization that balances semantic alignment with the source data and classifier feedback. This encourages the generation of samples that are both domain-consistent and helpful for refining decision boundaries, ultimately improving model robustness and generalization in low resource fake news detection.
papers.title_zh: SharP：借助LLM的软提示与硬提示引导增强，用于低资源假新闻检测
papers.abstract_zh: 低资源条件下的假新闻检测受到标注数据稀缺以及难以捕捉细微欺骗模式的挑战。在这项工作中，我们聚焦于低资源假新闻检测，其中仅有一小部分标注集合可用于训练，而评估则在固定且不变的测试协议下进行。这种设定由代价高昂且模糊的事实核查，以及现有基准覆盖不足的新兴主题和领域所驱动。现有数据增强方法，如同义词替换、生成对抗网络以及基于大语言模型（LLM）的生成，往往会产生流畅但过于泛化的内容，缺乏准确检测所需的任务特定相关性。为解决这一问题，我们提出SharP，一个由软提示和硬提示引导的边界感知文本生成框架，它利用LLM作为经适配以生成任务特定合成样本的工具。SharP采用双提示机制：硬提示提供结构化指导与事实约束，而软提示引入从数据中学习到的语义模式。这两类提示被结合起来引导生成过程，使模型能够产生与新闻特征紧密对齐的样本。为了进一步增强检测性能，我们引入一种边界感知策略，将生成引导至分类器置信度较低的区域，从而有助于厘清真实内容与虚假内容之间的细微区别。此外，我们采用双目标优化，在语义与源数据对齐和分类器反馈之间取得平衡。这鼓励生成既与领域一致、又有助于细化决策边界的样本，最终提升模型在低资源假新闻检测中的鲁棒性和泛化能力。

papers.title: How Reliable are AMR Parser Outputs? Uncertainty Estimation for AMR Parsing
papers.summary: Recent advances have significantly improved the performance of Abstract Meaning Representation (AMR) parsers, yet determining when their outputs can be trusted remains largely unexplored. This work presents the first study of uncertainty estimation for AMR parsers in a black-box setting using top-k beam-search candidates. Uncertainty is estimated from pairwise candidate similarities and evaluated using the Prediction Rejection Ratio. This work characterises the relationship between parsing performance and uncertainty, evaluates the reliability of beam candidate distributions, analyses the effect of evaluation metrics on uncertainty assessment, and identifies parsers that provide the strongest balance between performance and reliability. Experimental results show the value of uncertainty estimation as a complementary dimension for evaluating AMR parsers.

papers.title: Do Prompt Optimizers Break Requirements They Are Not Scored On? A Preregistered Study
papers.summary: Prompt optimizers rewrite a prompt to raise one target metric, but prompts also state requirements the metric does not score, such as an output format, citations, or abstention. In a preregistered study, we run GEPA, MIPROv2, and TextGrad on HotpotQA, SQuAD 2.0, and IFEval and count per-item violations of unscored requirements with deterministic checks. By the preregistered criterion, all three optimizers produce regressions, substantially on HotpotQA, where net regression in citation validity reaches 10.7 to 41.6 points while exact match rises by 21 to 34 points. A post-hoc decomposition changes this reading. The optimized prompts elicit reasoning before the required JSON object, and under the 200-token output cap used throughout, 13.9% to 47.0% of responses end before any answer appears. Among parseable outputs, net regression is within 3 points of zero. With a 1,024-token cap, extraction failures disappear, content regression stays below 1 point, and exact match rises further. Two simple gates fail the preregistered criterion. The side effect is narrower than hypothesized: optimized prompts are more accurate and break an explicit output contract, and a lenient target metric does not show the cost.

papers.title: Agreement Without Alignment: Label-Free Rubric Clarification Increases LLM-Judge Consensus but Not Agreement with Humans
papers.summary: LLM judges are increasingly deployed as panels, and disagreement among panel members is often read as a symptom of an unclear rubric. We test a label-free procedure that turns this disagreement into rubric repairs. The procedure decomposes each rubric into sub-criteria, ranks them by cross-judge disagreement on a development split, and has an editor model rewrite only the most contested ones. An additional stage that moves text-checkable sub-criteria to deterministic checkers transferred none in our evaluation. Human labels are never used to select or edit clauses; they are used only to evaluate the outcome. We pre-specified four hypotheses in a version-controlled protocol and evaluated six rubric conditions with a panel of five judges from three providers on SummEval, the HealthBench meta-evaluation, and USR Topical-Chat, for a total of 129,770 judge requests, excluding retries. On SummEval, the procedure raised inter-judge Krippendorff's $α$ by 0.069 (95% CI 0.046 to 0.092) over the original rubric and by 0.074 over a control that applied the same edits to an equal number of randomly chosen clauses that were not selected. Agreement with expert ratings showed no detectable change (Kendall $τ$ difference -0.007, 95% CI -0.037 to 0.021). On HealthBench and USR, neither inter-judge agreement nor human agreement met the preregistered effect criteria. In a preregistered secondary comparison, human agreement after editing the contested clauses was lower than after editing the control clauses on all three datasets in point estimate, although no interval excluded zero. Selecting clauses by disagreement makes judges agree with each other more than editing arbitrary clauses does, but in our setting the added consensus did not bring the judges closer to human annotators. We will release code, frozen rubrics, item identifiers, and judge scores.

papers.title: Host-Aware Web Crawling for LLM Pretraining Data
papers.summary: Web crawling is a major source of large language model (LLM) pretraining data, yet data-selection pipelines discard a large share of crawled pages. We investigate how a crawler should allocate its budget across and within hosts to collect more high-quality pretraining data. Combining document-level quality classifier scores, web-graph centrality metrics, and Common Crawl's per-host crawl coverage, we find that roughly half of the variation in classifier scores occurs between hosts. In the crawls we analyze, a few pages from a host also provide a useful estimate of the quality of its remaining pages. Common Crawl uses harmonic centrality, a graph centrality metric, to guide its crawl allocation. In our simulations, using centrality to choose which hosts to crawl yields limited gains over random ordering and performs worse for some classifiers. For deciding how deeply to crawl each host, sampling a few pages and then fetching more from hosts with higher-scoring samples collects several times more high-quality pages per fetch than uniform depth or centrality-based allocation. Finally, Common Crawl's observed per-host coverage has little correlation with the evaluated quality signals. We estimate that tens of millions of high-quality pages remain among known but uncrawled URLs in each crawl examined, with most concentrated on a small share of hosts.
papers.title_zh: 面向LLM预训练数据的主机感知网页爬取
papers.abstract_zh: 网页爬取是大语言模型（LLM）预训练数据的一个主要来源，然而数据选择流程会丢弃很大一部分已爬取的页面。我们研究爬虫应如何在主机之间以及主机内部署其预算，以收集更多高质量的预训练数据。结合文档级质量分类器分数、网页图中心性指标以及 Common Crawl 的按主机爬取覆盖率，我们发现分类器分数中大约一半的变异发生在主机之间。在我们分析的爬取数据中，来自某个主机的少量页面也能为其剩余页面的质量提供有用的估计。Common Crawl 使用调和中心性——一种图中心性指标——来指导其爬取分配。在我们的模拟中，使用中心性来选择要爬取哪些主机，相较于随机排序仅带来有限收益，并且对某些分类器而言表现更差。对于决定每个主机要爬取多深，先采样少量页面，然后从样本得分更高的主机中抓取更多页面，相比统一深度或基于中心性的分配，每次抓取能收集到多几倍的高质量页面。最后，Common Crawl 观测到的按主机覆盖率与所评估的质量信号几乎没有相关性。我们估计，在每次所考察的爬取中，已知但未爬取的 URL 中仍存在数千万个高质量页面，其中大多数集中在一小部分主机上。

papers.title: Test-Time Memory Construction
papers.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) struggle to answer questions over long interaction histories, where relevant evidence may be scattered across distant sessions. Existing memory systems typically construct and maintain sophisticated memory representations offline, before user queries are observed, incurring substantial overhead and limiting their ability to adapt memory construction to query-specific information needs. In this paper, we propose T$^2$Mem, a Test-Time Memory construction framework that defers memory construction to inference and progressively builds memory along the reasoning process. Specifically, T$^2$Mem extracts lightweight episode-level metadata offline to capture key events and temporal associations as retrieval cues, while retaining links to the original interactions to facilitate the reconstruction of dependencies across episodes. At test time, the LLM adaptively retrieves and organizes metadata and raw interactions, progressively constructing query-specific memory as reasoning unfolds. Experiments on LoCoMo and LongMemEval show the effectiveness of T$^2$Mem by consistently outperforming strong baselines across different backbone LLMs while substantially reducing the overhead of memory construction. Further analysis demonstrates that deferring memory construction to inference enables the memory construction process to dynamically adapt to the information needs of individual queries. All code is available at https://github.com/OpenBMB/T2Mem.
papers.title_zh: 测试时记忆构建
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型（LLMs）难以回答跨越长交互历史的问题，其中相关证据可能分散在相隔遥远的会话中。现有记忆系统通常会在观察到用户查询之前离线构建并维护复杂的记忆表示，这会带来大量开销，并限制其使记忆构建适应查询特定信息需求的能力。在本文中，我们提出 T$^2$Mem，一种测试时记忆构建框架，它将记忆构建推迟到推理时，并沿着推理过程逐步构建记忆。具体而言，T$^2$Mem 离线抽取轻量级的片段级元数据，以将关键事件和时间关联捕获为检索线索，同时保留指向原始交互的链接，以促进跨片段依赖关系的重建。在测试时，LLM 自适应地检索并组织元数据和原始交互，随着推理展开逐步构建查询特定的记忆。在 LoCoMo 和 LongMemEval 上的实验表明，T$^2$Mem 的有效性体现在：它在不同骨干 LLM 上持续优于强基线，同时大幅降低记忆构建的开销。进一步分析表明，将记忆构建推迟到推理时，使记忆构建过程能够动态适应各个查询的信息需求。所有代码可在 https://github.com/OpenBMB/T2Mem 获取。

papers.title: Overcoming Data Imbalances with Expert Selection Biases
papers.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models have become the standard architecture for frontier LLMs. The multiple parallel experts in each transformer block theoretically enable expert specialization according to categories such as domains, languages, or modalities during pretraining. However, when data is imbalanced across categories, minority categories can become concentrated in a small fraction of the expert pool or spread inefficiently across them, effectively limiting their available capacity. In this work, we demonstrate that category-conditioned expert-selection biases can preferentially route tokens from different categories toward specialized expert pools. By applying biases based on input category, we provide a simple way to induce soft category-aligned specialization. This intervention encourages categories toward distinct expert subsets while retaining cross-category sharing when useful. More importantly, it enables the over-allocation of expert capacity to categories that would otherwise be disadvantaged by data scarcity. We observe performance improvements across modalities, low-resource languages, and code in models up to 10.6B parameters. At our smallest and largest model scales, these gains are equivalent to allocating 18.5% and 2.7% additional baseline training tokens, respectively. Overall, our results show that expert biases can serve as a lightweight control for category-level expert allocation, making room for low-resource categories while retaining standard MoE inference.

papers.title: From Structure to Validity: Mechanism-Guided Generation and Refinement of LLM Rubrics
papers.summary: Rubrics have been widely used to evaluate and optimize language models on open-ended tasks. However, existing work primarily focuses on generating better rubrics, with limited understanding of what makes rubric design effective. In this work, we conduct a systematic mechanistic analysis of rubric design across criterion organization, criterion operationalization, and score aggregation. Our analysis shows that structural organization enables more comprehensive criterion construction, semantic specification alone does not ensure effective criterion-level judgments, and sophisticated score aggregation provides limited additional gains. Guided by these findings, we introduce Adaptive Rubric Tree Search with Hybrid refinement (ARTS-Hybrid), which combines adaptive tree construction with semantic-first, response-calibrated refinement. Experiments across benchmarks show that ARTS-Hybrid improves both end-to-end evaluation performance and intrinsic rubric quality. Further experiments suggest that, beyond evaluation, rubrics generated by ARTS-Hybrid provide effective signals for model optimization.

papers.title: MoPrO-SD: Modular Prompt Optimization for Stance Detection
papers.summary: Stance detection remains challenging for large language models (LLMs) due to implicit opinions, sarcasm, and context-dependent expressions of stance. Although automatic prompt optimization offers an alternative to fine-tuning without updating model parameters, existing structured approaches are not specifically designed around stance-label semantics and class-specific ambiguities. We introduce MoPrO-SD, a stance-specific prompt optimization framework that decomposes prompts into functional semantic modules and refines them sequentially using LLM-based feedback. We study three refinement strategies: instruction-only optimization (I), instruction with reasoning (I+R), and instruction with per-example reasoning (I+R+E), using class-conditioned errors for stance-label refinement. We also introduce VaccineStance, a new human-annotated benchmark for vaccine stance detection. Experiments across four datasets and five open-weight LLMs show that MoPrO-SD improves upon the human-written Base prompt in many settings. On SemEval-2016, class-conditioned feedback achieves higher mean Macro-F1 than pooled feedback for four of five backbones. Both reasoning-based strategies, I+R and I+R+E, achieve strong performance, with their relative effectiveness varying across models and datasets, while remaining competitive with recent prompt optimization methods. The MoPrO-SD code and VaccineStance dataset are available on GitHub.
papers.title_zh: MoPrO-SD：面向立场检测的模块化提示优化
papers.abstract_zh: 由于隐含观点、讽刺以及依赖上下文的立场表达，立场检测对大语言模型（LLMs）而言仍然具有挑战性。尽管自动提示优化提供了一种无需更新模型参数即可替代微调的方法，但现有的结构化方法并未围绕立场标签语义和类别特定歧义进行专门设计。我们提出 MoPrO-SD，一个针对立场的提示优化框架，它将提示分解为功能语义模块，并利用基于 LLM 的反馈依次对它们进行细化。我们研究三种细化策略：仅指令优化（I）、带推理的指令（I+R），以及带逐样本推理的指令（I+R+E），并使用类别条件化错误来进行立场标签细化。我们还提出 VaccineStance，一个用于疫苗立场检测的新的人工标注基准。在四个数据集和五个开放权重 LLM 上的实验表明，MoPrO-SD 在许多设置中优于人工编写的 Base 提示。在 SemEval-2016 上，对于五个主干模型中的四个，类别条件化反馈比汇总反馈取得了更高的平均 Macro-F1。两种基于推理的策略 I+R 和 I+R+E 都取得了强劲的性能，其相对有效性因模型和数据集而异，同时与近期的提示优化方法相比仍具有竞争力。MoPrO-SD 代码和 VaccineStance 数据集可在 GitHub 上获取。
